issues.fix_note: A subprocess case now seeds a warn-only database (a warn-severity registered index dropped), asserts the CLI exits 0 without --strict and 1 with it. Measured: rewriting the CLI to pass strict=False now fails that case; before, it left the whole suite green.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Schema verification walks the registry and never the database, so an object dropped from the registry becomes invisible instead of reported. cpersona/checks.py:1132 iterates `_EXPECTED_OBJECTS` and compares each entry against `sqlite_master`; nothing compares the observed index and trigger set back against the registry. The golden test asserts only that this one-way check returns no issues on a fresh database (tests/test_v2437_checkup.py:90-94), so deleting an entry such as `idx_episodes_isolation` (defined at cpersona/checks.py:1017-1022) keeps it green -- the index still exists and is simply no longer looked at. A deployment later missing that index then gets no `schema_object_drift` issue and `--fix` has nothing to restore.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a golden test that compares the fresh database's own index and trigger names against `_EXPECTED_OBJECTS`, failing on any shipped load-bearing object the registry does not list.
issues.fix_note: A golden test now walks the fresh database's own indexes and triggers and fails on any shipped object _EXPECTED_OBJECTS does not list, which is the direction the one-way check could not run in. It found two: idx_memories_agent_channel and idx_episodes_agent_channel both ship from the migration ladder and were unwatched, so a deployment missing either got no drift issue and --fix had nothing to restore; both are now registered at warn, the severity their siblings carry. Detection power measured: deleting idx_episodes_isolation from the registry -- the mutation the finding names as staying green -- now fails tests/test_v2437_checkup.py.

issues.summary: (LOW) Mutation reporting counts a work item that produced no result and then leaves it out of the denominator, and the caller reports success regardless. scripts/mutation-diff.py:239-244 increments `counts["not_executed"]` when a work item has no worker result, while `in_scope` at :281-286 sums only killed, survived, incompetent and worker_error; the main path emits `"status": "ok"` at :497-499 whatever the classification said. Reproduced against the shipped functions: a seeded session holding one work item with no result gives `counts.not_executed = 1`, `in_scope = 0`, `survival_rate = null` and a pending count of 1, so the report's generated count omits the item entirely. The end-to-end half -- a run that exits successfully while leaving an item unexecuted -- was not reproduced, because the mutation runner is absent from this checkout and the execution helper uses `check=True` at :93-100; the accounting defect itself is measured.
issues.fix_sketch: Include `not_executed` in `in_scope` (or refuse to emit `status: ok` while it is non-zero), and add a case over a seeded session with one resultless work item asserting the report is not reported healthy.
issues.fix_note: not_executed is inside the generated count now, and a run holding one no longer reports status ok: it reports incomplete with a reason saying the figures are a lower bound. The counts table is still rendered, because what was wrong is only the word on top of it. It stays out of survival_rate by design -- the rate is over what was classified, the total over what the lane took on. The CI step only echoes the status, so nothing gates differently.

issues.summary: (LOW) `_minmax_norm`'s all-None branch, the one the documented substring-fallback path lands on, never executes in the suite. cpersona/memory_handlers.py:531-533 returns a uniform 1.0 when a channel carries no numeric score, which the docstring at :527 states as the contract for the LIKE fallback so that an exact substring match still casts a full keyword vote; a line-level trace over the full suite records :533 as never run, while its `hi <= lo` twin at :536 does run. The branch is a crash guard and a scoring decision at once and neither half is pinned: delete lines 532-533 and the next line raises `ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence` out of recall, or return 0.0 instead of 1.0 and every exact substring match casts a zero keyword vote and is pushed under the gate. Reaching it needs the rank-sum fusion mode and a query with no term of three or more characters, so the FTS query is empty and the keyword channel comes back from the LIKE fallback with every bm25 None (:2166, :632). Both mutations leave the suite green.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a rank-sum fusion case with a two-character query that forces the LIKE fallback, asserting an exact substring match survives the gate and that the normaliser returns 1.0 for that channel.
issues.fix_note: Two cases: a direct one pinning that an all-None channel normalises to a full 1.0 vote, and a rank-sum recall with a two-character query that forces the LIKE fallback so the branch is reached end to end. Detection power measured: returning 0.0 and deleting the guard outright are both red. The end-to-end case does not pin the 1.0-against-0.0 decision -- a 0.0 vote still clears the adaptive gate on a corpus that small, and tuning a corpus until it did not would pin the gate's arithmetic instead -- which is why the scoring half is pinned directly.

issues.summary: (LOW) The comment above the lost-embedding statements says a test pins the query plan for the unary plus on `agent_id`; for the chunked form no test can bite. Measured with `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on both statements against a 400-row seeded corpus: the range form's plan changes when the plus is removed, from `SEARCH memories USING INDEX idx_memories_lost_embedding (id>? AND id<?)` to `SEARCH memories USING INDEX idx_memories_span (agent_id=?)`, which fails tests/test_bug285_probe_bound.py:227 -- while the chunked form plans as `SEARCH memories USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid=?)` with and without the plus and satisfies both :227 and :274 either way. A reader trusting the comment removes the plus from `_lost_embedding_chunk_sql`, or the planner's costing shifts once statistics exist, and the scattered-selection probe can walk every row of the agent per chunk -- the 3.0 s against 41 ms regression the comment cites -- with no test able to report it.
issues.pattern: bug-417: a test pins that plan for the RANGE form only
issues.fix_sketch: Give the chunked form a plan assertion that fails without the plus (a corpus and statistics where the isolation index looks selective), or narrow the comment to the range form so it stops claiming coverage that does not exist.
issues.fix_note: The comment is narrowed to the form a test actually pins, and records what was measured when trying to pin the other: on 400 rows and again on 20,000 with a skewed agent distribution and ANALYZE run, the chunked form plans identically with and without the unary plus. Adjusting a corpus until the assertion passes would pin the corpus rather than the plan, so the absence of coverage is stated where the next reader will see it.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test in either proxy file looks at a forwarded request's headers, so the bridge's only credential is unasserted. cpersona/proxy_stdio.py:176-177 builds the `Authorization: Bearer` header from `CPERSONA_AUTH_TOKEN`, which the module docstring at line 9 documents as required. Both proxy test files drive `main()` end to end and neither reads a header: the hand-written fake at tests/test_proxy_stdio.py:23 accepts a `headers` argument and discards it, and the seven mock-transport handlers in tests/test_bug253_proxy_concurrency.py all branch on the request body only. Deleting the two lines makes every forwarded message reach an authenticated remote uncredentialed and return 401, which the proxy turns into a per-request error, with both files green; the `Mcp-Session-Id` threading on the next line is unobserved for the same reason.
issues.fix_sketch: Have one mock-transport handler assert the request carries the bearer header built from the configured token, and a second assert the session id is echoed back on the following request.
issues.fix_note: Three cases over the real main and the mock transport: the forwarded request carries the bearer built from the configured token, an unset token sends no header at all rather than an empty credential, and a session id from one response rides on the next request. The last one holds the second request inside its handler until the first response has been processed, since the two are forwarded concurrently and would otherwise assert the scheduler.

issues.summary: (LOW) The mutation report loads the waiver registry and uses it without running the registry's own consistency check. scripts/mutation-diff.py:382-390 calls `active_waivers()` directly; that function accepts approved, unexpired, code-present entries and indexes them by whatever fingerprint they declare (scripts/mutation_waivers.py:210-228), while the check that a declared fingerprint matches the recomputed one exists only in `verify()` at :185-205 and is never called from here. A waiver with valid approval, date, tool version and code hash but a fingerprint belonging to a different live survivor is therefore applied to that survivor at :263-275, understating `survived_unwaived` and overstating the waived count in the report that is read as the result.
issues.fix_sketch: Run the registry verifier before computing active waivers and fail the report on a fingerprint mismatch, with a case seeding an approved waiver whose declared fingerprint belongs to another survivor.
issues.fix_note: The lane runs the registry verifier before computing active waivers and refuses to apply a registry with hard problems, of which a declared fingerprint that does not match the entry own file, definition, operator and line is one. Soft problems (expiry, tool-version drift) stay advisory, which is what they were designed to be. Pinned two ways: the ordering is asserted in the lane source, and a hard problem is measured to stop it before active_waivers is reached.

issues.summary: (LOW) `get_profile` has no test at all. cpersona/admin_handlers.py:68-75 reads the stored profile row and returns it, and docs/tools.md:24 documents the tool as returning the accumulated profile; a search of tests/ finds no reference to `get_profile` or `do_get_profile`. Replacing the return at :75 with an empty profile -- so the common read path answers empty after a successful `update_profile` -- leaves the suite green.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a round-trip case: `update_profile` a known string, then assert `get_profile` returns it for that agent and an empty profile for an agent that has none.
issues.fix_note: Round-trip coverage added in tests/test_2512b2_handlers.py: update_profile then get_profile for the same agent, plus an agent with no profile so an empty answer means absence rather than the read failing open. Measured: replacing the return in do_get_profile with an empty profile now fails 5 cases; before it left the whole suite green.

issues.summary: (LOW) The ownership guards on `update_memory` and `unlock_memory` are untested; only the lock path's guard is driven. cpersona/admin_handlers.py:393 rejects a mismatched owner on update and :500 does the same on unlock; the pattern's third match, :476, is the lock guard, which tests/test_recall_quality.py does cover. The registered contracts at cpersona/server.py:1384-1404 and :1425-1439 state that ownership is enforced when `agent_id` is supplied, and tests/test_recall_quality.py:356-401 covers update success and not-found, unlock success and lock ownership, with no wrong-agent case for either of the other two paths. Removing either guard lets one agent rewrite or unlock another agent's memory with nothing red.
issues.fix_sketch: Add two cases against a memory owned by one agent: `update_memory` with a different `agent_id` returns an error and leaves the content unchanged, and `unlock_memory` with a different `agent_id` is refused and leaves the row locked.
issues.note: The pattern matches three ownership refusals in the file (update, lock, unlock); only the lock one at :476 is exercised today, so the entry stays anchored on the shared refusal string rather than on one line.
issues.fix_note: The wrong-agent cases for update_memory and unlock_memory are driven by the bug-367 regression test, which walks all four by-id write handlers against a foreign unlocked row, a foreign locked row and a missing id, and asserts both rows are unchanged afterwards. Measured by mutation: removing either ownership guard turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The bounded told-session map is asserted by size only, so its eviction order is unverified. cpersona/update_check.py:567-570 evicts the oldest insertion, and tests/test_update_check.py:487-494 checks the length bound and never which key left. Measured by mutation: with a newest-first eviction installed in place of the shipped one, the checked-in test's own body still passes, while both controls behave as expected -- on the shipped code the oldest key is evicted and the newest survives, and under the mutant the newest key is forgotten and receives a duplicate notice on its next call. The order is unspecified in docs/SESSION_IDENTITY_DESIGN.md:291-294, which promises only a bounded map whose worst case is one repeated notice, so the gap is in an unpinned property rather than a broken published contract.
issues.fix_sketch: Extend the bound test to assert which keys survive: after overflowing the cap, the first-inserted key is gone and the most recent one is still suppressed.
issues.fix_note: The bound test now asserts which keys survive rather than only how many: after overflowing the cap the first-inserted keys are gone, the most recent one is still suppressed, and the forgotten one receives its second notice. Size alone could not tell oldest-first eviction from newest-first, and the two differ in who pays the repeat -- a quiet session once, or the session that just arrived, on every call it makes.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The OpenAI-compatible embedding path pairs vectors with input texts by list position and never reads each item's `index`. `_embed_via_api` walks `data` with `enumerate` and appends `item["embedding"]` in arrival order (cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/embedding_client.py:470-475), then `_validate_batch` only checks the count. The API documents `index` as the position of the embedding in the input list and does not promise arrival order. Reproduced through the real client against a mock transport: a two-item response listed with `index` 1 before `index` 0 handed input 0 the vector documented for input 1, with ok=true, so the wrong vector is stored and searched for that text with no signal.
issues.fix_sketch: Read `index` from each item, refuse a response whose indices are not exactly 0..n-1 (missing, duplicated, or out of range), and place each vector by its index rather than its arrival position.
issues.note: The copy of this client that ships inside this package has diverged from the shared library it was vendored from; the defect line exists only in this package's copy, so the fix lands here.
issues.fix_note: Each item's index now places its vector, and a response whose indices are not exactly 0..n-1 -- missing, duplicated, out of range, or not an integer -- is refused rather than paired by arrival order. A backend that omits index was previously accepted and silently trusted to answer in order; it is now a reported failure, because the correspondence the pairing depends on cannot be established from such a response. Regression in tests/test_2512b2_handlers.py covers the out-of-order pairing and four refusals with an in-order answer as the control: restoring the whole pre-fix block turns those six red and leaves the control green.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) A backend vector holding an integer outside float range escapes the client's failure boundary as an unhandled OverflowError. `_validate_vector` converts every element with `float(value)` (cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/embedding_client.py:387), and `embed_with_outcome` catches only `httpx.RequestError`, `httpx.HTTPStatusError`, `ValueError` and `KeyError` (lines 238-240); `float()` raises `OverflowError`, which is an `ArithmeticError`, for an int that does not fit. Reproduced through the real client against a mock transport: a JSON body whose embedding contained a 401-digit integer raised OverflowError out of `embed_with_outcome` instead of returning the documented `EmbedOutcome(attempted=True, ok=False)`, so the caller's store path aborts rather than storing the row without a vector.
issues.fix_sketch: Convert inside a try that maps OverflowError to EmbeddingResponseError (the element is not a usable number, which is the same verdict as a non-finite one), or add OverflowError to the boundary's except tuple.
issues.note: The copy of this client that ships inside this package has diverged from the shared library it was vendored from; the defect line exists only in this package's copy, so the fix lands here.
issues.fix_note: The conversion runs inside a try that maps OverflowError to EmbeddingResponseError -- the same verdict a non-finite element already gets -- so an integer with more digits than float64 holds reaches the caller as the documented EmbedOutcome(attempted=True, ok=False) instead of escaping the failure boundary and aborting the caller's store path. Regression in tests/test_2512b2_handlers.py sends a 401-digit integer through the real client against a mock transport; restoring the unguarded conversion turns it red while the seven index tests stay green.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) A failed embedding request is logged with the raw exception before the sanitised evidence is built, so an endpoint URL carrying credentials in userinfo or a query string reaches the log verbatim. `embed_with_outcome` runs `logger.warning("Embedding request failed: %s", e)` (cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/embedding_client.py:239) and only then calls `_failure_evidence`, which strips the endpoint for the value returned to the caller (lines 416-430). httpx status and transport errors embed the request URL in their message. Reproduced through the real client against a mock transport answering 500 with the API URL configured as `https://user:PASSWORD@host/...?key=SECRET`: the returned `error` was sanitised, the WARNING record contained both the password and the query secret.
issues.fix_sketch: Log the sanitised `_failure_evidence(e)` string (or the exception's class name plus the safe endpoint) instead of the exception itself.
issues.note: The copy of this client that ships inside this package has diverged from the shared library it was vendored from; the defect line exists only in this package's copy, so the fix lands here.
issues.fix_note: The safe evidence is built first and logged, so the sanitiser the returned error already went through now covers the log line too. httpx carries the request URL inside its own message, which is how an endpoint configured with credentials in the userinfo or the query string reached a WARNING record verbatim while the value handed to the caller was clean. Regression in tests/test_2512b2_handlers.py asserts both halves plus a control that the failure is still reported at all, so a log line that simply disappeared would not pass.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The suite shares one database for the whole process (tests/conftest.py pins a single CPERSONA_DB_PATH before any cpersona import), and several tests drift its schema objects as setup -- dropping the dedup UNIQUE indexes, or replacing one with a non-UNIQUE definition of the same name, to exercise check_schema_objects, the migration's non-fatal index creation and the ACL-scoped repair. Their fixtures restore the rows and not the schema, so the drift outlives the test. Measured 2026-09-07: two tests leaked. tests/test_store_recall_surface.py::test_concurrent_unique_index_loser_reports_skipped asserted only that an index of the expected NAME existed, accepted the drifted non-UNIQUE one, and then failed on INSERT OR IGNORE reporting 'stored' -- red under a -k selection, green alone and green in the full suite, naming the victim rather than the test that dropped the UNIQUE. The second leak also left duplicate rows that make the canonical index unbuildable, so nothing downstream could repair it.
issues.fix_note: An autouse teardown runs the production comparison and repair (checks.check_schema_objects with fix=True) against the shared connection after every test and fails the test that left drift. A private copy of the canonical DDL in the test tree was rejected: it would drift away from the schema it is meant to pin, silently and in the direction that reports nothing. Reporting rather than only restoring follows the MGP-filter fixture beside it -- schema drift has a culprit to name, unlike the DB_PATH move, which is what the CLI under test is supposed to do. An object the repair cannot rebuild is reported once and then muted, so one leak fails one test instead of every test after it. The two leaking tests were also fixed at their source, with the schema restored after their rows are deleted rather than before, since the duplicates they seed are what blocks the UNIQUE create; the fixture is what keeps the class closed. The victim's precondition now asserts UNIQUE rather than the index name, so the same drift reaching it again reads as a diagnosis instead of an unexplained do_store result.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) do_store writes a row with a NULL embedding and answers `embedded: false` with nothing logged, although that is also the correct answer under EMBEDDING_MODE=none. cpersona/memory_handlers.py gates the embed on `vector._embedding_client`, which server.main() installs; any caller reaching the handlers without it -- an embedded host, a script, a harness -- stores unembedded rows silently. Reproduced with EMBEDDING_MODE=http and no client: result 'stored', embedded false, zero WARNING or ERROR records. An install whose whole corpus never got a vector is indistinguishable from one deliberately configured not to embed, until someone searches and finds nothing.
issues.fix_note: Warn once per process when local blobs are expected and the client is absent, suppressed under EMBEDDING_MODE=none. Once rather than per row because the condition is a property of the process -- the client is installed at startup, so a store that finds it missing finds it missing every time, and per-row logging would bury the one line that matters under the import that provoked it. No response field was added: the caller already gets `embedded: false`, and what was missing is the reason, which belongs in the log the operator reads at startup rather than in a per-write payload.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) check_health / the checkup CLI report `status: healthy` and exit 0 for a database in which every row is missing its embedding and the configured backend is unreachable. Reproduced: 20 rows, all embeddings NULL, EMBEDDING_MODE=http pointing at a dead port -- status healthy, exit 0, severity_summary {critical 0, warn 0, info 3}. The verdict is derived from severity counts over findings about database contents, and by that definition an all-NULL corpus is internally consistent. The embedding_backend_unreachable / _not_probed findings cannot appear at all on a report-only run, because nothing contacts the backend unless fix=true, so their absence was read as evidence the backend answered.
issues.pattern: pipeline that fills it is working
issues.fix_note: The tool description and the CLI docstring now say what the verdict scores and what its silence does not prove. The `status` VALUE was deliberately left alone: it is a machine field derived from severity counts that callers branch on, so changing what it returns for the same database is a contract break, and the severity of null_embedding was likewise left where it is -- an all-NULL corpus really is a resting state under EMBEDDING_MODE=none, and escalating it would fire on every correctly configured install of that shape. Adding a liveness probe to the report-only path was rejected as a feature: it would make an unattended monitoring run reach the network.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The NULL-embedding finding explains its own unrepairability with the generic hint for `repairable: 0` -- 'every offending row is out of its reach (locked, or a shape it refuses to rewrite)' -- when the actual cause is that no embedding client exists to produce the vectors. cpersona/checks.py _reembeddable collapses three unrelated situations into zero: EMBEDDING_MODE=none, a configuration that stores no local blob, and a client that was never built although the mode asks for one. Reproduced through `python -m cpersona.checkup --json` with EMBEDDING_MODE=http and an unreachable URL: repairable 0, needs_human_review true, and a hint blaming row locking. It sends the operator to inspect the corpus instead of the configuration.
issues.fix_note: Both NULL-embedding checks now set their own hint, naming which of the three situations produced the zero. The de-escalation that used to fill the generic text uses setdefault, so a hint set in the check survives it -- no change to the shared path was needed, and the checks that the generic wording IS true of keep it. The switched-off case gets its own wording rather than the missing-writer one, so an install that is behaving as configured is not described as broken.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) calibrate_threshold reports `embedding_model: text-embedding-3-small` on the http transport, where that name is never used. Measured in the client: the api path posts {"model": ..., "input": ...} to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, while the http path posts {"texts": ...} and the backend chooses its own model -- the configured name never leaves the process. cpersona/config resolves EMBEDDING_MODEL to the api default when unset, so an operator running a local backend was shown an OpenAI model name on the field whose purpose is to say what the numbers were measured under.
issues.fix_note: A reporting helper returns the resolved name only when it was explicitly configured or the transport actually sends it, and empty otherwise -- empty meaning 'not knowable here', since the backend does have a model. Only the two response sites use it. The calibration sidecar and the vector-index fingerprint keep the resolved name on purpose: they compare a stored model against the current one to decide whether stored numbers still describe the corpus, so feeding them the reported value would make every existing http-mode sidecar and index read as stale on upgrade, recalibrating thresholds and rebuilding indexes that are still valid. That asymmetry is pinned by a test rather than left to be tidied up. Probing the backend for its real model name was rejected as a feature.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The registry verifier reported [VERIFIED] for any entry whose pattern was the empty string, without consulting the file it named. `grep -c "" file` matches every line, so match_count came back as the file's line count, the `expected: present` branch saw a positive count, and the entry was recorded as proven while nothing about it had been checked. Same shape as bug-309 and bug-400 — a row that leaves the gate with a verdict it did not earn — reached from a different direction: a registry edit that drops the pattern field, or a registry whose pattern sits under a nested key the extractor does not read. Measured on 2026-09-08 with a crafted single-entry registry carrying pattern "": the run printed [VERIFIED] and exited 0.
issues.pattern: empty pattern: it matches every line
issues.fix_sketch: Refuse an empty pattern where the row is checked, counting it as an error rather than handing it to grep, and add a case feeding the verifier such a row and asserting a non-zero exit.
issues.fix_note: The check refuses an empty pattern before the file is opened rather than after: no file content can make an empty pattern meaningful, so there is nothing the open would tell us. It is counted as an error, which keeps the property bug-012 established — Total equals the sum of the four counters — and makes the run non-zero, so an entry that checks nothing cannot sit in the registry with the gate green. Found by comparing this script against the sibling implementations it was forked from and forked into: each had hardened against a different failure and none had converged, and this particular guard existed in the oldest of them since July 2026.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The registry verifier had no reconciliation between Total and the four counters, so a row that reached no verdict at all was invisible. bug-309, bug-400 and bug-431 each closed one route to that state, but each was found only after it had already hidden an entry, and the check that made the original instance visible -- Total 344 against 149 + 0 + 192 + 0 = 341 -- was never carried into this script. Without it, a row counted in Total and absent from every bucket produces no output and exits 0, which is indistinguishable from a clean run. Measured on 2026-09-08 by dropping one counter increment from a copy of the script: two rows were counted in Total, none in any bucket, and the run exited 0.
issues.fix_sketch: Compare verified + stale + fixed + errors against total after the transport reconciliation, and fail when they disagree.
issues.fix_note: The transport check that already existed proves the rows arrived; this proves they were checked, and the two are not the same question -- a dropped entry is still a row, so it goes missing from the buckets rather than from the input and the transport check passes while it happens. It is fatal on its own rather than adding to `errors`, so it does not depend on the order of the later checks. It reports the arithmetic (which numbers disagreed), since a mismatch names no entry and is otherwise unactionable. The guard is unreachable through the front door now that every known route is closed, so the tests reach it by dropping a counter increment from a copy of the script: asserting only that it stays quiet on healthy runs would pass just as well if it were deleted.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The registry's `$schema` field was read by nothing, so the only pointer from the data to the document describing its shape was unverified. Here it happened to resolve; in a sibling registry the same field held a URL that had rotted into a 404, and in another it named a file that repository does not contain -- both with their gates green, because a pointer no one follows is free to be wrong in the one way that matters. The root `version` field was decoration for the same reason: four registries in this project all declared "1.0" for four incompatible shapes, because nothing compared the number to anything.
issues.pattern: is not a file in this repository
issues.fix_note: The verifier refuses a registry whose `$schema` is absent, is a URL or an absolute path, or does not resolve to a file inside the repository. Repo-relative is the only form it accepts, because a gate that must work offline cannot follow a URL -- and the URL form is exactly the one that rotted elsewhere. The root `version` is removed rather than given a meaning: with one producer and one consumer, both here and versioned together by git, there is no skew for it to describe. Per-entry `version` is untouched, being a fact about the defect rather than about the file. The schema document also stops claiming the sibling scripts are kept in sync with this one -- they are not, and saying so was what let four verifiers diverge in detection power while every registry still said "1.0".

issues.summary: (LOW) The version-selector gate's check that a selector row leads to a page that exists has no test. scripts/check-version-selector.py:211 reports a row whose target is not in the assembled tree, and that is one of the three questions the file's own docstring says are asked separately because each can fail while the other two pass. Making the branch unreachable leaves tests/test_docs_applies_to_banner.py entirely green -- measured alongside three other mutations of the same gate, each of which turned exactly one test red. The failure this branch is the only check for is a selector that renders, names the right line, and links to a tree the assembler never built: every row looks correct and one of them returns a 404.
issues.note: Found while repairing the positive control in the same test file, which had been red since a second version line was declared: the fixture published one line where the gate asks its question per line. That repair made the positive control assert the whole run is clean, so the tree it writes now exercises this branch in the passing direction -- a row pointing at a page that is not there would fail it. What is still missing is the negative: no test writes a tree whose selector points at a line the assembler did not build, so deleting the branch costs nothing. Left open rather than fixed with the repair, to keep a build-restoring change to the failure it restored.
issues.fix_note: A test publishes every declared line, removes one line's landing page while keeping a page below it (so the line is still published and the banner question stays satisfied), and asserts the gate reports the selector row by its href. Making the branch unreachable now turns exactly this test red. The pattern lives in the test file because the fix is the test: the gate's branch was already correct.

issues.summary: (HIGH) Message-ID reconstruction ignores the stored project namespace, merging unrelated records and fabricating supersession when multiple projects are visible. Reproduced with two successful stores of the same ID into sibling projects: two facts became one item.
issues.note: Found in the reconstruction candidate built on the first 2.6 alpha, before release; the published alpha does not include this reconstruction tool.
issues.fix_note: Use a shared project-scoped identity key for bundling, supersession and conflicts; unknown context cannot establish identity. Preserve positive same-namespace version and conflict assertions with explicit stage fixtures, and pin real-store sibling/global separation.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Reconstruction consumes recall advisory and update notices, marking the session as informed, but does not return those fields. A later recall receives only the short degradation reminder or no update notice.
issues.note: Found in the reconstruction candidate built on the first 2.6 alpha, before release; the published alpha does not include this reconstruction tool.
issues.fix_note: Forward the advisory/update allowlist before empty-result returns. Tests exercise real per-session notice suppression for populated and empty responses, including count zero.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Reconstruction compares returned candidates against requested top_k after recall clamps it to the library ceiling. With five records, requested20 and library ceiling2, it returns two with truncated false.
issues.note: Found in the reconstruction candidate built on the first 2.6 alpha, before release; the published alpha does not include this reconstruction tool.
issues.fix_note: Resolve the effective candidate bound before retrieval; retain requested top_k and report effective_top_k when clamped. Mark a clamped bound even for empty or undersized pools, and compare returned rows against the effective bound.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) A multi-row recall item always quoted its newest row. That is correct for versions of one record but not for distinct rows bundled by adjacency or episode span: a relevant statement followed within the adjacency window by an unrelated remark returned the remark as the item's content, and an evidence cut dropped the older relevant rows first.
issues.note: Found in the reconstruction candidate built on the first 2.6 alpha, before release; the published alpha does not include this reconstruction tool. The design named a head claim without defining which row it is.
issues.fix_note: The head is the most relevant row, resolved to the latest version when newer versions of that record are in the item; head_ref names it and claims stay newest first. An evidence cut keeps the head, then the most relevant remaining rows.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) check_sqlite_integrity reported critical FTS5 corruption for an intact index. FTS5 caches each table's segment structure on the connection that last read it and PRAGMA quick_check verifies the index against that cache; on the long-lived shared read connection, a merge or optimize made by the write connection left the cache stale, and quick_check reported 'malformed inverted index' while every other connection read the index as intact.
issues.note: Surfaced as an order-dependent test failure: enough FTS writes in earlier test files moved the index under the read connection's cache. Reproduced before the overflow-tree work, so it was not introduced by it.
issues.fix_note: A quick_check finding is confirmed on a read-only connection opened for it, which has no cached structure. A healthy run pays nothing; a genuine corruption is on disk and the fresh connection reports it too.

issues.summary: (LOW) Over MCP, every store without associations ran an empty declaration and returned an extra `associations` key, and every declare_associations call without retract returned an empty `retracted`. The argument validator hands an omitted object argument over as {} rather than None, and both boundaries tested `is not None`. The library-level tests passed None directly and never saw what a client sends.
issues.note: Found on the production deployment of 2.6.0a4: a plain store answered with associations: {entities: [], mentions: 0, relations: [], dropped: []}. Nothing was written to the graph tables; each store paid one empty write transaction.
issues.fix_note: An empty associations or retract object is treated as absent. Tests call the registered handler, the path an MCP client takes, and fail on the previous code with the extra key in the response.

issues.summary: (LOW) A recall trace named the configured embedding model rather than the one that produced the vectors. Over HTTP the request carries texts and the backend chooses the model, so the configured default never reaches it; the trace wrote that default into config.embedding_model, and on one evaluation every trace said text-embedding-3-small while bge-m3 answered.
issues.note: Trace only: nothing ranked or stored read the field. Found when a stage replay could not tell from its traces which model the results came from.
issues.fix_note: A traced recall asks the backend what it is (bounded by the existing refresh interval; an untraced recall does not ask) and names the model the capability report gives, else the name this process can vouch for (config.reported_embedding_model), else empty -- not known here.

issues.summary: (LOW) CPERSONA_PRIOR_FAR_WEIGHT=0 was not the reach turned off, as PRIOR_FUNCTION_DESIGN.md says it is. The far list was still scanned and fused at a weight of 0; under rrf the gate reads a row's cosine rather than its fused score, so far rows entered at a score of 0 passed it and filled the tail of any answer the near and lexical lists left short of limit. Under rsf the answer was unchanged, but the far region was still scanned on every recall.
issues.note: Reachable only with CPERSONA_VECTOR_REACH set above the window and the weight set to 0; both are off by default. Found while registering the far-weight sweep, whose w=0 arm is an identity control against the reach off: on a corpus where three near rows and no lexical list answered, the reach off returned 3 rows and w=0 returned 10.
issues.fix_note: Both fusions ask the vector retriever for the far list only when the weight is above 0. At 0 no far scan runs, so the answer is the reach-off answer by construction rather than by the gate. tests/test_vector_reach.py pins both the answer and the absence of the scan, and proves the scan counter live at a weight of 1.

issues.summary: (LOW) A time_cue the parser cannot represent escapes as OverflowError or TypeError instead of TimeCueError, so recall and reconstruct (which catch only TimeCueError) raise instead of returning the documented refusal. Reproduced: before '9999-12-31' overflows in parse(); ago {unit: months, value: 100000} and a vague after '0001-01-02' overflow later in period(); ago.unit given as a list raises TypeError (unhashable). The tool schema bounds none of them.
issues.fix_sketch: Catch OverflowError and TypeError in parse() and re-raise as TimeCueError, and bound ago.value and the year range there so period() cannot overflow afterwards.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Reproduced by running it.
issues.fix_note: Two changes, because the escapes had two causes. A malformed unit (a list, say) is refused as TimeCueError: the membership test raised TypeError on an unhashable value, so the check is now isinstance-first. A period that reaches past the representable range is clipped to it rather than refused: _later / _earlier saturate at datetime.max / datetime.min, and so does the ago product when it passes the largest timedelta. Clipping rather than refusing because the reach is not always the caller's: an open end is closed by the scope's oldest stored stamp, and a record stamped in year 1 makes an ordinary vague cue reach past it -- no refusal of the cue could prevent that, and raising turned a recall into an undocumented error. sql_instant now formats with isoformat, because strftime's %Y does not pad a year below 1000 on every platform and a clipped bound at year 1 would compare as text in the wrong order. Regression: tests/test_recall_cue.py -- the finding's four cues through recall and reconstruct, a stored year-1 stamp, a list unit refused through both tools, and the four-digit year. The four-digit-year test is detective only where strftime does not pad a year below 1000 (glibc, where CI runs the suite); on platforms that pad, the old spelling produced the same string, so no mutation-proof entry pins it -- one would survive there and fail a local run.

issues.summary: (LOW) segment() emits a whitespace-only block whenever a sentence end is followed by a line break: the sentence-end rule cuts before the newline and the line-break rule after it. Reproduced: 'Remember this.\n' divides into ['Remember this.', '\n']. A one-sentence record with a trailing newline therefore gets a block build it should not, and every such newline block embeds to nearly the same vector, so they tie in the Hamming pass and compete for reserved places.
issues.fix_sketch: Drop or merge spans that are whitespace only before building the block list.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Reproduced by running it.
issues.fix_note:
segment() folds a block that is only whitespace into the block after it (the last one, having none after it, into the block before), so 'Remember this.
' is one block and 'A.
B.' divides into 'A.' and '
B.'. Forward rather than backward because that is where a sentence end already leaves the whitespace after it ('Hello.' / ' World.'), and it keeps a quoted sentence free of a trailing break -- the backward fold was tried first and changed the quotation test_a_line_break_does_not_join_independent_sentences pins, which is a behaviour this fix has no reason to move. A fold never crosses a node end and is not made when it would pass max_chars; in those two cases the whitespace block stands, because both constraints outrank this one. Block sets already stored keep their division until their record is rebuilt: they are still partitions of the text, and the whitespace block only costs a place in the Hamming pass. Regression: tests/test_blocks_segment.py::test_no_block_is_only_whitespace and the node-bound and limit cases beside it.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) context_range() does not attach a qualifier that starts on the next line, because the whitespace-only block between the two sentences is what the forward qualifier check inspects. Reproduced: 'Enable caching.\nHowever, never in production.' quotes only 'Enable caching.' with complete=True, while the same text joined by a space attaches the qualifier. The unqualified clause is then served as complete evidence, which is the failure the module says the design prevents.
issues.fix_sketch: Skip whitespace-only blocks when looking for the following qualifier (and fix the block that produces them).
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Reproduced by running it.
issues.fix_note: The forward check now reads from the next block through the first block that is not blank, so a qualifier behind a line break is seen as the next thing a reader meets; the extension still proceeds one block at a time and still reports incomplete when the limit cannot hold it. The whitespace block itself comes from the divider (bug-444, left open): removing it would change every record's division and so the stored block sets and read-time ranges, a larger change than this one, which only alters what one direction reads. The backward check was already right because it strips leading whitespace from the combined text. tests/test_blocks_quotation.py covers English and Japanese with one and two line breaks (failing before the fix) and the same text joined without one (passing before and after), plus independent sentences on separate lines that must stay apart.

issues.summary:
(LOW) Fence protection uses a strict a < end < b where b is the start of the closing fence line, so the newline just before the closing ``` is an allowed cut. Reproduced: 'intro
```
code. more

x
```
after' divides into ['intro
', '```
code. more

x
', '```
', 'after'], separating the code block from its closing fence, against the rule that a fenced block is never cut into.
issues.pattern: ranges\.append\(\(marks\[i\], len\(text\) if line_end == -1 else line_end \+ 1\)\)
issues.fix_sketch: Let the protected range end at the end of the closing fence line, or compare with <=.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Reproduced by running it.
issues.fix_note: A fence range now ends after the closing fence's line break (or at the end of the text), not at the start of that line, so the break before the closing ``` is inside the range and the cut after the closing line is the first one allowed. The strict a < end < b test is kept: widening the range is what moves the boundary, and the cut at the range's own end is exactly the one that should survive. Regression: tests/test_blocks_segment.py::test_a_closing_fence_stays_with_its_code (and the end-of-text variant).

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) retract() checks ids with isinstance(x, int), which accepts JSON booleans (validate_int elsewhere rejects bool for this reason). Reproduced: declare_associations(retract={relations: [true]}) deletes relation id 1 and reports nothing dropped; the same applies to mention entity ids. A malformed argument silently destroys declarations.
issues.fix_sketch: Reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)) for relation and entity ids.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Reproduced by running it.
issues.fix_note: Both ids in retract (the relation id and a mention's entity id) go through associations._is_id, which excludes bool the way the shared validate_int does; a boolean is dropped with the same reason as any other non-integer. validate_int itself was not reused because it returns a default instead of saying the value was refused, and retract has to report the item. tests/test_associations_declare.py retracts with true and with false on a store where relation 1 and entity 1 exist; before the fix true deleted both and neither case was reported.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) A project-scoped declaration that names an entity already registered in the global pool reuses that entity, and its aliases are attached to it; entity_aliases carries no scope columns, so the aliases become readable from every project. Reproduced: an alias declared with project_id 'P' on a global entity is returned by traverse(..., project_id='Q'), and query_terms in Q expands on it. This breaks the invariant that isolation follows the call's read semantics.
issues.fix_sketch: Store the declaring scope with each alias and filter aliases by the reader's scope, or register a scoped entity instead of extending the global one.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Reproduced by running it.
issues.fix_note: A declaration that carries aliases now registers, or reuses, an entity of its own scope, and its aliases and mention attach there; the wider entity is not touched. Readers of that scope see both entities, which traverse already treats as starts (a project's and the global pool's). Adding a scope column to entity_aliases was the other option, and was not taken because it is a schema change, outside a beta. A declaration without aliases still reuses the wider entity, since a mention or a relation carries its own scope. Aliases stored before this fix are not changed: entity_aliases records no scope, so an alias a project hung on a global entity cannot be told apart from one declared globally, and neither a report nor a move is possible from the stored data. tests/test_associations_traverse.py declares an alias in P on a name that exists globally and checks that Q and the global pool cannot resolve it, P can, and query_terms follows the same line; before the fix Q resolved it. The control declares an alias in the entity's own scope and checks that no second entity appears.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) anchor_ref is validated with parse_ref (which accepts leading zeros) but the raw string is stored as the mention ref and the relation anchor. Reproduced: anchor_ref 'mem:001' is stored as 'mem:001'. The graph walk looks records up as 'mem:1', and the delete trigger matches 'mem:' || id, so such a mention is never walked and outlives its record; declaring 'mem:1' and 'mem:01' gives two rows.
issues.fix_sketch: Store the canonical f'{kind}:{id}' built from parse_ref's result, here and in retract.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. The stored value was reproduced; the walk and delete consequences come from the review's own run.
issues.fix_note: associations.canonical_ref builds the one spelling the triggers and the walk use ('mem:' || id). declare stores the anchor in that spelling once it has been validated, and retract compares a mention by it, so any spelling of a record names the same row. Normalising at the write, rather than teaching the triggers and the walk to accept leading zeros, keeps one spelling in the table, which is what makes the unique index on mentions collapse 'mem:1' and 'mem:01' into one row. tests/test_associations_declare.py stores through 'mem:001' and 'mem:01', checks one mention and one relation anchored at 'mem:1', deletes the record and checks both are gone, and retracts through 'mem:00<id>'. Rows written before the fix keep the spelling they were given; this change does not rewrite them.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) _resolve_entity searches only the exact (project, channel) and the fully global ('', '') pools, while reads use X-union-global on each axis. An entity declared in (P, '') or ('', C) is invisible to a declaration in (P, C), so the rule that one alias resolves to at most one entity per scope breaks: the same alias can register a second entity, and re-declaring the name creates a duplicate.
issues.pattern: return \[\(p, c\) for p in projects for c in channels\]
issues.fix_sketch: Resolve through the same axis union the readers use, in the same precedence.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: _visible_scopes gives the scopes a reader of the declaring scope sees, most specific first: (P, C), (P, ''), ('', C), ('', ''). Resolution, and the alias conflict check, search them in that order, so a (P, C) declaration reuses the (P, '') entity its reader resolves and an alias that reader already resolves cannot name a second entity. A declaration without a channel does not reuse a single channel's entity, because readers of other channels would not see it. Together with bug-448 an alias still attaches only to an entity of the declaring scope. tests/test_associations_traverse.py checks the reuse and the refused alias (before the fix a second entity was created) and the channel-less direction.

issues.summary: (LOW) declare()'s docstring says an anchor_ref that is not a record of this agent drops every item that needed it, but the code reports the anchor as dropped and then inserts every relation and mention unanchored. Such a relation is not removed with the evidence the caller meant, and a later correct declaration adds a second row because the unique key includes anchor_ref.
issues.pattern: is not a record of this agent
issues.fix_sketch: Either drop the items that needed the anchor, as documented, or change the documented contract.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code. Re-judged 2026-09-30 and left open for a decision rather than for lack of a fix. Three sources disagree: the docstring says every item that needed the anchor is dropped; the tool description says malformed items are reported and skipped and nothing else in the call is refused for them; and tests/test_associations_declare.py::test_an_anchor_that_is_not_this_agents_record_is_dropped_and_nothing_is_anchored pins the unanchored insert. Dropping the relations avoids the duplicate a later, correct declaration creates, but it refuses items the published description says are not refused and rewrites a test written to hold the present behaviour; making the docstring match the code keeps the contract and leaves the duplicate. Either is a contract decision, which a fix release does not take on its own.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The expected-object entry for idx_record_blocks_axes has severity 'warning', but run_health_checks tallies into a dict whose keys are critical / warn / info, outside the per-check try. When that index is missing or has drifted, summary['warning'] raises KeyError, check_health and the checkup CLI fail instead of reporting it, and under fix=True every other repair in the run is rolled back.
issues.fix_sketch: Use 'warn', as every other entry does.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: The entry now says 'warn'. The runner's tally was left strict on purpose: counting an unknown severity under some default would have turned this crash into a finding reported at the wrong level, which no gate reads. The guard went into the tests instead: tests/test_record_blocks_schema.py drives run_health_checks with the index dropped (the check alone never reaches the tally, which is why the existing test passed) and holds every entry of the expected-object table to checks.SEVERITIES, because a wrong severity there fails only when its object is missing or drifted, which no ordinary run exercises. Before the fix the first test failed with KeyError: 'warning' at the tally.

issues.summary: (LOW) The recall_count / last_recalled_at bump credits every returned row, including held seats (time cue, propagation) and block-reserved rows that no quality gate admitted. The comment above it excludes below-gate rows for exactly this feedback loop (bug-183). Under CPERSONA_CONFIDENCE_ORDERING=legacy a seated record's count then lifts its confidence until it passes the gate on unrelated queries; under the default ordering only the returned confidence moves.
issues.fix_sketch: Leave out rows admitted by reservation (_cue_seat, _propagation_seat, _block_distance) when building returned_ids.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: The rows the bump credits are fixed at the point where the gate, autocut, the prior, the count and the cue's bounded move have decided the answer -- before the block reservation, the cue's seats and the propagation seat are added beside it. Those rows passed no quality gate, and crediting them fed the loop bug-183 closed for rescued rows. Fixing the set there, rather than filtering the returned rows by their markers afterwards, means a future held place is excluded without anyone remembering to add its marker to a list. Regression: tests/test_recall_cue.py::test_a_seated_row_earns_no_recall_count and tests/test_blocks_retrieval.py::test_a_reserved_row_earns_no_recall_count_credit_with_confidence_on, each with the window's own row as the control that the bump ran (with confidence off nothing is bumped at all, which is why the older block test could not see this).

issues.summary: (LOW) Block hits are cut to limit + BLOCK_RESERVATION before _block_reserved_rows applies the source_id filter, the exclude set and the episode suppression, so hits those filters drop use up the window and the reservation stays empty although eligible hits lie further down. Example: a source-scoped recall with no channel whose best hits are episodes or other users' memories reserves nothing.
issues.fix_sketch: Filter before cutting, or keep reading hits until the reservation is filled or the list ends.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code. Only with block retrieval on (off by default).
issues.fix_note: The provider hands _block_reserved_rows the hits uncut, and the function hydrates them `wanted` at a time, applying the isolation, source, episode and exclude rules to each page, until `wanted` rows are built or BLOCK_HYDRATE_CAP hits have been looked at. The cap is the re-rank's own depth (BLOCK_RERANK_DEPTH): the ordered hits a recall normally has are the parents of at most that many rows, and the Hamming fallback's longer list is not read further than the re-ranked one would be, so a scope whose filters drop almost everything cannot turn one recall into hundreds of hydration queries. Regression: tests/test_blocks_retrieval.py::test_hits_the_filters_drop_do_not_use_up_the_reservation -- four other users' records whose tail is a block of its own rank first (checked on an unscoped recall), and the caller's record below them is now reserved.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The per-parent cap keeps each record's first N blocks by block_index, while docs/BLOCK_REACH_DESIGN.md says a per-parent best is retained within the examined set. Blocks past the cap in a long record are never examined, so a paraphrase matching the tail of a long record is unreachable through the block arm, which is the case the arm exists for.
issues.pattern: each record contributes at most its
issues.fix_sketch: Rank within each parent by distance before applying the cap, or document the first-N rule and measure what it loses.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: Resolved by making the design describe the code, not the other way round: each record contributes its first BLOCK_PER_PARENT_CAP (64) blocks in text order, and only then is the examined set ranked and each record represented by its best block. Ranking inside each record before the cut was the other option; it means reading every block's bits and changes the scan's cost, which is not a beta change. What the rule gives up was measured and is stated in the design: on a private pack of real agent memories (4,478 records) 82 records (1.8%) run past 64 blocks, 1.4% of block rows lie beyond the share, and 2 of 389 evidence passages of its 300 questions are among them (one question has all its evidence there). The block arm is off by default. tests/test_blocks_retrieval.py pins the first-blocks share and that the design states the constant's value.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Without a current block set, _filled_quote measures an episode head in recall's display string '[Episode] <summary>' rather than in the stored summary, so ranges and expand.span are offset by 10 characters from the text get_contents serves (nodes use episodes.summary). Following a severed quote's expand returns shifted text, and whether an episode's content carries the prefix depends on whether it has a block set.
issues.pattern: text = block_entry\[0\] if block_entry is not None else claim\.content
issues.fix_sketch: Quote episode heads in the stored summary (strip the display prefix before measuring), as the block path already does.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: Without a block set the head quote is now measured in the stored text: for an episode, recall's '[Episode] ' label is removed before ranking and filling, which is the text get_contents, nodes and blocks already measure in. The quote's content therefore no longer carries the label, as it did not on the block path either, so the two paths agree; the item's head_ref still says it is an episode. Keeping the label in content and shifting only the offsets was rejected: content would then not be the concatenation of its ranges, which is what the quote contract and the excerpt tests hold. tests/test_reconstruct_filled_quote.py quotes a long episode, reads every range back through get_contents and requires the joined text to equal the quote, and expands a severed quote and requires it to continue the quote; before the fix both read text 10 characters to the right.

issues.summary: (LOW) resolve_budget raises a low budget only to one preview excerpt (500), but a head is cut to RECONSTRUCT_QUOTE_CHARS (800 by default) and allocate always admits the first head. budget=600 with a long head returns about 800 characters, and because nothing was cut _compact removes the budget fields, so the overrun is not reported.
issues.fix_sketch: Use the head cap as the floor, here and in config.validate_reconstruct_counts.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: resolve_budget raises a caller's budget below one head quote -- RECONSTRUCT_QUOTE_CHARS, or the preview tier with filling off -- rather than below one preview-tier excerpt, so the first head always fits the budget reported. budget=600 with the default 800-character head is now raised to 800 and says so: requested_budget and budget_policy stay in the compact response. The startup refusal of configured values below one preview-tier excerpt is unchanged, so no configuration that starts today stops starting; a configured value between that and a head quote is raised at run time and reported like a caller's. The tool description, the docstrings and RELIABLE_RECALL_2_6 (English and Japanese) now name the head quote. The behaviour golden's m1-reconstruct-count-budget moved in effective_budget alone (500 to 800) and was re-recorded; two tests that named 500 or 600 as their budget were moved to the new floor and above it, their assertions unchanged. Regression: tests/test_reconstruct_filled_quote.py::test_a_budget_below_one_head_quote_is_raised_to_it and ::test_what_is_returned_fits_the_budget_it_reports.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) declare_associations is annotated destructiveHint=False, but its retract argument deletes relations and mentions. Hosts that read destructiveHint to decide whether to ask for approval treat these deletions as non-destructive.
issues.pattern: # Destructive because of `retract`, which deletes relations and mentions \(bug-458\)
issues.fix_sketch: Annotate the tool destructiveHint=True, or move retract to its own tool.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: The tool is annotated destructiveHint=True, the worst thing one call can do, as merge_memories already is for the delete it can reach. Moving retract to a tool of its own was rejected for this line: a new tool is a contract addition, and the annotation alone gives hosts the signal they gate approval on. idempotentHint stays True: declaring or retracting twice leaves the same rows. tests/test_associations_declare.py checks the annotation and pins the set of tools annotated destructive, so a change to any of them is a deliberate one.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) reconstruct's max_hops has no upper bound (the schema sets only minimum 0), while traverse caps the same walk at TRAVERSE_MAX_HOPS = 5. A large max_hops walks the whole connected entity graph, with queries per frontier batch and per entity, so one read call's cost grows with the graph rather than a declared bound.
issues.fix_sketch: Share one cap with traverse and add a maximum to the schema.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: reconstruct lowers max_hops to associations.TRAVERSE_MAX_HOPS, the constant traverse already applies, and both tool schemas now read their maximum from it, so the ceiling lives in one place. A lowered value is reported through fields the response already has: bounds.max_hops states the value applied, and bounds is kept in the compact response when the value was lowered, which is what the contract means by a bound lowered by the library ceiling. Refusing the call was rejected: traverse clamps, and a read that errors on a large bound would differ from its sibling for no gain. The operator default (CPERSONA_RECONSTRUCT_MAX_HOPS) goes through the same ceiling. tests/test_associations_reconstruct.py walks a chain two links longer than the ceiling with max_hops 1,000,000 (before the fix it reached hop 7) and checks that a lowered call keeps bounds while the same call at the ceiling does not carry it.

issues.summary: (LOW) Since 2.6.0a7 the cosine backfill runs only when confidence orders (legacy), but with CPERSONA_CONFIDENCE_ENABLED=true under the default fusion ordering the confidence value returned beside each row is still computed. A lexical-only row therefore takes the cosine-less branch and reports an inflated confidence (and no match_reason.cosine), the bug-155 inversion in the returned value.
issues.pattern: await _backfill_cosines\(db, results, query, project_id, channel, into="_shown_cosine"\)
issues.fix_sketch: Backfill whenever a confidence value is returned, or stop returning confidence for rows without a cosine.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code. Display only: under the default ordering confidence neither orders nor gates.
issues.fix_note: Under the default fusion ordering the cosine is now taken for the returned rows, after the gate, and written to _shown_cosine, which only the returned confidence and match_reason.cosine read. Running the scoring pass's backfill under fusion as well was rejected: _gate_score reads _cosine before _rrf_score, so a backfilled cosine would have changed what the rrf gate compares -- the ordering a7 set out to leave alone -- and the bug-183 rescue keys on the backfill's marker. The rows are fetched on one read connection with the bug-472 counts, only with confidence enabled. Regression: tests/test_bug155_cosine_backfill.py::test_bug460_a_lexical_row_is_shown_on_its_real_cosine_under_fusion, and ::test_bug460_the_shown_cosine_moves_no_gate_order_or_signal, which holds the rows, their order and each gate signal equal with confidence off and on.

issues.summary: (LOW) Node (and block) builds stamp and judge currency with generation.node_keys(), but the backend fingerprint is refreshed only at boot and on traced recalls. If the embedding backend is redeployed with another model under the same URL, later builds stamp the old fingerprint and old nodes stay current, so vectors from two models are ranked together.
issues.fix_sketch: Call generation.refresh() before stamping or judging currency in the build paths and the health check.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: build_nodes, build_blocks, the block backfill and the health repairs (the missing_nodes / missing_blocks prefetch and live scan) call generation.refresh() before they read a key. refresh already kept its answer for REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS (300 s), so this costs at most one /capabilities request per interval, not one per build; it simply had no callers on these paths, only at boot and on traced recalls. A backend redeployed under the same URL is now picked up by the next build after the interval, and nodes and blocks written under the old fingerprint read as not current and are rebuilt. Regression: tests/test_generation_key.py::test_a_block_build_stamps_the_backend_as_it_is_now, ::test_a_node_build_stamps_the_backend_as_it_is_now and ::test_a_health_repair_judges_by_the_backend_as_it_is_now.

issues.summary: (LOW) The node feature is considered available when the client has a callable count_tokens, which is always true for EmbeddingClient; the method returns None without a request in any mode but http. In api mode every health check therefore reads the full text of every record for missing_nodes and every store schedules a no-op probe. The same predicate is repeated in nodes.py.
issues.fix_sketch: Use one predicate: client is not None and client.mode == 'http'.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: nodes.token_report_available() is the one answer to whether the backend can report tokens: an EmbeddingClient only in http mode (the method exists in every mode and answers None without a request in the others), any other client by its method, as before, so test doubles and embedded hosts are unaffected. building_enabled, prepare_nodes, overflowing and the health check's _node_report_available all use it. In api mode the missing_nodes check now reads no record text and a store schedules no probe; the finding it reported there was already none, so no output changes. Regression: tests/test_record_nodes_build.py::test_only_an_http_client_has_a_token_report, ::test_a_client_that_is_not_an_embedding_client_is_taken_at_its_method and ::test_an_api_mode_health_check_reads_no_record_text.

issues.summary: (LOW) A failing build_nodes / build_blocks / backfill task retries by sleeping TASK_RETRY_DELAY (30 s) while it is still the head of the FIFO queue, so every task queued behind it (profile updates included) waits about 90 s per failing build during an embedding outage. These builds are derived data the health check repairs anyway.
issues.pattern: elif task_type in derived and await self\._other_work_waits\(task_id, derived\):
issues.fix_sketch: Requeue derived-data builds at the tail, or drop them after the first failure and leave them to the repair.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: A failing derived build (build_nodes, build_blocks, backfill_blocks) that has a task of another type queued behind it is moved to the back of the queue with its retry counted (_requeue_at_tail: the row takes the next id, keeping its payload and its session attribution), instead of sleeping TASK_RETRY_DELAY at the head. Builds with only other builds behind them keep the delay: rotating among themselves would spend all their retries in a second of an outage, and they are what the delay is for. Discarding a failing build outright was rejected for the same reason -- a short outage would cost every queued build. Retry counting and the discard at TASK_MAX_RETRIES are unchanged. Regression: tests/test_task_queue.py::test_a_failing_build_does_not_hold_a_profile_update, ::test_a_moved_build_keeps_its_session_and_its_place_is_new and ::test_builds_waiting_only_behind_builds_keep_the_delay.

issues.summary: (LOW) shortfall_reason reports budget_exhausted whenever allocate cut any head, including a held (reservation) item that sits outside the window. When the window was short because the candidates ran out and the budget only cut a held item (already reported as reserved_omitted), the reason blames the budget.

issues.fix_note: shortfall_reason blames the budget only when it cut one of the window's own items (fewer window items returned than the window held). A held item the budget cut is already reported as reserved_omitted, and a window short because the candidates ran out now says exhausted_candidates. Regression: tests/test_reconstruct_block_reservation.py::test_a_short_window_is_blamed_on_the_budget_only_when_it_cut_the_window.

Regression: tests/test_reconstruct_block_reservation.py::test_reserved_rows_do_not_make_a_short_retrieval_look_full, whose precondition asserts the recall filled its limit with one held row.

issues.summary: (LOW) excerpt_basis reports 'blocks' (documented as ranked lexically and by bits) even when no bits took part: the query vector is missing, or the stored bits' width differs from the query's so the ranking falls back to lexical only.

issues.summary: (LOW) Block currency checks count, first, last and model only; the node layout is not part of it. A block set built before its record's nodes existed (a node build that failed and was retried later, or a backfill that reached old records first) stays current after the nodes land, although it may cross a node boundary, against the rule that a block does not cross a node.
issues.pattern: return all\(end in ends for end in node_ends if 0 < end < text_len\)
issues.fix_sketch: Record the node bounds a block set was cut against and treat a change as stale.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: Block currency now includes the node layout: a set is current only if every node end inside the text is also a block end, so a set built before its record's nodes existed is found stale once they land, and the rebuild cuts at the node ends. The rule is blocks.block_set_is_current (see bug-479), which every reader applies; the builder, the sweep and the missing_blocks check read the node ends beside the block rows. Regression: tests/test_blocks_rerank.py::test_a_set_that_crosses_a_node_end_is_not_current (stale, listed by the check, rebuilt at the node end, then current) and ::test_the_rule_reads_the_node_ends_it_is_given.

issues.summary: (LOW) Recall excerpts read stored block sets without checking CPERSONA_BLOCK_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED, while reconstruct reads them only behind that switch. With blocks built but retrieval off, a recall excerpt is ranked on stored node-bounded spans and bits while reconstruct's head quote for the same record and query re-segments and ranks lexically, so the two disagree although the code says they are the same passages.
issues.pattern: block_sets = await reconstruct\._current_block_sets\(agent_id, parsed\) if blocks\.retrieval_enabled\(\) else \{\}
issues.fix_sketch: Gate both on the same switch (see the duplicated excerpt rule).
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: Recall excerpts read a stored block set only while CPERSONA_BLOCK_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED is on, as the quotation does: off means the index may exist and nothing reads it (the configuration page says so). With building on and retrieval off, an excerpt is now divided at read time and reports 'lexical'. Two excerpt tests that asserted 'blocks' with only building on were moved onto retrieval on, where their assertions hold unchanged. Regression: tests/test_recall_excerpt.py::test_a_block_set_is_not_read_while_block_retrieval_is_off.

issues.summary: (LOW) Changing CPERSONA_PRIOR_FAR_WEIGHT changes the fused score distribution (and at 0 the channel count), but neither SCORING_VERSION nor the calibration sidecar records the weight, so a restored fused gate filters a quantity it was not calibrated on.
issues.fix_sketch: Include the far weight in the calibration identity, or recalibrate when it changes.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code. Only with the vector reach set above the scan window.
issues.fix_note: memory_handlers.calibration_fingerprint() is SCORING_VERSION, with '+far_weight=<w>' appended when CPERSONA_PRIOR_FAR_WEIGHT is not the default. The sidecar is stamped with it, and the restore guard, the carry of other agents' values and deep_calibration_staleness compare against it, so a gate calibrated at one weight is not restored at another and the startup guard recalibrates. Appending only off the default keeps every sidecar written so far valid: a deployment at the default sees no change and loses no per-agent calibration. Read from memory_handlers' copy of the weight, the one the fusion reads. Regression: tests/test_gate_remediation.py::test_the_far_weight_is_part_of_the_calibration_fingerprint and ::test_a_gate_calibrated_at_another_far_weight_is_not_restored (both directions).

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Whether a node set is current is decided three ways: nodes._nodes_current and nodes._current check count, first, last and model, while reconstruct._current_node_sets also requires contiguous spans and non-NULL embeddings. A node set with a gap or a NULL embedding is rejected by the reader (the record is quoted from its start) but judged current by the build and the missing_nodes check, so it is never rebuilt.
issues.pattern: return bool\(count\) and first == 0 and last == text_len and current == count
issues.fix_sketch: One helper applying the strict rule, used by all three.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: nodes.node_set_is_current is now the only rule: the spans cover the stored text from 0 to its length with no gap or overlap, and every node has an embedding from a model this server reports. The builder, the missing_nodes scan and the reader all call it. The strict rule was taken, not the loose one, because the reader's strictness is what protects a quote: a gap puts an offset into text no node was measured over, and a NULL embedding is a node nothing can rank. The health scan now reads per-node spans (never the blobs) instead of an aggregate, since contiguity cannot be read from MIN/MAX/COUNT, and joins them to the parent so an agent-scoped run stays in scope. tests/test_record_nodes_build.py damages one built set three ways (gap, NULL embedding, overlap), each keeping count, first, last and model as a healthy set has them, and requires the three judges to agree and the builder to rebuild; before the fix the scan did not list the record and the builder answered 'nodes already current'. The block-set copy of the reader (the duplication entry of the same review) is left for its own change.

issues.summary: (LOW) The confidence shown for cue-seat and propagation-seat rows is computed with recall_count 0 and the window's time range, because recall_counts holds only the window's own rows. A seated memory with a real recall history reports a lower confidence than the same row would inside the window.
issues.pattern: unread = \[i for i in _memory_ids\(results\) if i not in recall_counts\]
issues.fix_sketch: Read the seat rows' counts too, or omit confidence for seat rows.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code. Display only.
