The time range was never the window's: it is the scope's span, the same for every row. Regression: tests/test_recall_cue.py::test_a_seated_row_shows_the_confidence_of_its_own_history, on seats no ordinary arm reached (a seat the count cut was scored, which is why the count-cut scenario could not show this).

issues.summary: (LOW) One unclosed bracket inside a balanced quotation makes the outer quotation look unclosed too, so the divider cuts inside it. Reproduced: '彼は「今日は休む。(たぶん」と言った。' divides into ['彼は「今日は休む。', '(たぶん」と言った。'], while the same text without the '(' is one block.
issues.fix_sketch: Track each bracket kind separately, or reset inner depth when the enclosing quotation closes.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Reproduced by running it.
issues.fix_note: The first pass of _bracket_depth now lets a closing bracket close the nearest opening it matches, marking every opening left above it on the stack as unmatched; before, only the top of the stack could close, so one unclosed ( inside 「…」 held the 」 back and both were read as unclosed. The second pass is unchanged: with the true strays removed it pairs the rest exactly as the first pass did. A closer that matches nothing on the stack still closes nothing. Regression: tests/test_blocks_segment.py::test_an_unclosed_bracket_inside_a_quotation_does_not_open_the_quotation, with the finding's own control (the same text without the ( divides identically) and a case where the closer passes over an unclosed opening and no further. Re-anchored with bug-536: the matching pass now keeps a stack per closing bracket, so it is linear; the line that marks every opening above the match as unclosed is the one pinned.

issues.summary: (LOW) do_reconstruct reads providers.active() once, and its candidate recall reads it again instead of receiving the same set, breaking providers.py's contract that a reconstruct's candidate recall uses the same set. A providers.install between the two reads builds the pool with one set and the items with another. The time cue is also parsed twice.
issues.fix_sketch: Pass providers_ (and the parsed cue) from do_reconstruct into do_recall.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code. No production caller installs another set today.
issues.fix_note: do_recall takes the provider set, an already-read TimeCue and a list for the query vector as library arguments, and reconstruct passes the set it read, the cue it parsed and a list (bug-494) to its candidate recall. The pool and the items are built with one provider set, and the cue is read once. Regression: tests/test_reconstruct_filled_quote.py::test_one_provider_set_and_one_reading_of_the_cue.

issues.summary: (LOW) validate_dict turns an absent or non-object argument into {}, so this branch (and associations.declare's non-dict report) is unreachable over MCP: a malformed retract such as a list is silently ignored instead of reported.
issues.fix_sketch: Check the raw argument before validate_dict, or remove the dead branches.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: Measured before changing anything: over MCP a malformed retract is not silently ignored. The schema declares it an object and the MCP layer refuses a list, a string or a number with 'Input validation error' before the handler runs. What the finding did establish is that the handler's own report was unreachable, and that the report therefore rests on the schema alone -- validate_dict would turn a non-object into {} had the schema not caught it. The dead branch is removed with a comment saying where the report comes from, and a test drives the tool boundary with three non-object values so that dropping `type: object` from the schema turns it red. associations.declare keeps its non-dict report: it is a library entry point as well, and a direct caller does reach it. Regression: tests/test_associations_declare.py::test_a_retract_that_is_not_an_object_is_refused_at_the_boundary.

issues.fix_sketch: Either keep the slots as a declared extension point, or call the stages directly; traced recalls would lose trace.providers and trace.budget.iterations, so decide against the replay contract first.

issues.summary: (LOW) record_nodes.token_count and record_nodes.window are written by write_nodes but read only by tests: no runtime check enforces token_count <= window, and the currency rule ignores window.
issues.fix_sketch: Use them (window in the currency rule when no fingerprint is known, or a check of the invariant) or stop maintaining them.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.

issues.summary: (LOW) _drain handles the same circular import two ways: a nodes parameter with a lazy-import fallback, and inline imports in the block branches.
issues.fix_sketch: Import nodes inside _drain like the block branches and drop the parameter.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: _drain resolves both lazily imported modules once, at its start; the block branches no longer import inside themselves, and they dispatch on blocks.TASK_TYPE and blocks.BACKFILL_TASK_TYPE rather than repeating the strings. The nodes parameter stays, because tests hand in the module they patched. Behaviour-preserving: the queue and build tests pin the dispatch.

issues.summary: (LOW) _ASSOCIATIONS_PROPERTY is shared by store and declare_associations but carries a store-only sentence (malformed items reported in associations.dropped, the memory stored regardless), which is wrong for declare_associations whose drops are top-level. declare_associations' description also repeats the normalization, extraction and alias sentences the property carries; about 1.9k characters are sent twice every session.
issues.fix_sketch: Keep the store-only sentence in store's copy and remove the repeated sentences.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: declare_associations takes the same object as store's rider with a description of its own (_DECLARE_ASSOCIATIONS_PROPERTY): it no longer speaks of a stored memory or of associations.dropped, since this tool's drops are top-level. The tool description stops restating the normalization and alias sentences, which the nested entity and alias descriptions carry and which are sent with the tool anyway; the entity description now says names and aliases are compared after normalization, so nothing the tool description said is lost. declare_associations' description and schema together are about 430 characters shorter; the nested object is still sent once per tool, as MCP has no shared definitions across tools. Regression: tests/test_associations_declare.py::test_declare_associations_describes_its_own_object and ::test_declare_associations_does_not_restate_the_nested_descriptions.

issues.summary: (LOW) blocks._parent_text and the block currency predicate copy nodes._parent_text and nodes._current, and write_blocks reads the same parent row twice (_parent_text, then _parent_axes).
issues.fix_sketch: Reuse the nodes helpers and read text and axes in one SELECT.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: blocks uses nodes._parent_text rather than its own copy, and write_blocks reads the record's text and its isolation axes in one statement (_parent_row) inside its transaction, instead of two reads of the same row. The currency predicate is no longer a copy of the node one but the shared-shape block rule of bug-479. Behaviour-preserving: the compare-and-swap is pinned by the build and sweep tests of a record that moved under the build.

issues.summary: (LOW) For refs without a current block set, excerpts.for_refs opens another connection and reads each record's text with one SELECT per ref, although the text is already in the row being turned into the message (and _current_block_sets read it in a batch). Excerpts are on by default at the MCP boundary, so this runs on ordinary recalls.
issues.pattern: known = \{ref: stored_text\(ref, shown\) for ref, shown in \(texts or \{\}\)\.items\(\) if shown\}
issues.fix_sketch: Pass the texts in (or return them from _current_block_sets); the text is identical, so the excerpts are.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: excerpts.for_refs takes the texts the recall rows already carry, and recall passes them; a ref without one is read in one query per kind, not one SELECT per ref on its own connection. Regression: tests/test_reconstruct_filled_quote.py::test_excerpts_read_no_record_the_recall_row_already_carries, from the statements the read connection traces.

issues.summary: (LOW) Every recall builds bookkeeping that only off-by-default features read: the reached set, cue_rank, admitted_rids, the window copy, and the admitted copy with check_reorder's two sorts; scope spans are also read separately for the prior, the cue and scoring.
issues.pattern: window = list\(results\) if propagation_seat and not gate_fallback else \[\]
issues.fix_sketch: Build each only when its feature is on (time_cue, propagation_seat, a non-built-in prior) and reuse one span read; each value is consumed only in those branches.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: The reached set and the admitted set are built only when a time cue is given, and the window copy only when the propagation seat will run. The prior's copy and its reorder check are kept: the prior is a provider slot, and the check is the contract an installed provider is held to, whatever the rate. The scope span stays read where each consumer reads it -- every read after the first is a cache hit (scope_stats), and threading one value through the provider slots would change their signatures for no measured gain. Regression: tests/test_recall_cue.py::test_a_plain_recall_builds_no_seat_bookkeeping (no row identity is computed for a plain recall; the cued recall is the control).

issues.summary: (LOW) With the propagation seat on, every recall reruns the whole pipeline at depth 100 on a second connection (vector scan, both lexical arms, profile read, scoring, gate), roughly doubling its cost, although each arm's shallow list is a prefix of its deep one.
issues.fix_sketch: Run the arms once at the larger depth and slice for the window (the window stays byte-identical).
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code. Off by default.

issues.summary: (LOW) reconstruct embeds the query a second time, although the candidate recall already embedded it and keeps it in query_vec_out (excerpts already reuse that vector).
issues.pattern: query_vec = np\.asarray\(recalled_vec\[0\], dtype=np\.float32\) if recalled_vec else await _query_vector\(query\)
issues.fix_sketch: Return the recall's vector to reconstruct; same model, same input, same vector.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: reconstruct reads the query vector its candidate recall embedded (handed back through do_recall's query_vec_out), and embeds the query itself only when that recall produced none, as a remote vector search does. Regression: tests/test_reconstruct_filled_quote.py::test_a_reconstruction_embeds_its_query_once.

issues.summary: (LOW) Node sets, embeddings included, are read for every head even under the default head cap, where heads are quoted by _filled_quote and never use nodes; a non-empty result then triggers a query embedding nothing uses, and can report quote_selection 'lexical_only' when that embed fails although no node chose a quote.
issues.pattern: node_claims = \[c for _, head, others in entries_claims for c in \(\(head,\) if head_cap <= 0 else \(\)\) \+ tuple\(others\)\]
issues.fix_sketch: Read node sets only for non-head claims (and heads only when the head cap is 0).
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: Node sets are read only for the claims a node can quote: the other claims, and the heads only with filling off. Under the default head cap a filled head reads no node set, so no embeddings are read for it, and quote_selection 'lexical_only' is reported only when a node or block ranking actually lacked the vector. Regression: tests/test_reconstruct_filled_quote.py::test_a_head_quoted_by_filling_reads_no_node_set.

issues.summary: (LOW) One reconstruct call reads the same memory texts and episode rows several times, each on its own connection (node set text, block set text, candidate context and episode spans).
issues.fix_sketch: Merge _episode_spans into the candidate-context read and read parent text once for both node and block sets.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: The candidates' context and the episodes' spans are read on one connection, each episode once (_read_candidates replaces _candidate_context and _episode_spans), and the node and block sets on one connection with each text read once (_current_sets, bug-479). Behaviour-preserving: the bundling, containment and quotation tests pin what these reads feed.

issues.summary: (LOW) Each block vector runs vector.pack_for_storage twice (in pack_bits and pack_int8), a per-element Python loop whose bytes are discarded, so a 1024-dimension, 20-block record does about twice the needed work per store.
issues.fix_sketch: Validate once and derive both the bits and the int8 bytes from one array.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: blocks.quantise returns both stored forms of a block vector after asking vector.pack_for_storage once; prepare_blocks uses it instead of calling pack_bits and pack_int8, which each asked it. The refusal itself stays delegated to pack_for_storage rather than restated, for the reason pack_bits gives: one answer to whether a vector is usable. pack_bits and pack_int8 are kept for their other callers (the query's bits, the tests). Regression: tests/test_blocks_rerank.py::test_a_build_asks_the_storage_refusal_once_per_block and test_quantise_is_the_two_packers.

issues.summary: (LOW) A record that divides into one block never has block rows, so the backfill treats it as not current on every sweep (one is queued at each process start) and sends each through a per-record connection, node query and segment(), counted against the sweep's caps, ending with a full coverage scan.
issues.fix_sketch: Fetch the page's node bounds in one query, segment inline, and skip single-block records without counting them.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: The sweep reads a page's node ends in one query (_bounds_for) and divides each non-current record offline before doing anything else with it. A record that divides into one block is counted as needing none and passed over without its own connection, node query or embedding call, and it no longer counts against the record and character caps, so a corpus of short records does not stop every run at its first few. _build_one takes the node ends it was handed. What is not changed: such a record still has no block rows, so the sweep still reads it on each process start -- recording that it needs none would be a new column -- but the read is now the page's own, and the time bound still ends a run. Regression: tests/test_blocks_backfill.py::test_records_that_need_no_blocks_do_not_use_up_the_record_cap and ::test_a_record_that_needs_no_blocks_opens_no_connection_of_its_own.

issues.summary: (LOW) divide() re-measures the whole remaining text before cutting each node, so an n-node record posts O(n^2) characters to /count_tokens, and the first measurement repeats the store-time probe.
issues.pattern: probe = rest if reach is None else rest\[: 2 \* reach\]
issues.fix_sketch: Measure a bounded prefix of the rest once a span is accepted; each span is still re-measured on its own text.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: Only divide()'s first measurement reads the whole text. After it, the text ahead is measured in a prefix twice as long as the last window reached, widened while the window does not close inside it, so the characters posted grow linearly with the record rather than with its square. A prefix that reaches the end is the rest itself, so the last span is judged exactly as before, and a cut is still accepted only on its own report. The divisions are identical to the old algorithm's on every text the suite divides, checked against a copy of it kept in the test as the oracle. The repeat of the store-time probe is not removed: that report is taken before the record is queued and is not carried across the queue. Regression: tests/test_record_nodes_build.py::test_a_bounded_measurement_divides_as_the_whole_rest_did and ::test_only_the_first_measurement_reads_the_whole_text.

issues.summary: (LOW) Nothing records that a record fits the embedding window, so every missing_nodes run sends the full text of every record without current nodes to /count_tokens, and check_health(fix=True) does it twice (the prefetch, then the residual re-run, which only needs the count).
issues.fix_sketch: Pass the prefetch's result into the residual run, and consider skipping records whose byte length cannot exceed the window.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code. Re-judged 2026-09-30 and left open as a design item. Not re-measuring a record that fits means recording that it fits, which is a column or a table. The half about check_health(fix=True) measuring twice is the residual re-run, and that re-run is the verdict bug-254 requires to come from post-repair state -- other repairs in the same run rewrite record text, so the first scan's answer cannot stand in for it without the same record of what was measured against which text.

issues.summary: (LOW) traverse selects full memory contents and episode summaries for every returned entity only to keep the refs, and always runs one or two COUNT queries even when fewer than limit rows came back.
issues.fix_sketch: Select ids only, fetch limit + 1 rows as walk_graph does, and count only when the extra row is present.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-09-29 review of the code added in 2.6.0a1..a8. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_note: _mentioning_records takes refs_only, which reads the ids alone and returns no row, and traverse passes it: the content and summary it read were dropped as soon as the refs were taken. walk_graph still reads the rows, because a walked claim quotes them. The count is a query only for a table whose read came back full (as many rows as the limit); a read that returned fewer has already counted itself, so an entity with few mentions costs no COUNT at all. Regression: tests/test_associations_traverse.py::test_traverse_reads_the_refs_and_not_the_text and ::test_traverse_counts_only_when_a_read_came_back_full, both read from the statements the read connection traces.

issues.summary: (LOW) With an empty query, the time cue's keyword half orders the period's rows by created_at -- when the row was stored, at one-second resolution -- rather than by the timestamp the period itself is defined on, and rows stored within the same second tie and come back in rowid order. tests/test_recall_cue.py::test_an_empty_query_searches_the_period_by_recency therefore passes only while its twelve seeded rows are stored within one second: reproduced by setting created_at directly, the cue arm returns the period's rows as seed positions [5, 6, 7] when all twelve share a second and [7, 5, 6] when the second changes after the seventh -- the order observed when the test failed once in nine full-suite runs. The test expects the order of the rows' own timestamps, and so does the comment above the query ('the period's newest records'); the ordinary recall's empty-query path, which the comment cites as its model, orders by created_at.
issues.pattern: id ASC" if window is not None else "created_at DESC, id DESC"
issues.fix_sketch: Either order the cue arm's empty-query list by the rows' own time (datetime(timestamp) DESC, id ASC), the axis the period is measured on -- a change to which rows a cue's seats take -- or keep created_at, give it a deterministic tie-break, and seed the test with distinct created_at values so it states the order it relies on.
issues.note: Found while running mutation baselines for the 2.6.0 LOW batch. Choosing between the two is a decision about which time a cue ranks by, not a test repair.
issues.fix_note: With a period, the empty-query keyword search orders by datetime(timestamp) DESC, id ASC -- the records' own time, the axis the period is measured on, with the row id settling equal times -- and without one it keeps created_at DESC, so only the cue arm changes. The alternative, keeping created_at with a tie-break and seeding the test with distinct created_at values, would have made the order deterministic but left it wrong: an import stores rows in an order unrelated to their own time, and created_at would then decide which of a period's rows the cue's seats hold. The episodes of the same arm were already ordered by their own time. Regression: tests/test_recall_cue.py::test_an_empty_query_orders_the_period_by_the_records_time_not_by_when_they_were_stored and ::test_records_of_one_time_in_the_period_come_back_in_the_order_they_were_stored (created_at written one second apart, running against the period's order), ::test_the_keyword_search_without_a_period_still_lists_the_most_recently_stored_first; mutations M216 and M217. Re-anchored with bug-575: the listing without a period now breaks a created_at tie by id.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) On Windows a rebuild of the contiguous index failed with PermissionError: [WinError 5] at the os.replace in build_index whenever any process still held the index it replaces. load_index mapped every array with np.memmap and cached_index keeps the loaded index for the life of the process, so a server that had searched since it started held the file mapped until it exited; Windows refuses to replace a mapped file, POSIX allows it. A production user reported the rebuild failing intermittently on Windows 11 (and once succeeding three times in a row with the same setup, consistent with the server not having searched in that session). The search stayed correct because rows outside the index are read from SQLite, but the index went stale and searches slowed.
issues.fix_sketch: On Windows, read the arrays into memory instead of mapping them, so no handle is left open on the file a rebuild replaces.
issues.note: Field report from a Windows 11 user (2.5.11). Reproduced on windows-latest in CI by loading the index and rebuilding it in the same process: PermissionError [WinError 5] Access is denied at vector_index.py:319.
issues.fix_note: load_index maps the file only where _maps_files() is true (not Windows); on Windows each array is read with np.fromfile at its offset. A new Windows CI job runs the reproduction; tests/test_vector_index_rebuild_while_loaded.py also runs the read path on every platform and compares it field by field with the mapped one.

issues.summary: (HIGH) The block arm's examined read ranked every block in the store before its cap applied. _examined numbered each record's admitted rows with ROW_NUMBER() and cut with LIMIT, and with agent_id = ? in the filter SQLite read the agent's rows through idx_record_blocks_axes and sorted all of them before returning the first, so BLOCK_EXAMINED_CAP bounded what was returned, not what was read. Recall cost grew with the whole block table on the default configuration: over 100,000 memories of real length (3,480,069 blocks) recall took a median of 20.7 s on an Intel N150, and on a laptop this one statement was 9.7 s of a 10.2 s recall.
issues.fix_note: The rows are read in primary key order through the key's own index, named with INDEXED BY so the planner cannot take the axes index and sort; both caps are counted while reading, over the rows the filter admits, and the read stops when the examined cap is full. On the same corpus the read went from 2.6 s to 0.11 s and returned the same 250,000 rows in the same order, and recall returned identical responses for every question compared. Rejected: adding INDEXED BY to the window statement alone, which kept the window's materialisation and an outer sort (1.4 s); and replacing the window with block_index < cap, which changes what a record contributes when some of its blocks are not admitted (no bits yet, or another model's).
issues.note: Found by timing recall over a corpus built through the store path with real conversation lengths; the earlier latency record used a synthetic corpus with no blocks, so it could not see this. Lands in the first release after 2.6.5a3.

issues.summary: (HIGH) The block arm read the two hundred re-rank vectors with a row-value IN: WHERE (parent_kind, parent_id, block_index) IN (VALUES ...). SQLite 3.40.1, the version Debian 12's Python links (and so the official python images built on it), does not search the primary key for that form: its plan is SCAN record_block_vectors, so every recall read every stored vector in the store. Over 100,000 memories of real length (3,480,069 blocks) this one statement took 4.6 s of a 6.7 s recall on an Intel N150; SQLite 3.50.4 searches the key and takes under a millisecond, so the cost appears only where the older library is linked.
issues.fix_note: The keys are joined as a table (a CTE of VALUES joined to record_block_vectors on all three key columns), which SQLite 3.40.1 plans as a search of the primary key per key: 6.1 ms against 4,277.6 ms for the same 200 keys on the same database. Rejected: reading by parent with parent_id IN (...), which the old library also indexes but which reads every block of each listed parent; and one point query per key, which costs two hundred round trips. A query plan cannot pin this in CI, whose SQLite searches the key for both forms, so the test pins the statement's form and a second test pins that only the listed keys come back.
issues.note: Found while profiling recall after bug-504 on the reference machine, where the CI-tested library hid it. The row-value IN in _stored_vectors was the only one in the package. Lands in the first release after 2.6.5a3.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The evidence order of reconstruct depended on the Python version, so the determinism invariant held on one interpreter and not across them. `evidence_order` fuses three ranks (the record's place, the passage's place inside it, the block cosine's place) with sum(1/(k+1+rank)). Two passages whose ranks are the same three numbers in another order, (0, 0, 1) and (0, 1, 0), have equal scores and the tie rule should put the earlier text first. Python 3.11's sum() adds left to right, so (a + a) + b and (a + b) + a can round one unit apart: at the default k = 60 they came out 0.04891591750396616 and 0.048915917503966164 and the later passage went first. Python 3.12 made sum() of floats compensated, which keeps the tie, so the same store and question returned a different quote under 3.11 and 3.12+ (1 of 150 development questions). The whole sequence calls the same order. The two-list fusions of nodes and blocks add two terms, which round the same in any order.
issues.pattern: fused = \[math\.fsum\(1\.0 / \(k \+ 1 \+ ranks\[n\]\) for ranks in lists\)
issues.fix_note: The fused score is math.fsum of the terms, which is correctly rounded and so independent of the order they are added in, on every Python version: equal terms give an equal score and the tie rule decides. This matches what 3.12+ already returned; only 3.11's output changes, on ties of this kind. Rejected: comparing the scores as exact fractions, which also fixes it but changes more code for no difference in the order; and fixing the order of addition, which keeps 3.11 and 3.12 apart. The tests pin the case found on the development questions and the same tie at every k from 1 to 399; adding left to right (functools.reduce) turns them red on 3.11 and 3.13, and plain sum() on 3.11.
issues.note: Found during the 2.6.8 development acceptance run, which used Python 3.11. Left unfixed until 2.6.8's test had been judged, so the baseline did not move during it. Lands in 2.6.10a1.

issues.summary: (HIGH) `merge_memories(mode='move')` permanently destroys the declared association graph of every moved record and still answers ok:true. The copy passes (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3686-3688) copy only memories, episodes and profiles under new ids; no entities, aliases, mentions or relations reach the target. `_delete_merged_source_rows` then deletes the copied source rows by id (`_MOVE_DELETE_SQL`, cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3551-3555), and the `associations_memories_ad` / `associations_episodes_ad` triggers (cpersona/database.py:922-934) delete every mention and every relation anchored on or naming those rows. `_MOVE_LEFT_SQL` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3557-3561) counts only memories, episodes and profiles, so `left_at_source` reads all zero while the source keeps its entities and aliases with no mentions, and the emptied-agent teardown (calibration and remote namespace purge, cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3724-3726) runs anyway. `_delete_agent_rows` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:663-664) does clear entities and relations, so the move path is missing that step. Reproduced on a fresh database through the public handlers: after a move, the target had no entities, mentions or relations, and traverse on the target returned `no_such_entity`. Primary data survives on the target; what is lost is the declaration layer.
issues.fix_sketch: Inside the merge transaction, before the move deletes anything, copy the source's entities and aliases into the target's scope and re-create mentions and relations with mem:/ep: refs remapped through the old-to-new id map; when a move empties the source, clear its leftover entities and agent-level relations and count graph rows in left_at_source. If carrying the graph is out of scope for now, refuse or report a move whose source has declarations instead of destroying them under ok:true.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced end to end on a fresh database. Introduced alongside the bug-218/bug-222 rewrite of the move path, which dropped the graph cleanup that the agent-delete path keeps.
issues.fix_note: Inside the merge transaction, do_merge_memories now reads the source agent's declared graph and carries it to the target before the move deletes anything. It goes through associations.carry using the copy passes' ref map, which covers both copied rows and rows skipped as equal to an existing target row. When the move empties the source, its leftover entities and record-free relations are deleted only if everything was carried. Otherwise they stay and are counted in left_at_source. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u01.py::test_merge_move_carries_the_declared_graph_to_the_target red.

issues.summary: (HIGH) The write seam never takes SQLite's write lock up front, so a second server process's committed edit or lock can be destroyed by merge_memories(mode='move') or deep_check(fix=true). `transaction()` serialises writers only with the in-process `async with _write_lock` (cpersona/database.py:347) and the write connection is opened with the driver's default legacy isolation (`aiosqlite.connect(DB_PATH)`, database.py:1145), so the SQLite transaction begins only at the first DML and any SELECT at the top of a body runs in autocommit without a snapshot. In do_merge_memories (admin_handlers.py:3685-3693) the first 500-row source page is read (admin_handlers.py:3327-3332), copied from those stale values, and the source rows are then deleted by id with no content or lock re-check (admin_handlers.py:3550-3554), so an edit committed in the gap is lost and a lock committed in the gap is dropped (the copy is unlocked and the locked source row is deleted). deep_short_content selects rows of 5 characters or fewer (checks.py:3797-3799) and deletes them by id guarded only by `locked = 0` (checks.py:3819-3821), so a row another process has just expanded into a real note is deleted. Both operations report ok:true and the other session's write also returned ok:true. Reproduced with two real processes driving production handlers: with no artificial lock hold, a stress loop of update_memory against deep_check(fix=true, checks=['short_content']) lost 1722 of 36069 acknowledged edits in 20 s; the merge edit and lock variants were reproduced with a second connection committing in the gap. Needs two or more server processes on one database file (the stdio deployment, one process per client); a single HTTP process is not affected.
issues.fix_sketch: Make transaction() take SQLite's write lock when the body starts, for example by opening the write connection with isolation_level=None and issuing BEGIN IMMEDIATE before the yield, so a body's reads share the cross-process serialization of its writes. As defense in depth, re-check the read state in the id-keyed deletes (re-test `LENGTH(TRIM(content)) <= ?` in short_content, and a locked/content predicate on the merge-move delete).
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced with separate OS processes against the production handlers. Related to bug-043, which serialised merge against in-process committers only.
issues.fix_note: transaction() issues BEGIN IMMEDIATE after taking the in-process _write_lock and before the body runs, so SQLite's write lock covers the body's reads as well as its writes and no other process can commit between a body's read and its write-by-id. Skipped for :memory: (the database belongs to one connection, and an open write transaction would make the export snapshot's backup refuse) and when the connection is already in a transaction. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a1_u03.py::test_bug508_* red (4 tests).

issues.summary: (HIGH) Under the default configuration (rrf fusion, confidence off, no calibrated gate) the heuristic gate rejects every row that only one arm voted for in a pool of 30 or fewer rows. The threshold is `min_score * RRF_MAX_SCALE` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:1135), where `RRF_MAX_SCALE = 3.0 / (RRF_K + 1)` (cpersona/config.py:987) assumes rank 1 in three arms, but a single-arm row scores at most 1/(K+1); with `min_score = 0.5 - 0.3*log(n+1)/log(500)` (memory_handlers.py:1004-1005) it passes only when n >= 31. With EMBEDDING_MODE=none every row is single-arm, and gate_fallback does not apply because it depends on CONFIDENCE_ENABLED. Reproduced through the real handlers on fresh databases: N=30 returned no messages for a query matching a stored memory's exact text (score 0.016393 below threshold 0.016436), N=31 returned the row, and reconstruct returned no items in the same case. Meanwhile the advisory says recall is keyword/FTS-only and cpersona/health.py:116 and :150 say recall still returns results on shared keywords, so the caller cannot tell a filtered result from a missing memory. The same applies with embeddings on, before calibration, to rows found by one arm only.
issues.fix_sketch: Make the heuristic rrf threshold reachable by a single rank-1 vote, for example by scaling it to the number of arms that can actually vote for the row's table and mode. Alternatively, give the default configuration a floor under which an exact lexical match is never silently dropped, independent of CONFIDENCE_ENABLED.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. Related: bug-216, whose floor of 0.5 is not reachable on the rrf scale by a single arm. The fix needs a scoring decision about the gate's scale.
issues.fix_note: _recall_rrf now flags the rows only one retriever could rank (_mark_single_arm_rows: no embedding client, a query that was not embedded with remote search unarmed, or a first-ranked keyword/episode-FTS row with a NULL embedding after the local scan ran). _apply_quality_gate caps the heuristic rrf threshold for those rows at the one-vote maximum 1/(RRF_K+1), so a lone retriever's rank-1 row passes on pools of 30 or fewer and lower ranks keep their old outcome. If this is reverted, tests/test_2611a1_u04.py::test_mode_none_returns_the_exact_match_on_a_small_pool, test_query_embed_failure_returns_the_exact_match, test_row_without_embedding_is_returned_while_the_vector_arm_runs and test_single_arm_cap_admits_the_first_rank_only go red, and so does tests/test_equivalence_252.py[m1-recall-cue-no-embedding]. The old open-state pattern 'else min_score \* RRF_MAX_SCALE' is still present after the fix (the line is kept), so the entry needs this new anchor.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The publish workflow uploads to PyPI with no test gate, and commits pushed directly to the maintenance branches get no CI. `.github/workflows/publish.yml` triggers on any `v*` tag push or manual dispatch (:18-27), checks only that the tag equals `__version__`, then runs `uv build` (:85) and the PyPI publish action (:88); it has no test job, no `needs:` and no CI status lookup. Its only safeguard is the comment at :11-12 that tags are cut only on merged, CI-green master. That is not true for the maintenance lines: `ci.yml` runs on push only for `branches: [master]` (:10-11), and the 2.4.x branch carries the same trigger, so a backport or version-bump commit pushed directly to 2.4.x or 2.5.x runs no job at all, and tagging it publishes it untested. This has happened: tag v2.4.41 is not on master's history, it points at a commit with no CI check runs and no associated pull request, and that version is on PyPI. A branch ruleset requires pull requests on 2.5.x but can be bypassed by the maintainer account, and 2.4.x is not covered.
issues.fix_sketch: Before building, make publish.yml require a successful CI run for the tagged commit (query its check runs or combined status, or run the test job inside the workflow). Also add the maintenance branches to ci.yml's push trigger, or cover them with a pull-request ruleset that cannot be bypassed.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed against the workflows and the repository's tag and check-run history. The variant where ci.yml's cancel-in-progress leaves a tagged master commit without finished CI was not tested; see bug-594.
issues.fix_note: The PyPI upload job now needs a test job that runs ruff, the issue registry and the full suite on the same resolved tag ref, and ci.yml runs on pushes to N.N.x maintenance branches. Reverting publish.yml turns tests/test_2611a2_w15.py::test_publish_uploads_only_after_the_suite_passes_on_the_same_commit red; reverting ci.yml turns ::test_a_push_to_a_maintenance_line_runs_ci red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) A deeply nested JSON body from the embedding backend escapes the client's failure boundary as `RecursionError`. `_parse_within_budget` parses with `response.json()` (`cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/embedding_client.py:581` and :606), which raises `RecursionError` for nesting about 10,000 deep, a body of roughly 20 KB and far under the 64 MiB response budget. `RecursionError` is not in the boundary tuples `(httpx.RequestError, httpx.HTTPStatusError, ValueError, KeyError)` at :406, :472 and :520, so it escapes `embed_with_outcome` and `capabilities_with_outcome`. Reproduced through the real client over a mock transport: a 20,015-byte body nested 10,000 deep made `do_store` raise and write nothing, while the same backend answering HTTP 500 stores the row without a vector. The recall, reconstruct, check_health and boot paths share the same unguarded calls (`cpersona/vector.py:1977`, and `generation.refresh` at `cpersona/server.py:3778`), confirmed by reading only. The trigger needs a buggy or hostile embedding backend.
issues.pattern: embedding response is nested deeper than the parser can follow
issues.fix_sketch: Catch `RecursionError` in `_parse_within_budget` and re-raise it as `EmbeddingResponseError` (a ValueError), or add it to the boundary's except tuples, so a pathological body becomes a failed EmbedOutcome; add a regression test next to the bug-424 one.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; the store path was reproduced, the other paths confirmed by reading. Same class as bug-424 (OverflowError at the same boundary). The defect lives in the vendored shared client, so the fix lands upstream first and is then resynced here.
issues.fix_note: Both response.json() calls in _parse_within_budget now go through _decode_json, which maps RecursionError to EmbeddingResponseError (a ValueError), so a deeply nested backend body becomes the documented failed EmbedOutcome for embed, capabilities and count_tokens, and store writes the row without a vector as it does on HTTP 500. The old anchor '^        return response\.json\(\)$' still matches (inside the new helper), so the entry needs the new pattern. Reverting the helper turns the six nested-body tests in tests/test_2611a1_u13.py red with RecursionError.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Integer arguments sent as JSON floats (for example `count: 3.0`) pass the tool's input-schema validation and are then silently replaced by the default. JSON Schema accepts 3.0 as an `integer`, but `validate_int` returns the default for anything that is not a Python int (`cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/validation.py:28-31`), and the registry passes every int parameter through it (`cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/mcp_utils.py:80`). Reproduced through the real `CallToolRequest` handler: schema validation is active (-5 and 2.5 are refused), yet `reconstruct(count=3.0)` returns `effective_count` 10 with no `count_policy`, `top_k=2.0` searches at the default depth, and `recall(limit=2.0)` returns 10 messages. The same applies to `budget`, `max_hops`, `max_evidence` and `pause_persistence`'s `ttl_seconds` (60.0 becomes the 1800 s default). This contradicts the count contract that a clamp is reported in `count_policy` rather than applied silently.
issues.pattern: if isinstance\(val, bool\) or not isinstance\(val, int\):
issues.fix_sketch: In `validate_int`, accept a float whose `is_integer()` is true and return `int(val)`, so the validator agrees with the JSON Schema `integer` it sits behind. Optionally report any value that is still replaced by a default instead of dropping it silently.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced through the MCP request handler. The defect lives in the vendored shared client, so the fix lands upstream first and is then re-vendored.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Under a per_subject ACL client, `reconstruct` in mode lite or pro reports `used_tokens` below the JSON the caller receives, and the response can exceed `cap`. The mode cap counts only the `envelope` passed in (`cpersona/server.py:618-619`, operating-context fields only), which `_shaped` merges before settling the count (`cpersona/reconstruct.py:1550-1554`). The ACL guard then adds `resolved_agent_id`, and `alias_issued` on first issuance, after the handler returns (`cpersona/acl.py:957-960`), outside anything the cap counted. Reproduced through the real request handler with a per_subject OAuth principal: `used_tokens` was 16-17 tokens below a recount of the returned JSON on every call, and pro responses reached 5,013-5,014 tokens against a cap of 5,000. This breaks the promise in docs/RELIABLE_RECALL_2_6.md:470 that the cap counts the JSON as the MCP layer sends it, tool boundary fields included. `tests/test_reconstruct_modes.py::test_the_cap_counts_what_the_tool_boundary_adds` covers only the operating-context fields.
issues.fix_sketch: Make the ACL echo part of the counted envelope, for example by having the guard publish the fields it will add (through a contextvar or argument) so `do_reconstruct_boundary` merges them before settling, or by re-fitting and re-settling a mode response after adding them. Extend the boundary test to the per-subject path.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced through the request handler with a per_subject client.
issues.fix_note: do_reconstruct_boundary merges acl.response_echo(), the resolved_agent_id/alias_issued fields the ACL guard publishes for the call in progress and applies after the handler returns, into the envelope reconstruct counts. used_tokens and the mode cap therefore include them. Reverting it (dropping **acl.response_echo(), or the guard's publication in acl._wrap) turns tests/test_2611a2_w13.py::test_used_tokens_counts_the_alias_echo and ::test_the_cap_holds_with_the_alias_echo_included red. The pattern matches exactly one line with grep -E and grep -P. The current open entry pins acl.py `result\["resolved_agent_id"\] = resolved_alias`, a line the fix removed, so verify-issues.sh now reports bug-513 STALE until the entry is updated.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Once the contiguous vector index is built, a row whose embedding is replaced in place keeps being scored by its old, build-time vector. `do_update_memory` writes the new text and a new non-NULL embedding under the same id in one UPDATE (`cpersona/admin_handlers.py:551-555`), and `check_health(fix=True)` can null and then re-embed rows within the same call (`cpersona/maintenance_handlers.py:168-173`). The index path's only in-place freshness probe asks whether an indexed row's embedding became NULL (`cpersona/vector.py:686`, SQL at `vector.py:770-786`), so the row is still scored from `index.embeddings` (`vector.py:1073`, `vector.py:1097`) while its new content is hydrated. Reproduced with `do_update_memory`: a query on the new wording scored the edited row 0.07 on the index path against 1.0 on the scan, and a query on the old wording returned it at 1.0 showing the new text; `check_vector_index` reported nothing. The coarse index's probe (`cpersona/coarse_search.py:340`) is the same NULL-only test, confirmed by reading. This contradicts the documented guarantee that the index changes latency, not answers (docs/operations.md:284). The divergence lasts until the index is rebuilt and only affects deployments that built an index; the stored rows are correct.
issues.pattern: changed, refusal = await vector_index\.changed_since_build\(db, index, table\)
issues.fix_sketch: Give the index read path a freshness signal for rows re-embedded in place, either a per-row embedding fingerprint or generation recorded at build time and compared by the probe, or have the in-place re-embed writers mark the id stale since the build, so the row falls back to the scan or is scored from its live blob. `check_vector_index` and `check_coarse_index` should report the same condition.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; the contiguous-index case was reproduced, the coarse-index case confirmed by reading. Extends bug-279 (which covers only the NULL case); related: bug-315, bug-011.
issues.fix_note: A change log kept by triggers (schema 20, VECTOR_LOG_SQL in cpersona/database.py) names every row the index files hold that changed since their build: an UPDATE that changes a column a file copies (embedding, agent_id, project_id, channel, created_at, and for records source and timestamp), an id change (both ids), and a DELETE. Each file records the log's generation, head and schema cookie at its build (contiguous format 3, coarse format 2); a read takes the ids logged since (vector_index.changed_since_build), leaves them out of the file's selection before the window limit, and reads them from the live table with the rows past the watermark, so the merge sees each as it is now. A log that was turned off, restarted, pruned past the file, behind the file, or changed by a schema change sends the read to the scan, and check_vector_index / check_coarse_index report it as vector_index_log_refused / coarse_index_log_refused. A build turns the log on before its first row and prunes what every file present holds; logging runs only while a file exists (vector_index.on_startup). The same log closes the re-tagging gap docs/CONTIGUOUS_INDEX_DESIGN.md section 7 used to accept, keeps a deleted row from sending the query to the scan (bug-588's fallback), and moves a record whose timestamp was rewritten to its new period in the coarse index. Reverting the exclusion turns tests/test_bug514_index_change_log.py::test_an_edited_memory_is_scored_by_its_new_vector red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) `delete_agent_data`'s index purge is not ordered against an in-flight block index build, so the build can put the purged agent's rows back on disk. `do_delete_agent_data` commits the delete and then unlinks the derived index files (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:838-841, `_purge_local_vector_index`, the bug-337 fix). `build_block_index` reads on its own snapshot connection with no write lock and publishes with an unconditional `os.replace` (cpersona/block_index.py:266-268). Reproduced 3 of 3 times on one event loop, the way the queue's build and a client delete share it: the delete answered ok:true and the purge removed the file. The build then published a file whose header still names the purged agent and which holds 200 of that agent's block rows, while SQLite holds none. Recall does not serve those rows, because the change-log filter drops records changed after `built_seq`. The residue stays in the data directory until the next build. The contiguous and coarse index builds (`os.replace` in cpersona/vector_index.py and cpersona/coarse_index.py) have the same ordering gap. That variant was not reproduced: `vector_index.build_index` aborts when its two passes count differently, so it publishes residue only when the delete lands after the embedding pass has started streaming.
issues.fix_sketch: Order the purge against builds. For example, keep a purge generation that a build checks before `os.replace`, discarding its output if a purge happened after its snapshot. Or take a build lock that delete_agent_data acquires before unlinking.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced for the block index; the contiguous/coarse variant was confirmed by reading only. Related: bug-337 (the purge this race undoes).
issues.fix_note: A purge that drops the index files first counts itself (vector_index.note_purge). Each of the three builds (contiguous, coarse, block) reads the count before it reads any row and checks vector_index.purged_since immediately before its os.replace, with no await between the check and the rename, so on the event loop the purge lands wholly before or after; a build overtaken by a purge discards its temp file and answers built:false instead of putting the purged agent back on disk. The block queue does not back off after such a discard. Removing the note_purge call (or making purged_since always false) turns test_a_block_index_build_does_not_republish_a_purged_agent and both test_a_vector_index_build_does_not_republish_a_purged_agent cases in tests/test_2611a1_u17.py red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) An unreadable calibration sidecar is overwritten without a backup outside the startup path, and deep_check recommends the call that does it. `_load_calibration_state` discards the unreadable flag from `_read_calibration_sidecar` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1339-1342), so `_stored_calibration_to_carry` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1215) carries nothing. `do_calibrate_threshold` then replaces the file through `_save_calibration_state` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1910-1923, `os.replace` at 1295). The bug-347 backup runs only in `ensure_calibrated_on_startup`, and only when that boot recalibrates (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2285-2290). `deep_calibration_staleness` reads through the same loader and reports a present but corrupt sidecar as `never_calibrated` with hint `run calibrate_threshold` (cpersona/checks.py:3899-3906). Reproduced: with the sidecar truncated by one byte and boot recalibration off (CALIBRATE_ON_MODEL_CHANGE=false, a documented setting), the boot was a noop and took no backup, although its WARNING says the file is copied aside. deep_check said never_calibrated. calibrate_threshold('a') then replaced the file, and agent b's threshold 0.42 and operator-set beta 2.0 were gone with no backup. Second variant, also reproduced: `_backup_calibration_sidecar` returns any existing backup for the same tag without copying (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1392-1401). Two different corrupt files on two boots therefore both reported the first backup, and the second file's bytes were kept nowhere.
issues.pattern: may_replace = not stored_unreadable or _backup_unreadable_calibration_sidecar\(\) is not None
issues.fix_sketch: Route the runtime save path through `_read_calibration_sidecar`. When the file exists but cannot be read, back it up under a tag that includes a content hash or timestamp, or refuse to persist. Make deep_calibration_staleness report a distinct 'unreadable' status without the calibrate_threshold hint.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Related: bug-347 (the startup-only backup), bug-246 (the backup dedup), bug-189 (the carry that works when the file is readable).
issues.fix_note: do_calibrate_threshold reads the sidecar through _read_calibration_sidecar and, when it is unreadable, copies it aside under a content-digest tag (_backup_unreadable_calibration_sidecar, also used by the startup path) before replacing it, refusing to persist when no copy can be made; deep_calibration_staleness reports status 'unreadable'. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u12.py::test_runtime_calibration_backs_up_an_unreadable_sidecar (and the refuses/both_kept/deep_check tests) red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) `CPERSONA_RECALL_MODE` and `CPERSONA_CALIBRATE_METHOD` are read raw, with no trim, case folding, membership check or warning (cpersona/config.py:962 and cpersona/config.py:864). The module's `_parse_choice` (cpersona/config.py:27-41) exists for this and is used by sibling settings such as RECALL_PRECISION (cpersona/config.py:911). RECALL_MODE is compared exactly with 'rrf' and 'rsf' (cpersona/builtin_providers.py:43,49), and anything else runs `_recall_cascade`. Reproduced: 'RSF' or 'rrf ' dispatched recall to the cascade instead of rsf or rrf, the fused-gate calibration signal became None, and nothing was logged. Because 'cascade' is a documented value, a typo cannot be told from an intended cascade. CALIBRATE_METHOD fills every calibration that omits `method` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1739), and the handler refuses values outside CALIBRATE_METHODS (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1756-1759). Reproduced: with 'Separation' or 'percentile ', the startup guard reported action 'initial' with global_ok false and calibrated no agent, and set_recall_precision failed with "Invalid method 'Separation'". Mis-casing is enough on its own. Whether a trailing space survives depends on the env loader.
issues.fix_sketch: Read both settings through `_parse_choice`: ('rrf', 'rsf', 'cascade') with default 'rrf', and CALIBRATE_METHODS with default 'separation'. A mis-cased value is then normalised, and an unknown one falls back to the default with a WARNING.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced for both settings. Same class as bug-321 and bug-371 (sibling settings moved to _parse_choice), and the contract stated in bug-133; related to bug-231 (the handler-side method check).
issues.fix_note: CPERSONA_RECALL_MODE and CPERSONA_CALIBRATE_METHOD are read through _parse_choice (trimmed, case-folded, an unknown value falls back to rrf / separation with a WARNING), and an out-of-range CPERSONA_CALIBRATE_PERCENTILE falls back to 0.95 with a WARNING. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_w02.py::test_recall_mode_is_trimmed_and_case_folded and ::test_mis_cased_calibrate_method_still_calibrates red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) calibrate_threshold turns a non-finite `z_factor` into 10 and persists a cosine threshold above 1.0. NaN is truthy, so it survives `z = z_factor or CALIBRATE_Z_FACTOR` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1738), and the bug-066 clamp `z = max(-10.0, min(10.0, z))` maps both NaN and Infinity to 10.0 (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1750). The zscore threshold `sim_mean + z_factor * sim_std` has a floor but no ceiling (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1108, 1116). Reproduced through the real CallToolRequest handler from raw JSON-RPC text: both NaN and Infinity were answered ok:true with z_factor 10.0 and new_threshold 1.1864. That value was persisted to the sidecar and installed for the agent, and recall for the same query fell from 10 rows to 1 (only the lexical match). A finite z=6 also persisted a threshold above 1.0 (1.0171) on the test corpus, so the missing ceiling holds apart from the NaN path. That corpus has a high null mean, so with real models a finite z must be larger to cross 1.0, but NaN and Infinity always map to the maximum. The response does show new_threshold above 1, and a recalibration recovers.
issues.fix_sketch: Reject non-finite z_factor and percentile values with math.isfinite before the `or` default and the clamp. Then refuse, or cap below 1.0, a computed cosine threshold above 1.0 instead of persisting it.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Related: bug-066 (the clamp whose stated purpose this violates).
issues.fix_note: do_calibrate_threshold refuses non-finite z_factor/percentile with math.isfinite before the `or` defaults and the clamp, and refuses a computed threshold above 1.0 before it is applied or persisted. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u12.py::test_a_zscore_threshold_above_one_is_refused_not_installed and test_non_finite_z_factor_is_refused[-inf] red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) set_recall_precision reports the new precision while the gate in force is still the one calibrated at the old beta, and persists that mismatched pair. When the fused-gate pass yields nothing, `do_calibrate_threshold` sets `fused_stats = None` and still answers ok:true (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1861-1879). The agent's gate is replaced only under `if fused_stats is not None:` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1880). `do_set_recall_precision` rolls back only when calibration is not ok or did not persist (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2079), so the sidecar write pairs the new beta with the old gate (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1910-1923). cpersona/vector.py:203-210 says the two must be restored together or they desync. Reproduced under the documented rsf mode: a healthy strict call moved the gate from 0.155 to 0.1904. With an embedding client whose embed raises (or the forced exception branch), the response said ok:true, precision strict, beta 2.0, and fused_gate null. The balanced gate 0.155 stayed in force, and the sidecar stored (beta 2.0, gate 0.155), so a restart restores the mismatch. Under the default rrf mode on that corpus both gates sat at the floor, so the mismatch was not visible there.
issues.pattern: if not cal\.get\("ok"\) or cal\.get\("persisted"\) is False:
issues.fix_sketch: When the fused gate is enabled and a signal applies but no gate was measured, treat it as a failure to apply in set_recall_precision. Roll the beta back, or drop the agent's stale gate so the heuristic is used, and never persist a beta beside a gate measured at a different beta.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. The fix needs a scoring decision on what a precision change without a measured gate should leave in force.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The calibration sidecar stores the width of whichever scope was calibrated last, but the startup guard compares it with the corpus-wide modal width. A mixed-width corpus can therefore recalibrate on every boot. Each `do_calibrate_threshold` call persists `embedding_dim = int(vecs.shape[1])` from its own sample (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1841, saved at 1910-1911), which is the agent's own rows for a per-agent call. `ensure_calibrated_on_startup` compares the stored value with `_corpus_embedding_dim()` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2210-2214, 1439-1448). Its loop calibrates global and then each agent (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2321-2333), so the last agent's width is stored. Reproduced: with agent a holding 30 rows at width 16 and agent z holding 20 rows at width 8, successive boots stored 8 against a corpus mode of 16. Every boot after the first reported dim_changed, logged 'Embedding dimension changed (8 -> 16)', backed up the sidecar and recalibrated every agent. This is the never-settling loop bug-344 was meant to close. Also reproduced: on a settled homogeneous corpus, one calibrate_threshold(agent_id='z') on a new-width agent flips the next boot to recalibrated. The per-agent carry also drops every stored entry on a width mismatch (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1179). A mixed-width corpus is a documented transient state during a model swap. With CALIBRATE_ON_MODEL_CHANGE=false nothing is restored at all. Memory data is not lost.
issues.fix_sketch: Persist the corpus-wide modal width (what `_corpus_embedding_dim()` returns, as the startup probe reads it) instead of the width of the calling agent's sample. Alternatively, store widths per agent and key both the restore check and the carry check on them, so a per-agent calibration cannot change the global staleness verdict.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Related: bug-344 (the probe-side fix this write side undoes); its regression tests seed a single agent and cannot see this variant.
issues.fix_note: do_calibrate_threshold fingerprints the sidecar (and the carry / refresh checks) with the corpus-wide modal width from _corpus_embedding_dim_on, the same query the startup guard runs, instead of its own sample's width; the response still reports the sample width. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_w02.py::test_mixed_width_corpus_settles_after_one_boot and ::test_calibrating_an_off_mode_agent_keeps_the_corpus_width_and_the_others red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) With two server processes on one database (a supported setup: each stdio client launches its own process against a shared CPERSONA_DB_PATH), the long-lived process reverts the other's acknowledged set_recall_precision. Every calibration write rebuilds the sidecar as carried values overlaid with this process's in-memory dicts, and the in-memory side wins: `agent_betas={**carried.get("agent_betas", {}), **dict(vector._agent_betas)}` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1922; thresholds at 1915 and fused gates at 1917-1920 the same way). A process that restored the sidecar at boot holds every agent's boot-time values, so when process B sets agent X to strict (sidecar beta 2.0, ok:true) and process A later calibrates or sets precision for an unrelated agent Y, A writes its stale X=0.5 back. After a restart X reads lenient and nothing reports it. The same overlay can write back stale thresholds and gates, a cleared override, or a purged agent's entries. No memory rows are affected.
issues.fix_sketch: Write only the entries this call changed (dirty-key tracking) over a fresh read of the sidecar, under a file lock or a compare-and-swap on calibrated_at or the file mtime. A process must not treat its boot-time snapshot as authoritative for keys it has not touched since.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced with two separate processes sharing one database. The bug-189 carry only fills keys absent from memory, so it does not cover this; the resurrection of a deleted agent's calibration is the bug-036 class.
issues.fix_note: Before each calibration write, do_calibrate_threshold re-reads the sidecar and _refresh_unchanged_calibration takes the stored value for every owned entry that is not pending (changed by this process since its last successful write), so a boot-time snapshot no longer reverts another process's set_recall_precision or resurrects a purged agent; pending marks clear on a successful write. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u12.py::test_a_value_another_process_changed_is_not_written_back red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) set_recall_precision accepts a non-finite beta. The standard JSON number 1e400 (and the literal Infinity) arrives as float inf, passes the schema and validate_float (cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/validation.py:53, which returns float(val) for any int or float), and passes the handler's only check `if beta and beta > 0:` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1997). In _separation_threshold the objective `tpr + beta * (1.0 - fpr)` (admin_handlers.py:914) is inf*0 = NaN at the candidate where fpr is 1, and np.argmax (915) returns that first NaN, so a request for maximum strictness installs the most permissive gate (the floor, 0.05, where strict gives about 0.65). The inf beta is persisted: json.dump writes Infinity into the calibration sidecar, json.load reads it back, so the loose gate survives a restart, and every later set_recall_precision or get_recall_precision response carries the bare token Infinity, which strict JSON parsers reject.
issues.fix_sketch: Reject a non-finite (and an absurdly large) beta in do_set_recall_precision with ok:false, and optionally declare a finite maximum in the tool schema. Making the shared validate_float refuse inf and NaN would also close it but touches every consumer of the vendored module.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced end to end through the MCP request handler. The non-JSON Infinity token in responses is the bug-300 class; a validate_float change would land in the vendored shared client upstream first.
issues.fix_note: do_set_recall_precision refuses a non-finite beta before resolving it, so beta=inf can no longer install the most lenient gate or put Infinity in responses and the sidecar, and NaN is no longer read as a clear. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u12.py::test_non_finite_beta_is_refused red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) set_recall_precision answers ok:true when the calibration sidecar could not be written. do_calibrate_threshold reports a failed write as `sidecar_persisted: false` with ok:true (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1911, 1927; _save_calibration_state returns False on OSError at 1297-1301), but the rollback condition tests only `ok` and the no-persist `persisted` key (2079), and the `calibrate` sub-object keeps only ok/scope/new_threshold/error (2117), so the persistence signal is dropped. With a full disk or a read-only sidecar directory the new beta stays live only in process memory, the caller sees success, and after a restart the old value comes back. That contradicts the tool description ('recalibrated at the new beta immediately and persisted', cpersona/server.py:2075-2076) and the handler's own invariant that the override never diverges from the unpersisted sidecar (2040-2044). A clear (precision='') is likewise reported as cleared:true while the stored override remains on disk. A later successful calibration in the same process before the restart would persist the beta, so the loss needs the restart to come first.
issues.pattern: if cal\.get\("ok"\) and cal\.get\("persisted"\) is not False and cal\.get\("sidecar_persisted"\) is False:
issues.fix_sketch: Treat `cal.get("sidecar_persisted") is False` as a failure to apply and roll back as on the other failure paths, or at minimum surface sidecar_persisted (or persisted:false) in the response and in the calibrate subset. Apply the same to the clear path.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced with the sidecar write failing at the OSError site. Related to bug-095 (which added sidecar_persisted) and bug-342.
issues.fix_note: do_set_recall_precision treats a calibration that reports sidecar_persisted:false as a failure to apply: it marks the result not ok with an explanatory error, so the existing rollback restores the previous beta (or the cleared override) and the call answers ok:false. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u12.py::test_set_precision_is_not_ok_when_the_sidecar_was_not_written red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Test gap: no test pins the EXPORT_DIR confinement against a sibling directory that merely shares the root's prefix. _confine_io_path accepts a path only when it equals the root or starts with root + os.sep (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2529), which is correct today, but the only confinement test uses a path plainly outside the root. Weakening the check to a bare `real.startswith(root)` lets export_memories write to <EXPORT_DIR>-old/x.jsonl and import_memories read from <EXPORT_DIR>2/any.jsonl, the bug-054 write and read escape, and every test that sets EXPORT_DIR still passes on that mutant.
issues.pattern: if real == root or real\.startswith\(root \+ os\.sep\):
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test that sets EXPORT_DIR=<tmp>/exports and asserts that export to <tmp>/exports-old/x.jsonl and import from <tmp>/exports2/any.jsonl are both rejected and that no file is created, with an inside-root control that succeeds.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced with a mutation: the bare-prefix variant wrote into the sibling directory and the suite stayed green. Pins the bug-054 and bug-130 confinement.
