Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_w02.py::test_malformed_forced_count_stays_unset, ::test_malformed_forced_budget_stays_unset and ::test_malformed_default_count_follows_a_lowered_maximum red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) `CPERSONA_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH` is parsed with no lower bound (cpersona/config.py:474), and the value is used directly as a slice bound. `check_oversized_content` (cpersona/checks.py:285-297) selects `length(content) > ?` with the cap and rewrites each unlocked row to `content[:MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH]` through `_rewrite_or_delete_on_collision` (checks.py:158-166), which deletes the row when the rewrite hits the content dedup UNIQUE index. With a cap of 0, `check_health(fix=true)` blanks the first row of each bucket and deletes the rest; in a full-registry run the empty-content check then deletes the blanked row too, so the agent's whole unlocked corpus is gone while the response reports `healthy`. With a small negative cap such as -3, every store silently loses its last characters (cpersona/utils.py:92-94) and each fix run shortens every row again, deleting rows that converge. Impact is narrower than it first appears: only the operator can set the value, a cap of 0 or a large negative value makes every store fail loudly with `empty after sanitization`, the dry run reports `degraded`, and the data loss needs an explicit `check_health(fix=true)`. `CPERSONA_MAX_PROFILE_LENGTH` (config.py:489) has the same unclamped shape. Reproduced on scratch databases.
issues.fix_sketch: Bound the cap at parse time (reject or clamp a non-positive `CPERSONA_MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH` and `CPERSONA_MAX_PROFILE_LENGTH` to at least 1, or define 0 as unlimited and handle it before any slice). Separately, make `check_oversized_content` refuse to rewrite when the cap is non-positive, so a bad value cannot reach the delete-on-collision path.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced; the reports claimed HIGH, and the severity was lowered because only the operator can set the value and the common bad values fail loudly first. Related to bug-127 (the shared rewrite-or-delete guard).
issues.fix_note: check_oversized_content (and check_oversized_profile) call config.require_positive_cap before reading. A cap below 1 therefore raises, the run reports check_crashed, and that check's savepoint is rolled back without rewriting or deleting a row. server.main refuses such a cap at startup (config.validate_content_caps), and the write-path sanitizers refuse it instead of slicing. If this guard line is reverted, tests/test_2611a1_u11.py::test_oversized_content_repair_refuses_a_non_positive_cap goes red. If the startup call is reverted, test_server_refuses_to_start_on_a_non_positive_cap goes red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Deleting a duplicate during maintenance silently destroys its declared associations instead of moving them to the surviving copy. check_duplicate_content(fix=True) keeps one survivor per (agent, project, content), preferring the channel '' row, and runs `DELETE {surplus}` over every other unlocked row (cpersona/checks.py:261-274) without considering associations. The associations_memories_ad trigger (cpersona/database.py:922-927) then removes every entity mention and every relation that names or is anchored on the deleted row, although the survivor holds byte-identical text. Reproduced on a fresh database: the same text stored in channel 'ops' and channel '', declarations anchored on the 'ops' row, then check_health(fix=true, checks=['duplicate_content']) kept the channel '' row and left 0 mentions and 0 relations; traverse no longer finds the relation and the response reports only `repairable: 1`. This contradicts the associative design's statement that retraction is the only way a declaration leaves the store. `_rewrite_or_delete_on_collision` (checks.py:157-166) deletes a colliding row with the same shape; that site was confirmed by reading only.
issues.fix_sketch: Before deleting the surplus rows, re-anchor their entity_mentions and relations to the group's survivor (INSERT OR IGNORE / UPDATE OR IGNORE), and do the same in `_rewrite_or_delete_on_collision`. Alternatively skip rows that carry declarations and report them, and report how many declarations a fix moved or removed.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced on a fresh database for the duplicate_content path. The survivor preference comes from bug-128.
issues.fix_note: Before check_duplicate_content's `DELETE {surplus}`, each surplus row that something declares about is mapped to its group's survivor using the same survivor rule. associations.repoint then moves its mentions to the survivor with INSERT OR IGNORE and re-points its relations in place with UPDATE OR IGNORE, so relation ids are kept. _rewrite_or_delete_on_collision does the same toward the row its rewritten text collided with. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u01.py::test_duplicate_content_repair_moves_declarations_to_the_survivor red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) One failed /capabilities request erases the learned backend fingerprint for the whole refresh interval. `generation.refresh()` caches every result, failures included, as `_learned = (now, learned)` with learned None (cpersona/generation.py:105), and serves it for REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS (300 s, generation.py:77-79). `block_keys()`/`node_keys()` then collapse to the legacy key (generation.py:135), so every block and node set stamped with the earlier fingerprint F reads as not current and is excluded from the block arm's read, with no degraded signal in the response. A block build in that window restamps records with the legacy key, which still reads as current after F is relearned, so model-swap detection on those rows is lost for good. Reproduced with the repo's own test helpers and fake client: after one failed ask the keys moved from (F, '') to ('', ''), the backend was not asked again within the interval, the F set read not current, the block arm examined nothing, and a build stamped ''. No stored content is lost and keyword/vector recall keep working.
issues.fix_sketch: On a failed or incomplete ask after a fingerprint was learned, keep the previous fingerprint (or accept it as an extra current key while identity is unknown) instead of caching None, and retry sooner than the full interval. Restamp with a different key only when the backend positively reports a different fingerprint.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Related to bug-461, which introduced fingerprint-keyed currency for nodes and blocks.
issues.fix_note: An ask that cannot name the backend after a fingerprint was learned keeps that fingerprint (and schedules a retry after RETRY_UNKNOWN_SECONDS) instead of caching None for the whole interval; only a reported fingerprint moves the key. Reverting makes tests/test_2611a2_w04.py::test_a_failed_ask_after_a_fingerprint_keeps_its_block_sets_current, ::test_an_incomplete_identity_after_a_fingerprint_keeps_the_keys and ::test_after_a_failed_ask_the_backend_is_asked_again_sooner fail.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) check_health(fix=True) re-embeds and writes NULL-embedding rows regardless of the `checks` subset, beyond the per-run cap, and without reporting it. The round-1 prefetch (cpersona/maintenance_handlers.py:87-89) and the bug-083 second pass (maintenance_handlers.py:168-173) are gated only on `fix` and an embedding client, never on checks_run, and the second pass calls `prefetch_null_embeddings`, which selects any NULL row up to REEMBED_ROW_CAP rather than only rows the locked run NULLed; the applied count of `apply_embedding_cache` is discarded. Reproduced with a fake embedding client: a run scoped to checks=['stale_pending_tasks'] sent 6 texts for 3 NULL rows and wrote embeddings on all 3 while returning issues []; and a null_embedding fix over 25 NULL rows with cap 10 reported re_embedded=10 and repairable=10 but embedded 20 rows. This breaks the tool contract that `checks` runs a subset (server.py:2380) and the per-run bound documented for CPERSONA_REEMBED_ROW_CAP (config.py:410-421). The writes are correct embeddings, so no data is damaged.
issues.pattern: reembed_tables = \[table for check, table in _NULL_EMBEDDING_TABLES if check in checks_run\]
issues.fix_sketch: Run the prefetch and the second pass only when null_embedding or null_episode_embedding is in checks_run, restrict the second pass to the rows the locked run NULLed or to what remains of the cap, and report its applied count in the null_embedding finding.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. The second pass was added by bug-083.
issues.fix_note: do_check_health embeds and writes NULL embeddings only for tables whose null-embedding check is in checks_run, limits the second pass to what the locked run left of REEMBED_ROW_CAP, and adds its writes to the finding's re_embedded. Reverting the gating turns tests/test_2611a2_w06.py::test_a_subset_fix_run_does_not_re_embed_unselected_null_rows red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Under check_health(fix=true) a single failed embedding probe is listed as an `embedding_backend_unreachable` warn in `issues`, but the verdict ignores it. severity_summary and status come from the residual fix=False re-run (cpersona/maintenance_handlers.py:199-203), which gets no embedding_cache; check_embedding_backend can then see unreachability only through a latched fault (cpersona/checks.py:686-690), and one failure does not latch (FAULT_PROMOTE_THRESHOLD = 2, cpersona/health.py:86), so the residual run reports not_probed at info. Reproduced with a fully embedded corpus and a failing embedding client: issues carried the warn while severity_summary had warn 0, status was healthy, and the checkup CLI exited 0 under --strict. A fresh checkup process starts with no latched fault, so the single-failure case is the normal one for scheduled checks; a long-running server whose recalls latched the fault does count it.
issues.fix_sketch: Pass the round-1 probe result (expected_dim and dim_probe_reached_backend) into the residual run, or carry the liveness findings from the locked run into severity_summary, so the verdict counts every warn the issues list carries.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. The residual split comes from bug-059 and bug-225, and this reopens the silence bug-274 removed; bug-500 concerns the same residual re-run.
issues.fix_note: The residual fix=False re-run that sets severity_summary/status is handed this run's probe result (expected_dim, dim_probe_reached_backend), so a single failed probe is counted as the warn the issues list carries. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_w06.py::test_a_backend_that_failed_this_runs_probe_degrades_the_fix_verdict red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) `deep_check(fix=true)` commits a repair that failed part way through and reports only an error. The fix-capable checks run inside one `transaction()` (cpersona/maintenance_handlers.py:355-357), but `_run` turns every exception from a check into `results[name] = {"error": ...}` (maintenance_handlers.py:328-334), so nothing escapes to the rollback in `transaction()` (cpersona/database.py:346-359) and the statements the check ran before it raised are committed. `deep_short_content` deletes in chunks of 500 (cpersona/checks.py:3819) and `deep_anonymous_source` (checks.py:3731) updates one row per statement, so both can be left half applied. Reproduced: with 600 short rows and a trigger that refuses a delete in the second chunk, the first 500 deletions were committed, the check's entry carried only an error with no `fixed` count, and the top-level `fixed` was true. This is the same class as bug-361, which `run_health_checks` closed with per-check savepoints (checks.py:3625-3631); the deep-check write seam has none. The realistic triggers are statement-level aborts (a trigger or constraint fault, an FTS delete-trigger error on a damaged index), and the rows removed are the repair the operator requested, so this is a broken rollback boundary and an under-reporting response rather than unrequested data loss.
issues.fix_sketch: Run each fix-capable deep check inside its own savepoint within the writing transaction, as `run_health_checks` does since bug-361, and roll back to it on exception. Report the error together with the fact that the check's writes were rolled back (or a partial `fixed` count if partial commit is kept deliberately), and do not report top-level `fixed: true` for a check that crashed.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Same defect class as bug-361 at the deep-check write seam introduced by the bug-324 split.
issues.fix_note: do_deep_check runs the fix-capable checks under an outer savepoint that is never released, plus one savepoint per check. On an exception it does ROLLBACK TO that check's savepoint and then RELEASE, which is the bug-361 pattern from run_health_checks, so a repair that raised part way is undone while the others commit. If this is reverted, tests/test_2611a1_u10.py::test_deep_check_rolls_back_a_repair_that_raised_part_way goes red (100 == 600 rows).

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) `migrate_channel_axis` moves memories to a new channel but leaves their declared entities, aliases and relations in the old one, splitting the association graph. Both UPDATEs (cpersona/maintenance_handlers.py:519-523 for recovered channels and :540-543 for the globalize path) rewrite only `memories.channel`; no statement or trigger retags `entities` or `relations`, which carry their own channel column, and association reads filter every table by channel through `isolation_where` (cpersona/isolation.py:102-104). Reproduced: a memory stored in channel `discord` with session_id `1234567:42:0` and an entity, alias and entity-to-memory relation declared in the same store call was migrated to channel `1234567`; afterwards a read in `1234567` found the memory but no entity (alias expansion returned nothing), and a read in `discord` still saw the entity but dropped its relation to the moved memory. No single channel-scoped read sees both halves, nothing reports the split, and the docstring (maintenance_handlers.py:422) calls the operation non-destructive. The memory rows themselves survive and stay recallable; what is lost is the alias expansion and relation walk for every migrated record.
issues.fix_sketch: In the same transaction, retag the entities, aliases and relations in the old channel that are anchored on or mentioned only by the migrated memories, using the same recovered channel (or '' on the globalize path), and decide how to handle entities shared by memories that land in different channels, for example by splitting them per channel. Add a health check that flags an association whose scope differs from the scope of its anchor.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. The same migration's treatment of locked rows is tracked separately as bug-664.
issues.fix_note: Inside the migration transaction, do_migrate_channel_axis records the 'discord' memories that something declares about before its UPDATEs and reads back which of them actually moved. It then calls associations.follow_rechannelled. That function moves each mention, and each relation anchored on (or naming) a moved memory, to the memory's new channel ('' on the globalize path). The 'discord' entities those name are carried into each landing channel with their aliases, so an entity whose records split is split per channel. Unanchored entity-entity relations are copied where both ends are visible. An original entity left with nothing is deleted, unless an alias could not follow. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u01.py::test_migration_takes_declarations_to_the_recovered_channel red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) `store` bounds content and refuses oversized source and metadata (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:207-214), but stores `id` (msg_id, :190), `channel`, `project_id` and `timestamp` (:199) verbatim with no length bound into the INSERT (:327-331); the store tool's schema declares no `maxLength` on any of them (for example cpersona/server.py:1099). Reproduced: a 9k-character metadata value was rejected, while 1 MB values for msg_id, channel, project_id and timestamp were all stored. msg_id and channel are also keys of the UNIQUE dedup indexes (cpersona/database.py:1068-1071), so the database plus WAL grows several MB per MB written. The read side is affected too: recall copies `timestamp` and `id` into every returned message (memory_handlers.py:2946-2949), and neither the preview tier nor the full-content budget counts them, so one write inflated a recall of four short rows to about 2 MB for every reader of that agent, against the rule that a write bound must not enlarge read budgets (bug-331). Reaching it needs a client with write access sending malformed or hostile input.
issues.fix_sketch: Add `maxLength` to the id, channel, project_id and timestamp schema properties and enforce the same caps in `do_store` with a `rejected` result, as is done for metadata. Also refuse a timestamp that does not parse as ISO-8601 instead of storing it verbatim.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Same family as bug-386 (session_key bounded at the schema) and bug-331 (read budgets charge every field); the empty-timestamp case is bug-666.
issues.fix_note: do_store refuses an id, channel or project_id longer than MAX_KEY_FIELD_LENGTH (256) and a timestamp longer than MAX_TIMESTAMP_LENGTH (64) with result 'rejected'. The store and archive_episode schemas publish the same bounds as maxLength. Reverting the handler checks turns tests/test_2611a2_w10.py::test_do_store_refuses_a_key_field_past_the_bound red. Reverting the schema turns ::test_an_oversized_field_is_refused_at_the_tool_boundary red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) A non-finite float (NaN or Infinity) inside source or metadata is accepted and stored as a bare `NaN`/`Infinity` token, which SQLite's `json_valid()` rejects, and `check_health(fix=true)` then blanks the whole column. Both write seams serialise with `json.dumps` and its default `allow_nan=True`: `do_store` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:198 and :200) and the import path (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2895 and :2897). The `invalid_json` repair (cpersona/checks.py:1851-1856) then sets `source = '{}'` and `metadata = '{}'` on every unlocked row that fails `json_valid`, erasing every other key and the producer attribution, so the row drops out of `source_id`-scoped recall. Reproduced through `import_memories` over a real stdio server (a JSONL line with `NaN` and `Infinity` imported with ok:true, then both columns became `{}` after the fix run) and through a library call to `do_store`. The `store` tool over the MCP transport is not affected: the SDK's receive loop re-serialises arguments in JSON mode, which turns NaN and Infinity into null before they reach `do_store`. The effect is limited to the caller's own rows, and a dry run does list the rows as repairable before the fix erases them.
issues.fix_sketch: Refuse non-finite floats at both write seams, or map them to null there (`json.dumps(allow_nan=False)` or a NaN-to-null pass in `do_store` and the import record writer, plus a `parse_constant` on the import's `json.loads`). Separately, make the `invalid_json` repair keep any object Python can still parse by re-encoding it with non-finite values as null, instead of blanking the whole column.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced on the import and library paths; the claimed path through the `store` tool over MCP did not reproduce, so the severity is MEDIUM rather than HIGH. The library-call seam is `do_store` in cpersona/memory_handlers.py:198-200.
issues.fix_note: The new utils.json_dumps_finite writes non-finite floats as null. It is used at both write seams: do_store for source and metadata (memory_handlers.py) and _import_memory_record for source and metadata (admin_handlers.py). check_invalid_json's repair now re-encodes each bad unlocked column through _reencode_json_object, keeping any object Python parses and writing '{}' otherwise, with a CASE json_valid guard. If reverted, test_import_writes_valid_json_for_non_finite_floats goes red for the import seam, test_store_writes_valid_json_for_non_finite_floats for store, and test_invalid_json_repair_keeps_an_object_python_can_parse for the repair.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) With CPERSONA_FTS_ENABLED=false, `_lexical_arms` returns two empty lists without calling `_search_memories_keyword` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:629-630), so under the default rrf mode and under rsf the keyword channel disappears entirely, including the LIKE fallback that docs/architecture.md describes for exactly the case where FTS cannot be used. Only cascade still reaches that fallback. Reproduced with FTS disabled and embeddings off: rrf and rsf returned nothing for a query whose exact substring is stored, at pool sizes 60 and 120, while calling `_search_memories_keyword` directly found the row through LIKE. With embeddings on, every lexical-only match is silently lost the same way.
issues.pattern: if FTS_ENABLED and \(not source_id or channel\):
issues.fix_sketch: When FTS is disabled, have `_lexical_arms` (and the keyword half of the cue arm) still call `_search_memories_keyword` so its LIKE fallback supplies the memory keyword list. Add a test that runs rrf and rsf with FTS off and expects the exact-substring row.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced.
issues.fix_note: _lexical_arms no longer returns early when FTS is disabled. Only the episode FTS search is gated on FTS_ENABLED, and the memory keyword search always runs, through its LIKE fallback when FTS is off. The cue arm's keyword half runs the same way. Reverting either site turns tests/test_2611a2_w11.py::test_fts_off_the_fusions_still_find_an_exact_substring (rrf, rsf), ::test_fts_off_the_lexical_arms_hand_the_like_rows_to_the_fusion or ::test_fts_off_the_cue_arms_keyword_half_still_runs red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) `exclude_contents` is applied to episode rows only when the vector or cue arm reaches them. The episode FTS loop in each fusion has no `_content_excluded` check (rrf at cpersona/memory_handlers.py:730-737, rsf at :872-877, cascade at :517-521), while the vector loops (:696, :847, :504) and the cue arm (:2164) do check. The episode branch of `_block_reserved_rows` (:1937-1941) also builds the row without the check that its memory branch applies at :1927, although its docstring (:1886-1887) says excluded content is excluded there too. Reproduced on a fresh database under the default rrf mode with embeddings off: excluding the exact content recall had returned for an archived episode still returned the episode, while the same exclusion removed a memory. `recall_with_context` then returns the caller's entry and the same episode twice.
issues.pattern: if episode is None or _content_excluded\(episode\["content"\], exclude_set\):
issues.fix_sketch: Apply `_content_excluded` to episode rows in all three episode FTS loops and in the episode branch of `_block_reserved_rows` before they take a vote or a seat. A single final exclusion pass over the fused results in `do_recall` would also cover future arms.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. Related: bug-454 (the block reservation's restriction ordering).
issues.fix_note: The episode FTS arms of rrf, rsf and cascade and the episode branch of the block reservation now apply _content_excluded, as the vector and cue arms already did. An excluded episode stays out whichever arm reaches it. The anchor is the block branch line. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_w11.py::test_the_block_reservation_excludes_an_excluded_episode red. Reverting the rrf, rsf or cascade site turns ::test_an_excluded_episode_stays_out_of_the_fusions, ::test_recall_with_context_does_not_return_an_episode_the_conversation_holds or ::test_cascade_gives_an_excluded_episodes_place_to_the_next_stage red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The cue arm merges its exact part (the period's first MAX_MEMORIES rows, read live) with the coarse remainder (index positions from MAX_MEMORIES on) without de-duplicating by id (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2095-2100). When a period row ahead of the boundary was deleted, retagged or re-timestamped since the index was built, the index positions run one ahead of the live table, so the live row at the boundary appears in both lists and receives two reciprocal-rank votes in the cue arm's fusion (:2167). Reproduced with six period rows, a cap of 3, a built coarse index and the newest row deleted: the boundary row was in both the exact part and the remainder and moved from third to first in the cue arm's output. This shifts the cue's lift and held seats and uses two depth places until the index is rebuilt.
issues.pattern: for hit in remainder if hit\.id not in capped_ids\],
issues.fix_sketch: De-duplicate by memory id when merging the exact part and the coarse remainder in `_search_cue_arm`, keeping the exact part's entry, or drop remainder hits whose id is already ranked, as the far seats do with their near-window ids.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. Same duplicate-vote class as bug-334, at a merge that has no overlap guard.
issues.fix_note: _search_cue_arm drops remainder hits whose id the capped exact part already ranked, keeping the exact part's entry, so a record both parts return is counted once. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_w11.py::test_a_store_between_the_cue_arms_two_reads_does_not_count_a_row_twice red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The documented empty-query 'recent memories' read orders by `created_at DESC` with no tie-break. `created_at` has one-second resolution, and the non-window branch of `_search_memories_keyword` uses `created_at DESC` alone (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:4078), as does the LIKE fallback (:4143); only the cue-window branch has a total order (`datetime(timestamp) DESC, id ASC`, bug-502). SQLite returns tied rows in ascending rowid order, so a batch stored within one second returns its earliest-stored rows. Reproduced with 12 rows pinned to one `created_at` second: an empty-query search with limit 3 returned ids [1, 2, 3] instead of the newest [12, 11, 10], and `do_recall('', 3)` returned the same three oldest rows with the oldest in the last-is-best slot. The existing test (tests/test_recall_cue.py:364-373) stores rows one second apart and so never creates a tie. Parallel tool calls and scripted batches routinely store several rows in one second.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a total-order tie-break on the non-window branch and on the LIKE fallback, such as `created_at DESC, id DESC`, so the most recently stored rows come first, and add a test that ties `created_at`.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. bug-502 fixed the ordering only on the cue-window branch.
issues.fix_note: The empty-query recent listing (no cue window) and the LIKE fallback now break created_at ties with id DESC, so a batch stored within one second returns its most recently stored rows first. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_w10.py::test_empty_query_listing_returns_the_newest_stored_rows_of_a_tied_second red (and the LIKE and do_recall tests in that module).

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The stdio proxy writes every response as text through `sys.stdout` (cpersona/proxy_stdio.py:283), so it is encoded with the platform's default stdout encoding rather than UTF-8. On Windows, with stdout a pipe and UTF-8 mode off (the default on the supported Python 3.11-3.13), that is the ANSI code page, while the remote server's results carry raw non-ASCII text (`json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False)` at cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/mcp_utils.py:201). Reproduced with stdout set to cp1252 (the strict encoding of such a pipe): a response containing Japanese text raised UnicodeEncodeError, the writer's guard (cpersona/proxy_stdio.py:125-132) logged and dropped it, and only the following plain response was written, so the client waits on that request until its timeout. The stdin side of the same proxy already reads raw bytes, and the MCP SDK's own stdio server wraps the stdout buffer as UTF-8.
issues.fix_sketch: Write responses as UTF-8 bytes to `sys.stdout.buffer`, or wrap the buffer once in a UTF-8 `TextIOWrapper` in `main()`, mirroring the stdin side and the SDK's stdio server.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Reproduced on macOS with the Windows pipe encoding simulated through PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252.
issues.fix_note: _write_stdout encodes each JSON-RPC message as UTF-8 and writes it to sys.stdout.buffer, so the console code page (cp1252/cp932 on a Windows pipe) no longer drops or mis-encodes non-ASCII responses. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a1_u14.py::test_the_proxy_writes_utf8_whatever_the_console_encoding[cp1252] and [cp932] red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) reconstruct assumes a candidate's `source.id` and `source.type` are strings, but the write path does not guarantee it. `_Candidate.__init__` calls `.strip()` on `source["id"]` (cpersona/reconstruct.py:310) and takes `source["type"]` as is (:311); the adjacency pass then sorts keys that start with that type (:566-568). The legacy `message` store form accepts an untyped source object (cpersona/server.py:1093), and `normalize_source` (cpersona/utils.py:511) folds the ClotoCore serde shape `{"User": {"id": 42}}` into an integer id. Reproduced on fresh databases: a row stored with source `{type: 'User', id: 12345}` or the serde shape makes `do_reconstruct` raise AttributeError ('int' object has no attribute 'strip'), and two rows sharing a source id where one has type null raise TypeError in the sort, while recall returns the same rows without error. Every reconstruct whose candidate pool contains such a row fails, including the empty-query session-start call.
issues.fix_sketch: Coerce source id and type to str when building `_Candidate` (str(v) when v is not None), and normalise or validate `source.id` and `source.type` as strings at the store seam (`normalize_source` and the serde fold) so stored rows hold strings.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Related: bug-035.
issues.fix_note: _Candidate reads source id and type through _source_field, which returns '' for absent/null and str(value) otherwise, so an integer id no longer hits .strip() and a null or integer type no longer breaks the adjacency sort. Reverting turns test_reconstruct_answers_for_rows_with_non_string_source_fields (4 cases) and test_candidate_source_fields_are_strings red with AttributeError/TypeError.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Raw-span expands handed back by reconstruct carry no `revision`, so get_contents serves a rewritten record's text under the old offsets. The severed-passage path of `_filled_quote` sets `quote["expand"] = {"ref": claim.ref, "span": [start, end]}` (cpersona/reconstruct.py:1185), and the start path (:1177) and `sequence_quote` (:1466) do the same; only the block expands (:1066, :1111) attach a revision. get_contents checks a revision only when one is given (memory_handlers.py `_resolve_range`), while docs/BLOCK_REACH_DESIGN.md section 5 and the `blocks.text_revision` docstring say a span handed back carries one so a rewritten record is refused. Reproduced: a 1,475-character record with no sentence end was quoted severed with expand {ref, span:[0,1475]} and no revision; after update_memory replaced the text, get_contents returned characters of the new text with no `unresolved` or stale-revision refusal. This happens on the default configuration with blocks on as well.
issues.fix_sketch: Attach `"revision": blocks.text_revision(text)` to every raw-span expand in reconstruct (the `_filled_quote` start and severed paths and `sequence_quote`), and add a test that rewrites the record and asserts get_contents refuses the stale span.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced with a store, reconstruct, update_memory, get_contents sequence. Related: bug-466.
issues.fix_note: _span_expand builds every raw-span expand reconstruct returns (filled head quote start/severed, sequence_quote) with the revision of the text its offsets were measured in, so get_contents refuses a rewritten record as stale_revision. Without it, tests/test_2611a2_w12.py::test_every_raw_span_quote_helper_attaches_the_revision and the *_expand_is_refused_after_rewrite tests turn red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Under mode lite or pro, one stored record can block the event loop for tens of seconds. Every mode call builds the whole sequence (cpersona/reconstruct.py:1532), and its per-record work is superlinear in the number of blocks: `record_passages` checks each block against every governed range with no limit (:1305-1309), and `sequence_costs` (:1413) and `cut_sequence` (:1392) re-sort and re-join the record's whole `before` list at every step. `blocks.segment` cuts at every full-width terminator, so a keyword followed by N copies of the ideographic full stop yields N one-character blocks while staying under the 16,000-character content cap. Reproduced: reconstruct took 0.63 s at N=2,000, 5.4 s at 8,000 and 21 s at 15,900 under lite, 9.4 s at 8,000 under pro, and over 60 s at 15,900 under pro; a ticker on the same loop saw gaps equal to the whole call, so other requests stall. A record of the same length in ordinary sentences takes 0.08 s.
issues.fix_sketch: Bound the work per record: cap the passages `record_passages` considers to what can fill the budget, and track each record's quoted length incrementally instead of re-sorting and re-joining `before` at every step. Merging tiny adjacent blocks at segmentation, or running the sequence off the event loop, would also help.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced with timed reconstruct calls on fresh databases. Related: bug-705.
issues.fix_note: There are two fixes. record_passages now checks a block's range for overlap with one bisect over the sorted ranges already taken, instead of scanning all of them. The ranges do not overlap, so their ends are sorted too. The new _step_costs generator gives each step's cost in constant time by tracking each record's joined runs by their start and end. cut_sequence and sequence_costs both use it, and cut_sequence stops at the budget. Before, the record's whole quote was sorted and re-joined at every step, and the pro cap search repeated that for each budget it tried. Reverting the cost change turns test_the_sequence_costs_and_cut_grow_near_linearly_with_the_passages and test_one_long_record_does_not_hold_the_event_loop[lite/pro] red. Reverting the bisect turns test_record_passages_grows_near_linearly_with_the_blocks red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Under mode lite or pro, held (reserved) items with short records are placed ahead of window items in the budget and can push a window item out. Modes force the whole sequence, and the whole-record floor flag is set for every record, held ones included: `basis == "whole" and i < floor_items` (cpersona/reconstruct.py:1809, with `floor_items` = all records under lite and 10 under pro at :1807). `whole_order` then puts every short record ahead of all other passages (:1366). The comments at :1693 and :1905 say held items come last and are cut first, and docs/RELIABLE_RECALL_2_6.md section 7 says they displace no item of the window. Reproduced end to end: with five long records passing the gate and one short record admitted only through the keyword seat every mode requests, reconstruct(count=3, mode='lite') returned one window item plus the held record instead of two window items, with shortfall_reason budget_exhausted.
issues.pattern: basis == "whole" and i < floor_items for i
issues.fix_sketch: Restrict the whole-record floor to window positions, or order held items' passages after every window passage, so held items sit at the end of the cut sequence as the contract says. Add the two-arm comparison (with and without the held row) as a regression test.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced end to end without patching the candidate list. Related: bug-464, bug-708.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) reconstruct `max_evidence` has no upper bound. The schema gives it only `minimum: 1` (cpersona/server.py:1737-1741), and cpersona/reconstruct.py:1545 applies only `max(1, int(max_evidence))`, unlike `max_hops`, which is clamped at :1543 (bug-459). The value becomes the relation walk's per-entity fetch limit (:1701, reading `per_entity + 1` full rows per reached entity in associations.py), the number of claims each item keeps, and the driver of `structure()`'s `_roles_for` pass, which scans all claims per claim. Claims are not counted by the character budget. Reproduced with a seed record linked to a hub entity mentioned by N records: with the default the call returns 40 claims in about 0.01 s; with max_evidence=1e6 it returned N+1 claims and 205 KB at N=2,000 and 496 KB in 1.1 s at N=5,000 (the `_roles_for` time grew about 11x for 2.5x rows), synchronously on the event loop; mode lite turned the same call into `cap_below_minimum` after 3.5 s; and 2**63 escaped as an uncaught OverflowError from SQLite.
issues.fix_sketch: Give `max_evidence` a ceiling as bug-459 did for `max_hops`: a schema maximum plus `min(..., ceiling)` at reconstruct.py:1545, reported as a lowered bound in `bounds`. `TRAVERSE_MAX_LIMIT` fits, since the walk's per-entity read is the read traverse already caps, and it keeps `per_entity + 1` inside the SQLite integer range.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced on fresh databases through the server boundary. Sibling of bug-459.
issues.fix_note: do_reconstruct lowers max_evidence to traverse's per-entity ceiling (associations.TRAVERSE_MAX_LIMIT = 100), because the walk's per-entity read is the same read traverse caps. The lowered value is reported in bounds.max_evidence, and bound_lowered keeps bounds in the compact response. The reconstruct schema now states maximum = TRAVERSE_MAX_LIMIT (server.py). Reverting the clamp turns test_max_evidence_shares_traverse_s_per_entity_ceiling, test_a_lowered_evidence_bound_is_reported_even_when_nothing_else_is and test_a_max_evidence_past_the_sqlite_integer_range_is_served red. Removing the schema maximum turns test_the_schema_states_the_evidence_ceiling red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Under `mode` (lite / pro), reconstruct refuses with `cap_below_minimum` whenever the shaped JSON of the smallest quoted-text prefix exceeds the token cap (cpersona/reconstruct.py:1934-1956), and the detail always blames the first passage. That JSON also carries the first item's claims list, which is bounded by `max_evidence` (reconstruct.py:1545, 1719) and not by the cap, so the cap search cannot trim it. The documented condition is only 'a cap the first passage alone exceeds' (docs/RELIABLE_RECALL_2_6.md:475). Reproduced: a 100-turn burst from one source 0.5 s apart bundles into one item whose head passage is 94 characters, yet `mode='lite'` with `top_k=100, max_evidence=100` returns no items and `cap_below_minimum` naming the first passage; the same call with `max_evidence=5` answers in 459 tokens. A caller who raises `top_k` as the tool description advises gets an error with a false cause.
issues.pattern: attempt, attempt_quoted = assemble\(ends\[0\], \{i: middle for i in first\}\)
issues.fix_sketch: Make the claims list (and any droppable per-session notices) part of what the mode cap may trim, for example by reducing retained claims and marking `claims_omitted` before refusing. Refuse only when the head passage alone exceeds the cap, and state the actual cause in the detail.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. The same exit also drops forwarded notices, filed as bug-709.
issues.fix_note: When no prefix fits a mode's cap, the items of the first step are rebuilt with the largest evidence bound whose response fits (cut stated in claims_omitted) instead of refusing; cap_below_minimum remains only when the first passage with its head claim and fields is over, with a detail naming the real cause. Without it, tests/test_2611a2_w12.py::test_a_mode_trims_the_claims_rather_than_refusing, ::test_a_mode_keeps_as_many_claims_as_fit and ::test_a_refusal_names_what_did_not_fit turn red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The check_health description says 'Nothing contacts the embedding backend unless fix=true' (cpersona/server.py:2375), and docs/operations.md:103-104 says '`check_health(fix=false)` makes no network call'. Both are false. A report-only run calls `generation.refresh()` (GET /capabilities in http mode) whenever embedding_model is selected, before and regardless of `if fix:` (cpersona/maintenance_handlers.py:83-84); leaves `embedding_cache` as None, so `check_embedding_dimension` sends a live `embed(["test"])` (cpersona/checks.py:454); and the missing_nodes live scan posts un-noded record text to /count_tokens. Reproduced: a check_health(fix=False) run sent POST /embed ['test'] and POST /count_tokens with record text, then reported `embedding_backend` as `not_probed` with a hint that liveness was not tested, although a probe was sent and its result discarded. get_session_findings uses the same fix=False path. During an outage the 'network-free' diagnostic can block up to the client timeout (default 30 s) per request.
issues.pattern: Only fix=true judges the backend's liveness: a report-only
issues.fix_sketch: Either correct the tool description, operations.md and the SKILL text to say a report-only run contacts the backend (capabilities, a dimension probe, a token report), or make fix=False truly offline by skipping the refresh, the dimension embed and the missing_nodes live scan. If the probe stays, use its outcome for the liveness finding instead of reporting not_probed.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced with a recording backend. Related: bug-428, whose fix note restates the premise that a report-only run does not reach the network.
issues.fix_note: The check_health description (and operations.md/.ja.md, the skill and its repair reference) now say a report-only run can contact the backend but does not read it as liveness. Restoring the old 'Nothing contacts the embedding backend unless fix=true' sentence turns tests/test_2611a2_w06.py::test_a_report_only_run_contacts_the_backend_and_the_docs_say_so red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) A source checkout made with `core.autocrlf=true`, which is Git for Windows' default, corrupts the shipped tokenizer vocabulary, and then every `reconstruct` call with `mode` lite or pro fails. The repository has no `.gitattributes`, so git detects `cpersona/vocab/cl100k_base.tiktoken` as text and rewrites its 100256 line endings to CRLF. `tokens._load` hashes the raw bytes and raises `VocabularyError` on a digest mismatch (cpersona/tokens.py:52-53), and no caller catches it. A probe reproduced this: a store followed by `reconstruct(mode='lite')` raised `VocabularyError` on the CRLF checkout and succeeded on the LF control. The source install (git clone plus pip install) is documented, including the Windows activation line (getting-started.md). PyPI and uvx wheels are built from LF bytes and are unaffected, and calls without a `mode` keep working.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a `.gitattributes` that marks `cpersona/vocab/*.tiktoken` as binary (or `-text`), so git never converts it. Optionally, normalize CRLF to LF in `tokens._load` before hashing, so an already-converted checkout still loads.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced with an `autocrlf=true` clone of the committed vocabulary bytes.
issues.fix_note: tokens._load normalises CRLF to LF before the SHA-256 check (base64 tokens and ranks cannot contain a carriage return, so any other alteration still fails), and a new .gitattributes marks cpersona/vocab/*.tiktoken -text so git never converts it on checkout. Reverting the normalisation turns tests/test_2611a1_u14.py::test_a_crlf_checkout_of_the_vocabulary_still_loads_and_counts red (VocabularyError); removing the .gitattributes line turns test_git_never_converts_the_vocabulary_line_endings red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) uvx detection misses the default Windows uv cache and any custom `UV_CACHE_DIR`, so a uvx process is classified as a pip install. `detect_install` recognizes uvx only when `sys.prefix` contains the segment `uv/archive-v0` (cpersona/update_check.py:761). A uvx environment's prefix is actually `<cache root>/archive-v0/<hash>`. The Windows default root is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\uv\cache`, so the prefix contains `uv\cache\archive-v0` and never matches, and any cache root whose last component is not `uv` misses on every OS. The inline comment's claim that the segment match survives `UV_CACHE_DIR` is false. Such a process falls through to the site-packages branch and gets `METHOD_PIP`. The update notice and the check_health hint then give a pip / `uv pip install --upgrade` command. A probe reproduced this: `check_update(apply=true)` ran that upgrade against the cached uvx environment and reported `applied=True`, which is the case the `apply` docstring says must be refused. The upgraded environment is discarded on the next launch. The only tests use the `~/.cache/uv/archive-v0` layout (tests/test_update_check.py:110, :585).
issues.fix_sketch: Detect uvx by an `archive-v0` parent directory of `sys.prefix`, and optionally check it against the resolved uv cache dir. Add tests for the Windows default layout and for a custom `UV_CACHE_DIR`.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced against measured uvx prefix layouts, with the install step stubbed.
issues.fix_note: detect_install now asks _launched_by_uvx(sys.prefix), which splits the prefix on both / and \ and requires the parent directory to be archive-v0, so the Windows default %LOCALAPPDATA%\uv\cache and any UV_CACHE_DIR are detected as uvx and apply refuses. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_w15.py::test_uvx_is_detected_under_any_cache_root and ::test_apply_runs_nothing_under_a_uvx_launch red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) `_parse_timestamp_utc` lets OverflowError escape for a well-formed stamp at the edge of the datetime range that carries an offset. It returns `dt.astimezone(timezone.utc)` (cpersona/utils.py:169) and catches only `(ValueError, OSError)` (cpersona/utils.py:170); for '0001-01-01T00:00:00+01:00' or '9999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00' the conversion leaves the representable range and raises OverflowError, an ArithmeticError. Reproduced from a fresh database: store raises instead of answering `result` (through `future_timestamp_issue`, cpersona/memory_handlers.py:243), and reaches the client as a bare error; archive_episode loses the whole episode (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:4303); recall_with_context aborts on one such `external_context` entry (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:3328); and import_memories rolls back an entire restore because of one memory stamp (the check runs after the insert, cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2955). Episode start/end are imported verbatim, and a stored episode with such a span makes check_health report `check_crashed` for `episode_timestamp_format_drift`, because the drift checks call `astimezone` outside their try (cpersona/checks.py:2112, 2180), so the repair path is lost too. The `cue.sql_instant` window conversion has the same unguarded call (cpersona/cue.py:257). A reconstruct failure on such an episode was claimed but did not reproduce in the probe configuration.
issues.fix_sketch: Catch OverflowError (or ArithmeticError) in `_parse_timestamp_utc` so these stamps read as unparseable, as cue.py's parse already does, and apply the same guard to the `astimezone` calls in the timestamp_format_drift and episode_timestamp_format_drift checks and in `cue.sql_instant`.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Reproduced. Same class as bug-443, which was fixed only inside cue.py; related to bug-291 and bug-299.
issues.fix_note: _parse_timestamp_utc catches OverflowError so a stamp whose offset carries its UTC instant out of range reads as unparseable; both timestamp-format-drift checks move astimezone inside their try and skip such a value; cue.sql_instant clips an overflowing bound to the end it passed. Reverting turns the store, archive_episode, recall_with_context, import, drift-check and cue tests in tests/test_2611a1_u13.py red with OverflowError: date value out of range.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The store-time future-timestamp gate and the SQL health checks parse timestamps differently, so reject mode is bypassed and a literal 'now' is stored permanently. `future_timestamp_issue` reads the stamp with Python `fromisoformat` and answers None for anything it cannot parse (cpersona/utils.py:194-196), deferring to `invalid_timestamp`; but `invalid_timestamp` uses SQLite `datetime()` (cpersona/checks.py:1871), which accepts Julian-day numbers, 'now' and out-of-range dates such as Feb 30. Reproduced with `CPERSONA_FUTURE_TIMESTAMP_MODE=reject`: the ISO spelling of an instant 73 years ahead was rejected, while '2500000' (2132 to SQLite) and '2099-02-30T00:00:00+00:00' were stored; the future_timestamp check later finds and repairs those two, so for them the damage is the bypassed reject contract. A literal 'now' was also stored, is flagged by neither `invalid_timestamp` nor `future_timestamp`, survives `check_health(fix=true)` as an unfixable naive drift row, and becomes the scope's raw MAX(timestamp). Python cannot parse it, so the confidence span read (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:1620-1622) is dropped for the whole scope, the bug-237 effect by another route. The span damage matters only with confidence scoring or a nonzero prior age rate.
issues.fix_sketch: Give the write gate and the SQL checks one parse definition: refuse at store any stamp `_parse_timestamp_utc` cannot read, or make `invalid_timestamp` flag rows Python cannot parse and not only rows SQLite cannot, and have the span read skip ends that are not ISO.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Reproduced. Related: bug-237.
issues.fix_note: future_timestamp_issue now judges a stamp that _parse_timestamp_utc declines but SQLite's date functions read ('2500000', 'now', 30 February, a lower-case 'z') with SQLite's own reading and the exact strftime predicate check_future_timestamp evaluates against future_timestamp_boundary. reject refuses such a stamp when it is ahead, warn reports it, and a restore counts it. check_invalid_timestamp also claims SQL-only stamps that are not ahead and repairs them to created_at; scope_stats.get_span skips ends its caller cannot parse. Reverting the anchored line turns tests/test_2611a2_w14.py::test_reject_refuses_a_stamp_only_sqlite_reads_as_ahead, ::test_the_verdict_reads_a_stamp_only_sqlite_reads_the_way_sqlite_does, ::test_the_seam_and_the_health_check_name_the_same_rows, ::test_warn_reports_a_stamp_only_sqlite_reads_as_ahead and ::test_a_restore_counts_a_stamp_only_sqlite_reads_as_ahead red. The invalid_timestamp and span halves are pinned by ::test_invalid_timestamp_finds_and_repairs_a_stamp_only_sqlite_reads and ::test_the_span_skips_an_end_the_caller_cannot_parse.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The bug-315 fix is incomplete: a row deleted after the contiguous index was built still takes one of the window's positions when it is not a survivor, so the index path silently drops the live row at the window edge. `_index_phase1` selects `limit=scan_offset + scan_limit` positions from the index file, deleted ids included (cpersona/vector.py:661-668). The only deletion fallback compares hydrated rows with survivors (`if from_index and len(payload) < len(survivors):`, cpersona/vector.py:1588), and the lost-embedding probe asks `embedding IS NULL` (cpersona/vector.py:770-786), which a deleted row cannot satisfy; a deleted row below the threshold or outside the top cut triggers neither. Reproduced with 4 rows, a 3-row window and a built index: deleting the newest row (unrelated to the query) moved row 1 (cosine 1.0) into the scan's window, the scan returned it, and the index path returned nothing. With k deletions the k oldest window rows are missing from every recall until a rebuild. The episode path has the same shape (cpersona/vector.py:1762). The check_vector_index hint says the index hands each query back to the scan (cpersona/checks.py:2849-2852), and docs/CONTIGUOUS_INDEX_DESIGN.md:188-189 says the hydrate fails closed on a deleted row; neither holds for these queries. It needs a corpus larger than `CPERSONA_MAX_MEMORIES` with an operator-built index.
issues.fix_sketch: In `_index_phase1`, detect selected index ids that no longer exist (extend the lost-embedding probe to count existing rows, not only NULL embeddings) and fall back to the scan when the counts differ; apply the same to the episode path and correct the check_vector_index hint and the design doc.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Reproduced. Completes bug-315; the same window-shortening concern is the reason bug-279's fix rejected filtering lost embeddings.
issues.fix_note: _index_phase1 now counts, after the lost-embedding probe, how many selected index ids still exist (on the agent's (agent_id, created_at) index bounded by the oldest selected created_at, range form for a contiguous id run, json_each form otherwise) and falls back to the scan when the count differs; this covers memories and episodes since both go through _index_phase1. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a1_u05.py::test_a_deleted_window_row_does_not_push_the_edge_row_out (and the scattered and episode variants) red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The index builders read the row plan (`plan_rows`, meta query at `cpersona/vector_index.py:213`) and the embedding blobs (`_stream_embeddings` / `iter_embedding_chunks`, `cpersona/vector_index.py:369`) as two separate autocommit statements on the shared read connection, which the CLI uses (`cpersona/vector_index.py:735-736`). They do not share a snapshot, contrary to the docstring at `cpersona/vector_index.py:316-321`. The only guard is the row count (`if written != count`, :370). A count-neutral pair of commits between the passes, such as deleting one planned row and filling the embedding of a row that was NULL at plan time, passes that check, and the file is written with the vectors between the two positions shifted one slot against their ids. Reproduced: rows 1-6 with row 5 NULL, a concurrent DELETE of id 2 plus a fill of id 5 gave `built: True, count: 5` with ids 4 and 3 holding the vectors of ids 5 and 4. Index-path recall then ranks those rows by their neighbours' vectors, silently, until the next rebuild. `build_coarse_index` has the same shape (`cpersona/coarse_index.py:143` then :197-201). The documented cron build against a live server is the trigger setting.
issues.fix_sketch: Run both passes inside one pinned snapshot, for example by building under `database.read_snapshot()` (a BEGIN on a private connection) for both the contiguous and coarse builders. Alternatively, have the blob pass also select the id and check it against the planned order.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. The bug-315 survivor check and the lost-embedding probe do not detect this shift.
issues.fix_note: The blob pass shared by both builders (iter_embedding_chunks) now selects each row's id and checks it against the metadata pass's ids in order, raising IndexUnusable on any difference, so neither builder can publish vectors or sign bits shifted against their ids whatever connection it is given. The operator CLI also builds both files inside database.read_snapshot(), so a build against a live server succeeds from one snapshot. Reverting the id check turns tests/test_2611a1_u05.py::test_a_build_never_pairs_an_id_with_another_rows_vector and ::test_a_coarse_build_never_pairs_an_id_with_another_rows_bits red; reverting the snapshot turns ::test_the_operator_build_reads_one_snapshot_while_a_server_writes red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Under reconstruct `mode` lite or pro, a record reached only through a declared alias can become an item, which the documented contract says cannot happen. reconstruct passes the alias cue terms into the lexical arms and, under a mode, asks for a keyword seat (`cpersona/reconstruct.py:1559-1569`). The keyword-seat eligibility filter (`cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2798-2802`) admits any `_lexical_only` row whose gate score is rrf, without distinguishing rows that are lexical-only because of the alias terms, and the seated row becomes a held item with admission `reservation`. This contradicts `docs/behavior-contracts.md:340-343` (an alias-only record 'stays below the gate exactly as it would without the alias'), ASSOCIATIVE_MEMORY_DESIGN section 9, and the tool description (`cpersona/server.py:1695`, associations add evidence 'inside items, never items'). Reproduced: a target sharing no word with the query was not an item with no mode, or under lite without the alias, but was returned as a reservation item under lite with the alias declared. The admitted record names the declared entity, so the harm is a broken documented contract rather than unrelated results.
issues.pattern: An alias adds a keyword vote
issues.fix_sketch: Decide the contract: either exclude rows whose only lexical match came from alias cue terms from keyword-seat eligibility, or amend behavior-contracts section 11, ASSOCIATIVE_MEMORY_DESIGN section 9 and the tool description to say an alias-only match can take the keyword seat under a mode. Pin the chosen behavior with a test.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. The fix needs a contract decision before code or docs change.
issues.fix_note: Contract follows the code (maintainer decision): an alias is a keyword vote, gated like any other keyword match, so a record found only through it comes back when the match clears the gate (under rsf a lone keyword match can) and can take a mode's keyword seat. behavior-contracts section 11, ASSOCIATIVE_MEMORY_DESIGN invariant 3 and section 9, the keyword-seat policy in RELIABLE_RECALL_2_6 and the bundled skill say so, in English and Japanese. issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The test suite is hermetic only when the shell has no CPersona settings. tests/conftest.py:28-29 pin the database and embedding mode with `os.environ.setdefault("CPERSONA_DB_PATH", ...)` and `os.environ.setdefault("CPERSONA_EMBEDDING_MODE", "none")` (and CPERSONA_OPERATING_CONTEXT at :33 the same way), so an inherited value wins. cpersona/config.py:67 then binds DB_PATH to that file, and fixtures in 67 test modules run unscoped `DELETE FROM memories` (for example tests/test_bug439_quick_check_stale_fts_cache.py:59-66), irreversibly wiping every agent's memories in a real store and writing test rows into it; an inherited `CPERSONA_EMBEDDING_MODE=http` likewise reaches the suite. This breaks the conftest docstring (lines 8-12) and CONTRIBUTING.md:39-40, which call the suite hermetic. Reproduced on scratch databases with a control: a sentinel row survived a run with the variable unset and was deleted when CPERSONA_DB_PATH pointed at it; a scratch conftest that assigns instead of calling setdefault passed. The trigger needs CPERSONA_DB_PATH exported in the shell that runs pytest; MCP client configs normally set it only for the server process, but docs/operations.md and SUPPORT.md give shell commands that read `$CPERSONA_DB_PATH`, which encourages exporting it.
issues.fix_sketch: Overwrite CPERSONA_DB_PATH, CPERSONA_EMBEDDING_MODE and CPERSONA_OPERATING_CONTEXT with hermetic values before cpersona is imported instead of calling setdefault, and route any deliberate override through a separate test-only variable. A session guard could also abort the run if config.DB_PATH resolves outside the pytest temporary directory.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced on scratch databases with a control run. Severity is MEDIUM rather than higher because the trigger is the developer's own shell environment, not anything a client or remote caller can reach.
issues.fix_note: conftest assigns CPERSONA_DB_PATH (a fresh mkdtemp conftest.db), CPERSONA_EMBEDDING_MODE=none and CPERSONA_OPERATING_CONTEXT=off before cpersona is imported, instead of os.environ.setdefault, so an exported real store or http embedding mode can't reach the suite. Reverting to setdefault turns tests/test_2611a1_u18.py::test_conftest_overrides_exported_settings and ::test_suite_run_leaves_an_exported_store_untouched red (the latter shows the seeded memory wiped, before=1 after=0).

issues.summary: (LOW) The weekly scheduled CI run shares the master concurrency group with push runs and can cancel them. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:29-31` sets `concurrency: group: ci-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`, and :23-24 adds a `schedule` trigger. A scheduled run executes on the default branch with `github.ref` = `refs/heads/master`, so it joins the same group as a push to master and cancels a push run still in progress. The scheduled run then runs only the unconditioned jobs (wheel-smoke at :169 and container at :324), because lint, verify-issues, version-map, test, windows-index, docs-facts and mutation-proof all carry `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'` (:43, :58, :80, :98, :125, :149, :239). The blocking gates for that commit are left cancelled while the newest CI run for the same SHA is green, and publish.yml reads no CI status before uploading. The collision window is roughly the length of one push run per week and no collision has been observed.
issues.fix_sketch: Put `github.event_name` into the concurrency group key so scheduled and push runs never share a group, or cancel in progress only for pull_request runs.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the workflow, not reproduced. Related to bug-510, which covers the publish workflow's missing CI gate.
issues.fix_note: The CI concurrency group includes github.event_name, so the weekly scheduled run on master can no longer cancel a push run's gates. Reverting the group to ci-${{ github.ref }} turns tests/test_2611a2_x16.py::test_scheduled_ci_run_does_not_share_the_push_concurrency_group red.

issues.summary: (LOW) CI never checks that `uv.lock` matches `pyproject.toml`. Every sync step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is a plain `uv sync` (:115, :135, :165, :253, and :289 for mutation-diff), with no `--locked` and no `uv lock --check` anywhere in the workflows. When the two disagree, `uv sync` re-resolves and rewrites the lock inside the runner and proceeds, so CI tests the fresh resolution while the committed lock stays stale and the change still merges green. The header comment at ci.yml:13 says these jobs resolve dependencies from uv.lock, which stops being true once the lock is stale, and CONTRIBUTING.md documents `uv sync --frozen` and `uv run --frozen pytest`, which use the stale lock without checking it. A pull request that raises a dependency floor (for example a security floor) without regenerating the lock would therefore pass CI while contributors keep testing against the version the floor excludes. The lock is consistent at this commit.
issues.fix_sketch: Pass `--locked` to the CI sync steps (or add one `uv lock --check` step that the other jobs depend on), so a lock that disagrees with pyproject fails the build instead of being re-resolved silently.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the workflow, not reproduced against this tree. The other affected sync steps are ci.yml:135, :165, :253 and :289.
issues.fix_note: Every uv sync in ci.yml passes --locked, so a stale uv.lock fails CI instead of being re-resolved in the runner. Removing --locked turns tests/test_2611a2_x16.py::test_every_ci_dependency_sync_refuses_a_stale_lock red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The docs workflow's path filters omit three of the four mkdocs build hooks. `mkdocs.yml:174-178` registers `scripts/docs_version.py`, `scripts/docs_search_rank.py`, `scripts/docs_ja_lines.py` and `scripts/docs_by_language.py` as build hooks, but the push and pull_request path lists in `.github/workflows/docs.yml` (:23-58 and :60-95) list only `scripts/docs_version.py` (:36, :73). A pull request that edits only one of the other three hooks runs no `mkdocs --strict` build and none of the site gates (anchors, heading parity, language routing, version selector, site URLs), and its merge to master does not redeploy Pages. ci.yml exercises those hooks only through unit tests with stub pages, so a hook that breaks under a real build surfaces later, on the daily scheduled run or the next unrelated docs edit, against a commit that did not cause it. The workflow's own comment (docs.yml:12-15) states that every file the build runs belongs on the trigger.
issues.pattern: # mkdocs\.yml runs these as build hooks, so they are part of every build
issues.fix_sketch: Add `scripts/docs_search_rank.py`, `scripts/docs_ja_lines.py` and `scripts/docs_by_language.py` to both path lists in docs.yml, and consider a test that fails when a hook registered in mkdocs.yml is missing from either list.

issues.summary: (LOW) A malformed configured embedding URL escapes the embedding client's failure boundary instead of returning a failed `EmbedOutcome`. Two routes, both reproduced against the real client. (a) For a non-numeric port such as `:abc` or `:443x`, httpx raises `httpx.InvalidURL`, which subclasses only `Exception` and is not in the boundary tuples `(httpx.RequestError, httpx.HTTPStatusError, ValueError, KeyError)` at `cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/embedding_client.py:406`, :472 and :520, so it escapes `embed_with_outcome`, `capabilities_with_outcome` and `count_tokens_with_outcome`; in api mode `do_store` then raises and writes no row (its guard at `cpersona/memory_handlers.py:314` does not catch it), where a backend 503 would have stored the row without a vector. (b) `_safe_endpoint` guards only `urlsplit()`, but `parts.port` at :95 raises `ValueError` for an out-of-range port; it runs inside the except handlers (via `_failure_evidence` at :724, and at :407 and :473), so a 503 caught at the boundary is replaced by `ValueError: Port out of range` that masks the real error and escapes. The recall path calls `embed_with_outcome` at `cpersona/vector.py:1977` with no guard of its own. Every trigger needs an operator-set malformed URL, and the failure is loud on every call.
issues.fix_sketch: Move the `parts.port` access inside `_safe_endpoint`'s try (or catch ValueError around it), and add `httpx.InvalidURL` to the boundary's except tuples, or validate the configured URLs once at client construction so a typo fails with a clear message at startup.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. Same class as bug-424 and bug-511 (an exception escaping the same boundary). The defect lives in the vendored shared client, so the fix lands upstream first and is then resynced here.

issues.summary: (LOW) A negative embedding cache size makes every successful single-text embed raise `KeyError` outside the client's failure boundary. `CPERSONA_EMBEDDING_CACHE_SIZE` is parsed with no lower bound (`cpersona/config.py:674`) and passed to the client unchanged (`cpersona/server.py:3768`). With a value of -1, `_cache_put` (`cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/embedding_client.py:341-347`) inserts the entry, then loops `while len(self._cache) > self._cache_size`, pops it, and calls `popitem` on an empty OrderedDict, which raises `KeyError`. The call at :551-552 runs after the try block that ends at :520, so the error escapes `embed()` and `embed_with_outcome()`, which document a `None` result for every unsuccessful case. `do_store` catches only `(httpx.RequestError, httpx.HTTPStatusError, ValueError, TypeError)` (`cpersona/memory_handlers.py:314`), so the store fails and the memory is not written; single-text recall embeds raise the same way. A size of 0 works; only negative values break.
issues.fix_sketch: Clamp or reject a negative cache size, both where the client stores it and where CPersona parses the environment variable, and keep the cache write from raising out of the embed call.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The defect lives in the vendored shared client, so the fix lands upstream first; the missing lower bound in config.py can be fixed here.

issues.summary: (LOW) `resolve_env_token` accepts a credential with trailing whitespace or a trailing newline that no HTTP client can present. `cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/identity.py:25-39` checks only that the resolved token is non-empty and ASCII (:38), and `validate_token_entries` (:51) applies the same checks. A token resolved from `${ENV}` whose value ends in a newline or space (for example a secret written to a file with `echo`) therefore loads as an ACL row through `cpersona/acl.py:93-97`, which wraps `resolve_env_token` unchanged. HTTP header parsing strips trailing whitespace and a header cannot carry a line feed, while `_bearer_credential` (`cpersona/server.py:2930`) and the byte-exact comparison expect the stored bytes, so that client gets a permanent 401 and nothing at load names the cause. This fails closed with no security impact; it is a diagnostic gap that runs against acl.py's stated rule (:175-177) that a credential must fail loudly rather than load as a row nothing can present, although that comment is literally about an omitted key.
issues.fix_sketch: Reject (or explicitly strip, with a startup warning) tokens containing leading or trailing whitespace or control characters in both `resolve_env_token` and `validate_token_entries`, so the misconfiguration fails at load with a message naming the client.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The defect lives in the vendored shared client, so the fix lands upstream first and is then resynced here.

issues.summary: (LOW) `parse_chat_think_result` raises `TypeError` when an OpenAI-compatible backend sends `"tool_calls": null` or object-typed tool arguments. In `cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/llm_provider.py:662-663` the tool-call branch is entered whenever the key is present (`"tool_calls" in message_obj`), and `message_obj.get("tool_calls", [])` then returns `None` for a null value, so the loop at :665 raises `TypeError`. At :670-673, `json.loads(arguments_str)` catches only `json.JSONDecodeError`, so arguments sent as a JSON object rather than a string raise `TypeError` as well. Either way a plain answer becomes an internal error for the caller. CPersona cannot reach this code: the module is excluded from the wheel (`pyproject.toml:160-161`) and no cpersona module imports it, which a structural test enforces; the impact is on other consumers of the shared library only.
issues.fix_sketch: Treat a null or non-list `tool_calls` as no tool calls (`message_obj.get("tool_calls") or []`), and accept an arguments value that is already a dict, or catch TypeError alongside JSONDecodeError.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The defect lives in the vendored shared client and has no import path from CPersona, so the fix lands upstream first and is then resynced here.

issues.summary: (LOW) Streaming `think_with_tools` discards text it already streamed when the upstream connection drops mid-body. The docstring of `handle_think_with_tools_streaming` (`cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/llm_provider.py:1150-1152`) promises a partial result on mid-stream network or timeout errors once a chunk has been produced, but the inner handler at :1242 catches only `(httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.ConnectError, LlmApiError)`, and `call_llm_api_streaming` maps only `ConnectError` and `TimeoutException` to `LlmApiError` (:923-932). A connection reset (`httpx.ReadError`) or a peer that closes a chunked body early (`httpx.RemoteProtocolError`) falls through to the outer `except Exception` (:1316) and `_error_response` (:1023), which returns `error_code: internal` with no content and no partial flag, although the chunks were already sent to the client as notifications. Reproduced with a real local TCP server that sends two content deltas and closes the socket without the terminating chunk; the same deltas followed by a stall (ReadTimeout) return the documented partial result. CPersona cannot reach this code: the module is excluded from the wheel (`pyproject.toml:160-161`) and has no import path from cpersona, so the impact is on other consumers of the shared library.
issues.fix_sketch: Widen the inner catch to `httpx.TransportError` (or `httpx.HTTPError`), or map ReadError and RemoteProtocolError to `LlmApiError('upstream_truncated')` in `call_llm_api_streaming`, so every mid-stream transport failure takes the partial-result path.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. The defect lives in the vendored shared client, so the fix lands upstream first and is then resynced here; for the other consumers of that library it is a MEDIUM contract violation.

issues.summary: (LOW) An `mgp/stream/cancel` sent straight after its streaming `tools/call` is answered `not_active` and forgotten, so the stream it was meant to stop then runs to completion. The interceptor forwards the `tools/call` into the inner session and moves on (`cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/mcp_stream_interceptor.py:101`), then answers the cancel from `active_streams` as it is at that moment (`mcp_stream_interceptor.py:135-144`, replying `{"cancelled": False, "reason": "not_active"}`). The handler registers its StreamState only after the SDK has dispatched the forwarded call (`cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/llm_provider.py:1166-1167`). A cancel read in that window gets not_active, nothing remembers it, and the generation then streams in full; re-sending the cancel races the same way. The documented meaning of not_active (already completed or never existed) is wrong in this case. These modules are excluded from the CPersona wheel (`pyproject.toml:160-166`), so the defect reaches consumers of the shared client, not the CPersona package.
issues.fix_sketch: Remember a cancel whose request_id names a `tools/call` the interceptor has forwarded but whose stream has not registered yet (for example a pending-cancel set keyed by request id that the handler checks when it registers), and answer it as cancelled rather than not_active.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The defect lives in the vendored shared client, so the fix lands upstream first and is then re-vendored.

issues.summary: (LOW) The DuckDuckGo provider can attach the next result's snippet to a result that has none. For each `result__a` match the snippet regex runs over `html[match.end() : match.end() + 2000]` (`cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/search.py:188-192`), a slice of the whole page that is not bounded at the next result's anchor. When result A has no `result__snippet` anchor and result B's snippet starts within 2000 characters, A is returned with B's snippet, so text is attributed to the wrong URL. `search.py` is excluded from the CPersona wheel (`pyproject.toml:164`) and CPersona does not use it; the defect reaches other consumers of the shared client.
issues.fix_sketch: Bound the snippet search at the start of the next `result__a` match (or parse each result block separately), so a result without a snippet gets an empty one.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The defect lives in the vendored shared client, so the fix lands upstream first and is then re-vendored.

issues.summary: (LOW) In ACL mode on Windows, `load_config` warns on every start that the ACL file is group/world-accessible and advises making it private, even when its NTFS ACL is owner-only. The check reads `os.stat(path).st_mode` and tests the group/other bits with no platform gate (`cpersona/acl.py:112-120`), but on Windows those mode bits are synthesised and are not the access control. The package already has the guard for this, `fileperms.mode_bits_are_enforced()` (`cpersona/fileperms.py:175`), which `database._warn_if_corpus_is_readable` (`cpersona/database.py:1178`) and `checks.py:3167` use for exactly this reason; the ACL check is the one copy without it. Operators learn to ignore the one warning meant to flag an exposed credential file.
issues.fix_sketch: Skip the mode-bit check when `fileperms.mode_bits_are_enforced()` is false, as the corpus-readability warning and the health check already do.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-296.
issues.fix_note: load_config judges the ACL file's group/other bits only where fileperms.mode_bits_are_enforced() says they are the access control, the gate the database warning and the permissions check already use; on Windows os.stat synthesises 0o666 and the warning fired on every start advising a chmod that changes nothing. Reverting the gate turns tests/test_2611a2_x14.py::test_the_acl_file_mode_is_not_judged_where_mode_bits_are_not_the_access_control red.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test pins the per-agent scoping of seven read tools in `ACL_CLASSIFICATION`: `traverse`, `recall_with_context`, `get_contents`, `get_profile`, `get_recall_precision`, `list_memories` and `list_episodes` (`cpersona/acl.py:508-514`). The classification is correct in 2.6.10 and the guard enforces it. But if any of these rows were demoted to the authenticated-only demand, the guard would skip the empty pattern in both the per-subject boundary loop and the grant loop (`cpersona/acl.py:850-851`, `cpersona/acl.py:882-883`), and a principal granted only agent B could read agent A. The existing tests would not notice: `test_every_registered_tool_is_classified_and_no_row_is_stale` checks set membership only, and `test_annotations_agree_with_classification` compares `max(required)`, which stays PERM_READ after a demotion. Reproduced by mutation: with each of the seven rows demoted, the existing ACL tests still pass, while a granted-only-B probe reads A's records. This is missing regression protection on an access boundary, not a runtime defect.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a parametrized regression test over all nine per-agent read tools (these seven plus recall and reconstruct) that calls each through the served handler with a principal granted only agent B, and asserts that a call for A is denied with agent_id A and leaks nothing, a call for B is allowed, and the per_subject boundary denies a foreign agent.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; the coverage gap was reproduced by mutation. Severity is lower than first reported because the classification itself is correct at this release.
issues.fix_note: Parametrized over the nine per-agent read tools: called through the served handler against real rows, a principal granted only agent B is refused agent A (agent_id A, no A secret in the response) and reads B's own records; the per-subject boundary refuses a foreign agent under a '*': read-write grant. Demoting any read row (e.g. "get_contents": _scoped(PERM_READ) -> lambda args: _AUTHENTICATED_ONLY) turns that tool's cases red.

issues.summary: (LOW) An ACL denial of `store` breaks store's documented contract that every response carries `result`. The store description says every response carries `result`, the one field to branch on (`cpersona/server.py:1005`), and the gate refusal was changed so that `result` is total over every store response (`cpersona/server.py:279`).
