The ACL guard's denial is built by `_denial` (`cpersona/acl.py:705-715`) with `ok`, `error`, `tool`, `agent_id`, `required`, `client_id` and `detail` but no `result`, so a caller that branches on `resp["result"]` gets a missing key instead of `rejected`. docs/ACL_DESIGN.md:223-226 documents that denial shape for store without `result`, so the two published contracts contradict each other.
issues.fix_sketch: Decide which contract wins: either the denial for store carries `result: "rejected"` (and the ACL design doc's example is updated), or the store description narrows its promise to responses the tool itself produces.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The fix changes a published response contract, so it needs a contract decision first. Related: bug-232.
issues.fix_note: The ACL guard builds every denial through _refusal, which adds result:'rejected' to a denial of store or declare_associations. Pinned by tests/test_acl.py::test_a_denied_store_or_declaration_answers_like_its_own_refusals and the two documented-shape tests; making _refusal add nothing turns all three red.

issues.summary: (LOW) A per-subject client calling a process-wide tool is told to scope the call with `agent_id "@me"`, advice that cannot work. `pause_persistence`, `resume_persistence` and `get_session_findings` are classified `_process_wide` (`cpersona/acl.py:495`, `cpersona/acl.py:539`), which always demands every agent, and `check_update` demands every agent unconditionally (`cpersona/acl.py:547`). For a per_subject principal the boundary loop meets the `*` demand and answers with the detail 'scope it to your own space with agent_id "@me"' (`cpersona/acl.py:858-866`). This branch runs before, and instead of, the intrinsic-sweep explanation the grant path gives (`cpersona/acl.py:930-948`). A client that follows the advice resolves `@me` (which can issue an alias as a side effect) and is denied again with the same detail; nothing says the tool cannot be called from a per-subject client.
issues.fix_sketch: On the per-subject boundary, when the demand is intrinsically all-agents (the process-wide tools and check_update), say that the tool is not available to a per-subject client instead of advising `@me`, reusing the reason the demand already carries.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Same class as bug-264 (advice that cannot work for an intrinsic sweep), recurring on the per-subject branch.
issues.fix_note: The per-subject boundary asks the same counterfactuals the grant path asks (_widened_by_omission for a sweep, _demanded_whatever_the_scope for a named agent) before advising "@me"; an intrinsic sweep is told its stated cause and that no agent_id narrows it, and an agent named by an export-directory file is named as such. Restoring the constant details turns tests/test_2611a2_x14.py::test_a_per_subject_sweep_no_scope_narrows_is_not_advised_at_me and ::test_a_foreign_agent_the_file_names_is_not_advised_at_me red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `_post_remote_side_effect` posts to the remote index with no timeout (`cpersona/admin_handlers.py:380`), so it inherits the embedding client's request timeout (30 s by default) instead of `REMOTE_INDEX_TIMEOUT_SECS` (`cpersona/config.py:810`, 10 s by default), which its sibling remote calls state (`cpersona/vector.py:160`, `cpersona/memory_handlers.py:369`). It is used by delete, update, episode delete, agent purge and the move de-index (`admin_handlers.py:475`, `:563`, `:745`, `:806`, `:2438`). Reproduced against a hung index endpoint: the sibling call returned at the index deadline while `delete_memory` waited the full client timeout. The move de-index calls it serially per 128-id chunk (`admin_handlers.py:744-750`), so a hung service multiplies the wait by the number of chunks. The call runs after the commit, so no data is at risk; the cost is latency.
issues.fix_sketch: Pass `timeout=REMOTE_INDEX_TIMEOUT_SECS` on the post. For the move de-index, stop after the first timed-out chunk or share one overall deadline across chunks so a hung service cannot multiply the wait.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced against a hung endpoint. Related: bug-330, bug-323, bug-159, bug-346.
issues.fix_note: _post_remote_side_effect passes timeout=REMOTE_INDEX_TIMEOUT_SECS and reports a timeout to its caller. _remove_moved_source_vectors stops after a timed-out chunk. Reverting the timeout turns test_every_side_effect_post_states_the_index_deadline[*] and test_side_effect_post_against_a_hung_service_returns_at_the_index_deadline red. Removing the break turns test_move_de_index_stops_after_a_timed_out_chunk red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `update_memory` has no handling for the content UNIQUE index. `do_update_memory` runs a plain `UPDATE memories SET content = ?, embedding = ?, embedding_model = ? WHERE id = ? AND locked = 0` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:551-556). The index `idx_memories_dedup_content` is on (agent_id, project_id, channel, content) (cpersona/database.py:1068-1069). Editing a row to text that another row in the same agent, project and channel already holds raises `sqlite3.IntegrityError` out of the handler. The vendored dispatcher then answers `{"error": "UNIQUE constraint failed: memories.agent_id, memories.project_id, memories.channel, memories.content"}` with no `ok` key and isError=false (cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/mcp_utils.py:204-205). Reproduced through the server's real MCP CallTool handler: the rows stay unchanged and the rollback is clean, so no data is lost. The caller gets an opaque message that names schema columns, with no duplicate id, and the tool description does not mention this refusal. Sibling write paths absorb the same collision on purpose (the `do_store` probes, and the content-rewriting health fixers in cpersona/checks.py:154-166). A client that follows the documented rule 'treat any response carrying error as a failure' still detects the failure, which is why this is LOW.
issues.fix_sketch: Probe for a same-bucket row with identical content before the UPDATE, or catch sqlite3.IntegrityError around it. Return error_response naming the existing duplicate (for example `duplicate_of`), and mention the refusal in the update_memory tool description.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Related: bug-113 and bug-127 (the same collision guarded on the health-fix path), and bug-161 (error_response as the single failure constructor).
issues.fix_note: do_update_memory looks for a same-bucket row holding the new text before it embeds (_same_bucket_holder). It also catches sqlite3.IntegrityError around the UPDATE, for a copy that lands during the embedding await, and in both cases answers error_response naming the holder. Reverting the catch turns test_update_racing_a_store_of_the_same_text_is_refused_not_raised red. Reverting the pre-probe turns test_update_into_same_bucket_text_is_refused_and_names_the_holder red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `update_memory` reports 'is locked' for a row that was removed concurrently. The guarded UPDATE matches `id = ? AND locked = 0` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:553). When it changes no row, the handler always answers `Memory N is locked and cannot be edited` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:556-557). A row deleted between the ownership/lock pre-check (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:498-509) and the UPDATE also gives rowcount 0. In that window a row can disappear through `delete_memory`, `delete_agent_data`, or a merge move, which DELETEs the source rows (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3551). The caller is given a wrong reason, and may try `unlock_memory` or tell the user the note is protected. A scoped caller should get the uniform not-found refusal of bug-367 instead. Confirmed by reading the code. The window is a narrow race.
issues.fix_sketch: When the UPDATE changes no row, re-read the row inside the same transaction. Answer through the same `_by_id_refusal` path as the pre-check: not found (uniform for a scoped caller) if the row is gone or owned by someone else, and locked only if it is actually locked.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-367 (the uniform by-id refusal for scoped callers).
issues.fix_note: After a no-match UPDATE, do_update_memory re-reads the row inside the same transaction. It reports 'locked' only when the row still exists and is locked, and otherwise answers not-found through _by_id_refusal (ambiguous for a scoped caller). Reverting turns test_update_of_a_row_deleted_meanwhile_says_not_found_not_locked, the scoped variant and the merge-move variant red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Sidecar rewrites restamp `calibrated_at`, so deep_check can report a stale calibration as fresh. `_save_calibration_state` always writes `"calibrated_at": datetime.now(...)` for the whole sidecar (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1288). `_purge_agent_calibration` rewrites the sidecar whenever it removed an agent's entries (on delete_agent_data and on a merge move) without re-measuring anything (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:690-710). It passes the stored `scoring_version` through so that dropping an agent cannot launder staleness (bug-184), but it does not pass `calibrated_at` through. A per-agent calibrate_threshold or set_recall_precision restamps the time for every carried agent in the same way. `deep_calibration_staleness` reads that single timestamp for every agent (cpersona/checks.py:3925-3944). A 200-day-old calibration of agent B therefore reads as status ok with age_days 0 after an unrelated agent is purged. Confirmed by reading the code. The effect is a wrong advisory status in deep_check.
issues.fix_sketch: Let `_save_calibration_state` take a `calibrated_at` and have rewrites that measure nothing (the purge) pass the stored value through. Consider recording the time per agent, so calibrating one agent does not reset the age of the others.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-184 (the same laundering, closed for scoring_version). Partly fixed in 2.6.11a2: _purge_agent_calibration passes the stored calibrated_at through the new calibrated_at parameter of _save_calibration_state, so dropping a deleted or moved-out agent keeps the stored time. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_x02.py::test_dropping_an_agent_keeps_the_stored_calibration_time and ::test_a_move_that_empties_its_source_keeps_the_stored_calibration_time red. Remaining half (one stamp for all agents, restamped by a per-agent calibration) is not fixed. The open anchor now names the remaining half.

issues.summary: (LOW) A calibration in flight can bring back calibration that delete_agent_data just purged. `do_calibrate_threshold` awaits `_sample_embeddings` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1797) and `_temporal_adjacency_sims`, then writes `vector._agent_thresholds[agent_id]` without rechecking (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1848). It also awaits `_calibrate_fused_gate_median` before the gate write (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1891). `do_delete_agent_data` commits the delete and then runs `_purge_agent_calibration` once (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:838-840). If the purge lands in an await window, the calibration writes the deleted agent's threshold back, and the sidecar save serialises it through `{**carried, **dict(vector._agent_thresholds)}` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1910-1922). A later agent created under the same id then restores calibration measured on the deleted corpus, which is the bug-036 state. set_recall_precision reaches the same path. The startup guard has the same stale-read shape: it reads the sidecar, awaits `_corpus_embedding_dim()`, then restores what it read earlier (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2210-2219). Confirmed by reading the code. It needs a delete to run concurrently with a calibration of the same agent.
issues.fix_sketch: Have the purge bump a per-agent generation (or record a tombstone) that calibration captures before its first await and rechecks before each write to the process dicts and the sidecar, discarding its result for a purged agent. Apply the same recheck to the startup restore.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-036 (the sequential case this race reopens).
issues.fix_note: do_calibrate_threshold notes vector._agent_calibration_purges(agent_id) before its first await. _purge_agent_calibration bumps that count. The calibration rechecks it before the threshold write and again after the last await (this line), and discards a measurement whose agent was purged. The startup guard reads the sidecar after its await, and its restore skips pending entries. Removing this line turns tests/test_2611a2_x02.py::test_a_delete_during_the_gate_measurement_is_not_undone_by_the_calibration red.

issues.summary: (LOW) A set_recall_precision that fails and is rolled back can still be persisted by a concurrent calibration of another agent. do_set_recall_precision writes the tentative beta into process state (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2051) and claims it (2057) before it awaits do_calibrate_threshold (2071), and every calibration's sidecar save serialises the whole beta dict (`**dict(vector._agent_betas)`, 1922). If agent B's calibration resumes and saves while agent A's beta is tentative (statements queue on the shared background connection), A's beta reaches disk. A's calibration then fails (for example fewer than 10 embeddings), A answers ok:false and rolls back in memory only (the bug-149 compare-and-restore), and the next startup restore (2186) reapplies the beta the caller was told was not applied, with no gate measured at it. The window is narrow: it needs a concurrent calibration plus a failing set.
issues.fix_sketch: Keep the tentative beta out of the shared dict until calibration succeeds (pass it to the calibration explicitly), or have sidecar saves exclude entries that are mid-transaction. The rollback path should also repair the sidecar if a concurrent save already wrote the tentative value.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, not yet reproduced. Residual of the bug-096 and bug-149 rollback work, which protects process memory but not a sidecar write another coroutine already made.
issues.fix_note: set_recall_precision hands the new beta to do_calibrate_threshold (precision_override) instead of writing it into vector._agent_betas first. The calibration writes it to the sidecar with the gate measured at it, and set_recall_precision adopts it only after that write succeeds, so no tentative beta exists for another agent's calibration to persist. Re-adding the tentative write turns tests/test_2611a2_x02.py::test_a_failed_precision_change_is_not_persisted_by_another_agents_calibration red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Export silently replaces non-JSON source and metadata with {}. The exporter maps both fields through _try_parse_json (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2630 and 2632), which returns {} on a JSONDecodeError (cpersona/utils.py:422-427), and import writes json.dumps of that value (admin_handlers.py:2895-2897). Legacy or hand-edited text values are therefore lost on a backup round trip with no per-line note. This includes locked rows, which the invalid_json health fix deliberately leaves untouched (`locked = 0` guard, cpersona/checks.py:1850-1856). Reaching it needs rows whose source or metadata is not valid JSON.
issues.pattern: return \{\}, text if isinstance\(text, str\) else None
issues.fix_sketch: Export a value that is not valid JSON verbatim (for example as a raw string field with a marker) and have import write it back unchanged, or at least record a per-line note in the export and import responses when a value was replaced.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, not yet reproduced.
issues.fix_note: Export writes non-JSON source/metadata text verbatim as source_text/metadata_text beside {}, and import stores it back as it was; reverting either half turns test_export_carries_non_json_source_and_metadata_through_a_restore red.

issues.summary: (LOW) A NUL byte in an export or import path escapes the error-response contract. os.stat, open and tempfile.mkstemp raise ValueError('embedded null character in path'), not OSError. A NUL in input_path passes _confine_io_path and escapes the `except OSError` around `os.stat(confined)` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2784-2787); a NUL in output_path escapes at the mkstemp call (2581) or the open. The exception reaches the generic registry wrapper in the vendored shared client, which answers `{"error": ...}` without ok:false, so a client that branches on `ok` gets neither ok:false nor the documented error_response shape. The input is malformed, so impact is limited to the response shape.
issues.pattern: if not path or "\\x00" in path:
issues.fix_sketch: Reject a path containing a NUL in _confine_io_path (or catch ValueError alongside OSError at the stat, mkstemp and open sites) and return an error_response with ok:false.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, not yet reproduced. Same contract class as bug-242, which was fixed only for UnicodeDecodeError.
issues.fix_note: _confine_io_path refuses a path holding NUL before any filesystem call, so export, import and the ACL guard readers answer in the error-response shape; reverting turns test_nul_byte_in_export_and_import_paths_is_an_error_response red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The content sanitiser is not idempotent, and import re-applies it, so a backup round trip can change content and duplicate a row. _sanitize_with_cap removes '[Memory from ...]' with a single re.sub (cpersona/utils.py:90), which can assemble a new annotation from the surrounding text (for example '[Memory fr[Memory from bot] om the harbour log] tide' stores as '[Memory from the harbour log] tide' and a second pass yields 'tide'). Import sanitises again (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2845) before the content dedup probe, so a stored row without a msg_id that is not a fixed point of the sanitiser comes back changed and is inserted as a second row under ok:true. Separately, the truncation note is appended (2850-2855) before the msg_id skip (2867-2873), so a skipped row can be reported as truncated. Reaching the duplication needs content containing a nested annotation.
issues.fix_sketch: Make the annotation strip idempotent (repeat the substitution until the text stops changing) so store and import agree, and move the truncation note after the msg_id duplicate check.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, with the sanitiser's non-idempotence checked directly; the import duplication was not reproduced. Related to bug-221.
issues.fix_note: The sanitiser strips annotations to a fixed point with a linear scan and trims after the cut, so sanitising twice equals once; reverting to the single sub turns test_sanitiser_is_idempotent_on_an_annotation_assembled_by_its_own_removal and test_a_round_trip_of_a_nested_annotation_neither_mutates_nor_duplicates red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `import_memories` restores a memory or episode record that has no `project_id` key into the global pool and says nothing. `_import_memory_record` defaults the axis with `record.get("project_id", "")` and `record.get("channel", "")` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2859-2860), and episodes do the same at admin_handlers.py:2998-2999. Exports written before the bug-016 fix never carried `project_id` or `channel`, yet they use the same header version string, `cpersona-export/1.0`, that the current exporter writes (admin_handlers.py:2602). Restoring such a file returns ok:true with no `errors` entry. Each restored row lands in project '' and then shows up in every other project's reads for that agent. This is relevance contamination within one agent, not an isolation breach: project_id is not an access boundary. The project information was already missing from the old file, so the importer cannot recover it, but it gives no warning. docs/tools.md:65 and docs/operations.md:32-34 do not mention that older exports lack these axes.
issues.fix_sketch: When a memory or episode record has no `project_id` key at all, add a line to `errors` saying the row went to the global pool. The current exporter always writes the key, even when its value is ''. Document in docs/tools.md and docs/operations.md that pre-bug-016 exports do not carry the project and channel axes, and bump the header version string with any future format change.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced: a legacy-format import reported ok:true with no errors, and the row appeared in another project's listing. Related to bug-016, the exporter fix that began writing these axes.
issues.fix_note: An export whose memory/episode records lack project_id is restored with an errors note saying how many rows went to the global pool; reverting turns test_records_without_the_project_axis_are_reported red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Several import fields are converted or bound only on the real-run path, so a dry run can preview ok:true for a file that the real run then aborts and rolls back in full. Memory `recall_count` goes through `int(record.get("recall_count") or 0)` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2923), which raises on a non-numeric value. Memory `last_recalled_at` and `created_at` (admin_handlers.py:2924-2925) and episode `start_time`, `end_time` and `created_at` (admin_handlers.py:3026-3031) are bound as whatever JSON type the file holds, so a dict or list fails at bind time. The dry run skips these INSERTs (`if not tally.dry_run:` at 2895 and 3014), so it never meets these errors. Because the import is atomic over the whole file, one malformed record among thousands blocks the entire restore. Invalid JSON lines, by contrast, are reported one per line.
issues.fix_sketch: Validate and coerce `recall_count`, the memory timestamps and the episode time fields on both arms before the dry_run split, as bug-094 does for keywords. Report a value that cannot be coerced as a per-line error that skips that record, not as an exception that aborts the file.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Extends bug-094; the null gamma-axis variant is bug-527.
issues.fix_note: Every imported value is checked before the dry-run split and an unbindable one refuses its own line instead of aborting the restore; reverting the check turns test_a_bad_field_refuses_its_line_not_the_restore red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The episode dedup probe that import uses, `SELECT id FROM episodes WHERE agent_id = ? AND project_id = ? AND channel = ? AND summary = ? LIMIT 1` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3004-3008), has no index that covers `summary`. Every episode index keys on agent_id plus project_id or channel, so each probe scans the whole (agent, project) bucket, including rows the same run has already inserted. Because episodes have no uniqueness constraint, this probe is the only dedup gate. Restoring E episodes into one bucket therefore costs O(E^2) comparisons, and the real run does this inside `transaction()` with the write lock held, so every other writer waits for it. `merge_memories` runs the same probe at admin_handlers.py:3462-3466.
issues.pattern: existing = await tally\.episode_keys\.find\(db, target_agent_id, ep_project_id, ep_channel, summary\)
issues.fix_sketch: Give the probe an index it can seek, for example on (agent_id, project_id, channel, summary) or on a summary hash column. Alternatively, preload the target bucket's summaries into a set once per run, then check each record against the set and add it after insert. Apply the same change to the merge path.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The probe was introduced by bug-220 and bug-076.
issues.fix_note: The episode dedup gate reads each agent's episodes once into a digest map (_EpisodeSummaryIndex) instead of issuing a bucket-scanning summary probe per incoming row, at both the merge and import sites; a digest hit is confirmed by primary key. Reverting either site to the per-row probe turns test_merge/import_episode_dedup_does_not_scan_the_bucket_per_row and test_merge_episode_dedup_is_linear_in_the_rows_read red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Importing a multi-agent export with `target_agent_id` set keeps only the last profile per `user_id` and says nothing. With a target, every record's agent becomes the target (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3201-3217). Each profile record then runs the unconditional `ON CONFLICT(agent_id, user_id) DO UPDATE` (admin_handlers.py:3093), so each earlier profile is overwritten by the next one in file order. Nothing is added to `errors`, and the response says only `profile_updated: true`. `merge_memories` handles the same collision by skipping it and reporting `skipped_profile`.
issues.fix_sketch: When a target agent is set and a second profile for the same `user_id` arrives in the same run, skip it, or merge it as merge_memories does, and report the collision in the response instead of overwriting silently.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Shares its upsert site with bug-528.
issues.fix_note: Import keeps the first profile it restores to a target (agent_id, user_id) key and reports each later one instead of letting it overwrite; reverting turns test_profiles_colliding_on_one_target_keep_the_first_and_report_the_rest red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Test gap: no test pins the conflict arm of the bug-223 fix. When a profile already exists, the ON CONFLICT branch of `_import_profile_record` carries the record's own `updated_at` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3095), as the comment at admin_handlers.py:3089 says it must. The existing test covers only the INSERT arm. Changing the conflict arm to restamp `updated_at` with `datetime('now')` breaks no test, although that regression would bring back the bug-223 symptom: a restore over an existing profile would disarm `deep_stale_profile`.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test that imports a profile record with an old `updated_at` over an existing profile row and asserts that the stored `updated_at` equals the record's stamp, not the import time.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code and by a mutation the suite did not catch. Related to bug-223.
issues.fix_note: New test restores a profile over an existing older row and asserts the stored updated_at is the file's stamp; turning the ON CONFLICT arm's `updated_at = excluded.updated_at` into `updated_at = datetime('now')` turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Test gap: the episode comparison in `_validate_file_header` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3126) can be deleted without any test failing. The memory-count and profile-count comparisons are pinned by the bug-091 and bug-110 tests. If the episode comparison regressed, an export of an agent with no profile that is cut inside the episode section would still pass the other two counts. The import would then commit a partial episode set with ok:true.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test that truncates an export inside the episode section, with matching memory and profile counts, and asserts that the import is refused and rolled back.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code and by a mutation the suite did not catch. Related to bug-091 and bug-110.
issues.fix_note: New test cuts a real export inside the episode section (memory and profile counts still matching) and asserts ok:false, a truncation error and nothing committed; replacing the episode comparison in _validate_file_header with `or False` turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Test gap: no test pins the bounded read `raw = f.read(config.MAX_IMPORT_BYTES + 1)` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3161), the bug-241 residual fix. Replacing it with an unbounded `f.read()` gives the same return value, because the file is then read whole and rejected by `len(raw) > MAX_IMPORT_BYTES`. The memory bound described by the comment at admin_handlers.py:3156-3159 could therefore regress silently: a file that grows between the size check and the open would be read into memory in full before it is rejected.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test that observes how many bytes are read, not just the return value. For example, report a small size from a monkeypatched stat over a large file, or wrap the file object, and assert that no more than MAX_IMPORT_BYTES + 1 bytes are read.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code and by a mutation the suite did not catch. Related to bug-241.
issues.fix_note: New test grows the file between the size check and the open and counts bytes read; replacing do_import_memories' `f.read(config.MAX_IMPORT_BYTES + 1)` with `f.read()` turns it red. A companion test pins the same bound in import_file_agents.

issues.summary: (LOW) The `merge_memories` dry_run preview disagrees with the real merge when the source agent holds identical memory rows, which happens in the documented bug-349 state where `idx_memories_dedup_content` could not be created because locked rows collide. `_MergeTally` keeps no within-batch content set for memories on the assumption that the source's UNIQUE indexes make intra-batch collisions impossible (comment at cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3293-3294). In the real run the content probe at cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3376-3382 sees the merge's own uncommitted copy of the first row and skips the second; dry_run inserts nothing, so it counts both as merged (preview merged/skipped 2/0, real run 1/1). Only the reported counts are wrong; no data is lost. The import path already tracks this with `seen_content` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2890).
issues.fix_sketch: Track within-batch (target, project, channel, content) keys for memories in dry_run, as the import path's `seen_content` and the episode merge's `seen_summary` already do, and correct the comment that says memories cannot collide within a batch.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Same class as bug-071 (episodes) and bug-070 (import); the trigger state is the one bug-349 documents.
issues.fix_note: The merge preview remembers the message ids and content it previewed (seen_msgid / seen_content on _MergeTally), so duplicate source rows on a database without the dedup indexes are counted as the real merge counts them. Reverting turns test_merge_preview_matches_the_real_run_on_duplicate_source_content and ..._msg_id red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `merge_memories` inserts new target rows (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3384-3410 for memories, 3473-3493 for episodes) but never calls `blocks.queue_build` or `nodes.queue_build`, unlike store and update_memory (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:411/419, cpersona/admin_handlers.py:582/590). In move mode the source rows' blocks are also dropped by the delete triggers. On a long-running server the merged records have no block set, so the block arm does not reach them until a restart's backfill sweep or a `check_health` fix of `missing_blocks`. The gap is detectable and repairable and degrades reach rather than corrupting data; it only affects deployments that enabled blocks/nodes. `do_import_memories` has the same gap.
issues.fix_sketch: After the merge (and import) transaction commits, queue block and node builds for every inserted memory and episode id, the same way the store path does.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The import path is a sibling site with the same omission.
issues.fix_note: After the merge commits, _queue_derived_builds queues block construction for every record the merge inserted and node construction for those past the token window (batched token report via nodes.overflowing), as store does; failures are logged, never raised. Reverting turns test_merge_queues_block_and_node_builds_for_written_records red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Three carried-through columns have no test that would catch a regression: the merged episode's `resolved` flag (`_merge_episode_rows`, cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3486), the merged profile's `project_id` (`_merge_profile_rows`, cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3531), and the exported profile record's `project_id` (`do_export_memories`, cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2687). The production code is correct today, but each line can be mutated (to `0` or `''`) with the suite staying green. Dropping either profile `project_id` would move a project-scoped profile into the global '' bucket of the target or of a restored database, where every project's reads see it; dropping `resolved` would land every merged episode unresolved.
issues.fix_sketch: Add merge and export round-trip assertions that a resolved episode stays resolved after a merge and that a profile stored under a non-empty project_id keeps it after a merge and after export followed by import.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code and by mutation, not reproduced as a live defect (test-only). Related to bug-219, which fixed the carry of episode timestamps on merge.
issues.fix_note: Tests added for the merged episode's resolved flag, the merged profile's project_id and the exported/imported profile's project_id. Red under: resolved -> 0 in _merge_episode_page (resolved test), prof_project_id -> '' in _merge_profile_rows (merge profile test), "project_id": row[4] -> "" in the export profile record (export/import test).

issues.summary: (LOW) `_merge_profile_rows` selects `id, user_id, content, project_id` but not `updated_at` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3510) and inserts the copy with `datetime('now')` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3529-3531). A copied or moved profile therefore looks freshly updated on the target, and `deep_stale_profile`, whose only input is `updated_at` (cpersona/checks.py:3830-3835), stays silent for `_STALE_PROFILE_DAYS` (30 days) even when the content is months old. The import path (`COALESCE(?, datetime('now'))`, bug-223) and the episode merge (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3477) both preserve the original timestamp, so this is an inconsistency rather than a design choice. The effect is a weakened advisory health check.
issues.fix_sketch: Select the source profile's `updated_at` and insert it with `COALESCE(?, datetime('now'))`, matching the import path.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Sibling of bug-223 (import) at the merge site; bug-219 and bug-131 fixed the same class for merged episodes and memories.
issues.fix_note: _merge_profile_rows selects the source's updated_at and inserts it with COALESCE(?, datetime('now')) instead of stamping the merge time. Reverting turns test_merge_keeps_the_copied_profile_updated_at red.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test moves more than one delete chunk, so the per-table `source_deleted` counts summed across chunks of `_MOVE_DELETE_CHUNK = 500` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3598) are unpinned. Every test that drives `do_merge_memories` seeds at most a few dozen rows and asserts deleted counts of 0, 1 or 2; with one chunk, `count += cur.rowcount` and `count = cur.rowcount` behave identically, so a regression that keeps only the last chunk's count (a 700-row move reporting 200 deleted) would pass. The production code is correct today.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a move test with more than 500 copied memories and assert that source_deleted.deleted_memories equals the number moved.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code and the tests, not reproduced (test-only).
issues.fix_note: Test added that moves _MOVE_DELETE_CHUNK+200 memories and _MOVE_DELETE_CHUNK+37 episodes and asserts source_deleted reports every row. Red under `count += cur.rowcount` -> `count = cur.rowcount` (reports 200 of 700).

issues.summary: (LOW) No test covers a move that leaves rows at the source, so the two gates that keep a still-live source intact can be inverted with the suite green: the agent-level teardown gate (`_purge_agent_calibration` and `_purge_agent_remote_namespace` only when `left_at_source` is all zero, cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3724) and the pending-task drain gate in `_delete_merged_source_rows` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:3606). Reproduced by mutation probe: forcing the teardown purges the remote namespace of a source that still holds a skipped locked memory and drops its precision beta and thresholds; forcing the drain deletes the pending tasks of a live source. The nearest guard, the bug-346 test, explicitly accepts a purge, so it cannot tell the teardown branch from the per-row removal branch. The shipped code is correct; these are post-commit side effects on a less common path.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a move test that leaves a skipped locked memory at the source and seeds a pending task, an agent beta/threshold and a recording remote client; assert no namespace purge, calibration and the pending task survive (deleted_pending_tasks == 0), and the moved ids get a per-row remove. Tighten the bug-346 test so it rejects a purge when left_at_source is non-zero.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced by a mutation probe (test-only). Guards the fixes for bug-218, bug-222 and bug-346.
issues.fix_note: Test added for a move that leaves a skipped locked memory at the source with a pending task, a beta/threshold and a recording remote client: asserts no source namespace purge, a per-id /remove of the moved row, calibration kept and deleted_pending_tasks == 0. The bug-346 test now rejects a purge when the move left a profile behind. Red under `if not any(left_at_source.values()):` -> `if True:` (both tests) and under `if any(left.values()):` -> `if False:` (new test).

issues.summary: (LOW) The alias ledger's re-read, merge, mint and whole-file rewrite take no cross-process lock. `resolve_or_issue` re-reads at cpersona/aliases.py:149, mints, and `_persist` replaces the file at cpersona/aliases.py:257 with no lock and no compare-before-replace, although the module names a second server process over the same path as a supported writer and bug-351's fix sketch asked for the re-read to happen under a lock. If process B issues an alias between process A's re-read and A's replace, A's write erases B's row while B has already answered `alias_issued: true`. Reproduced with two ledger instances over one path and an injected interleaving. If B restarts before issuing again, the subject gets a fresh alias, its memories are stranded, and the reserved-agent-id startup check can then refuse to boot. Rated LOW: the window is the synchronous merge-to-replace span, it needs two per-subject HTTP processes sharing a data directory (a deployment the docs do not describe), and it heals if B issues any other alias before restarting.
issues.fix_sketch: Hold an exclusive advisory lock on a sidecar lockfile across re-read, merge, mint and os.replace; alternatively re-check the file's fingerprint just before the replace and retry the merge if it changed.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced by a probe with an injected interleaving. Incomplete fix of bug-351; related to bug-531.
issues.fix_note: resolve_or_issue runs the strict re-read, the mint and the os.replace under an exclusive advisory lock on <ledger>.lock that every server process takes, so a second process's issuance can no longer land between this process's re-read and rename and be erased by it. Reverting the lock turns tests/test_2611a2_x14.py::test_a_second_process_issuing_inside_the_window_keeps_its_row red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `associations.declare` checks before it writes, outside a write-locked transaction, so a second process can change the database in the gap. The entity lookup (`_resolve_entity`, cpersona/associations.py:166) and the anchor check (`_record_exists`, associations.py:115-119) run as autocommit reads before the first INSERT opens the implicit transaction; the in-process `_write_lock` (cpersona/database.py:347) does not serialise other processes. (a) If another process registers the same normalized entity in the gap, the plain `INSERT INTO entities` (associations.py:172-176) raises a UNIQUE-constraint IntegrityError, which reaches the caller as a bare `{"error": ...}` instead of reusing the entity. (b) If another process deletes the anchor record in the gap, declare commits an `entity_mentions` row for a record whose delete trigger has already fired, and no health check sweeps such orphans. Both variants were reproduced through the MCP handler with a second connection committing at the injected point. Impact is limited: the window is one SELECT-to-INSERT gap, a retry of (a) succeeds, and the orphan in (b) is inert because record ids are never reused.
issues.fix_sketch: Open declare's transaction with BEGIN IMMEDIATE so the existence checks and the writes share one write-locked snapshot across processes. Alternatively, register entities with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING followed by a re-select, and re-check the anchor inside the write transaction.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. Through the `store` associations rider, variant (a) also produces the committed-but-reported-as-error symptom of bug-532.
issues.fix_note: transaction() now opens with BEGIN IMMEDIATE on a file database (bug-508), and declare runs its entity lookup and anchor check inside it, so another process can no longer register the same entity or delete the anchor between the check and the write: it waits for the lock or the lock waits for it. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u03.py::test_declare_reuses_an_entity_another_process_registers_in_the_gap and ::test_declare_does_not_mention_a_record_another_process_deletes_in_the_gap red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The documentation says a relation's predicate is kept as written and reported as declared, but the code stores and reports only the normalized form. `declare()` binds `normalize(predicate)` into `relations.predicate` (cpersona/associations.py:312-313) and keeps no as-written copy, so every reader of the column (traverse, and the `why: relation:<predicate>` of a reconstruct claim) returns the NFKC case-folded form; a predicate declared as `Maintains` comes back as `maintains`. The module docstring (associations.py:10-13) and docs/ASSOCIATIVE_MEMORY_DESIGN.md:130-133 say `name`, `alias` and `predicate` are kept as written with a normalized twin, and the design doc's section 9 says "The predicate is reported as declared" (line 324), while the same doc's schema comment (line 94) says the column holds the normalized form. Lookups and recall behave correctly; the defect is the contradictory documentation.
issues.pattern: The predicate is reported in its normalized form \(§2\)\.
issues.fix_sketch: Correct the module docstring and the design doc to say the predicate is stored and reported in normalized form, matching the schema comment. Keeping the declared spelling instead would need an as-written column, which is a schema decision.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: The design doc (§2, invariant 4, §9), its Japanese twin and the associations module docstring now say the predicate is stored and reported only in normalized form (Maintains reads back as maintains); only name and alias keep the as-written form beside a normalized twin. Docs only; the open anchor 'The predicate is reported as declared.' is gone.

issues.summary: (LOW) A `store` whose content holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate answers a bare `{"error": "'utf-8' codec can't encode character ... surrogates not allowed"}` with no `ok` and no `result`, against the store contract that every response carries `result` and that unusable content is refused with `result: 'rejected'`. Sanitization (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:218) lets the surrogate through, and the content dedup SELECT (memory_handlers.py:288-291) raises UnicodeEncodeError when SQLite binds it. Confirmed over the MCP in-memory transport with embedding off. The same input also fails `recall` and `reconstruct` (associations.py:391-396, the `query_terms` bind) with a clean error; the reported asymmetry where reconstruct fails but recall answers was not reproduced in that configuration. Reach is limited: the stdio transport rejects lone surrogates at JSON parse, so only the streamable-HTTP transport and in-process callers can deliver one.
issues.fix_sketch: Refuse or replace lone surrogates during content sanitization, so such a store returns `result: 'rejected'` (or stores the repaired text) instead of raising from the dedup query; apply the same treatment to query strings before `query_terms` binds them.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; the store contract violation was confirmed by running it over the in-memory transport, while the recall/reconstruct asymmetry in the original report did not hold.
issues.fix_note: reconstruct (and store, recall, recall_with_context, get_contents, archive_episode) check their text arguments with utils.lone_surrogate_issue before anything binds them and refuse in the tool's own failure shape; reverting reconstruct's check turns tests/test_2611a2_x05.py::test_reconstruct_refuses_a_lone_surrogate_with_its_collections red (UnicodeEncodeError), and reverting store's turns ::test_store_refuses_a_lone_surrogate_with_a_result red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Three behaviours of `associations.query_terms` are not pinned by any test, so a regression in them would pass the suite. (1) A term that two visible entities share (for example the global and project entities bug-448 creates) must match both: `found = term in found_terms` (cpersona/associations.py:410) lets the second entity reuse a span the first one claimed. (2) Spans that only touch must not count as overlapping (associations.py:414). (3) The `MAX_EXPANSION_TERMS` cut and its `terms_omitted` report (associations.py:447-455) are never executed by any test. Confirmed by mutation: with `found = False`, with `end < s or start > e`, and with `len(terms) > MAX_EXPANSION_TERMS`, all associations tests still pass. The production code itself is correct; this is a test-coverage gap.
issues.fix_sketch: Add tests that declare the same name in the global pool and a project with different aliases and assert both aliases come back, that two touching spans both match, and that a query naming more than `MAX_EXPANSION_TERMS` expansion terms is cut with the right `terms_omitted` count.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by mutation testing against the existing suite, not a runtime defect. Related: bug-448.
issues.fix_note: Test-only: tests/test_2611a2_y04.py pins query_terms' shared-term reuse (global and project 'Atlas' both named), touching spans as disjoint ('foobar' names Foo and Bar), and the 32-term expansion cut with an exact terms_omitted (and none at exactly 32). Mutant `found = False` at associations.py found_terms line turns test_a_name_two_visible_entities_share_names_both red; `end < s or start > e` and `len(terms) > MAX_EXPANSION_TERMS` turn the other two red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The relation walk reads `per_entity + 1` full-content rows for every entity within the hop bound, and nothing bounds how many entities that is, so a call's read cost grows with the caller's declared graph while its response stays the same size. `walk_graph` issues one `_mentioning_records` query per reached entity (cpersona/associations.py:704-707), and `max_evidence` is applied only after every record has been read. Reproduced under default bounds (max_hops 2, max_evidence 40): one `reconstruct(count=1)` read 2,624 rows for a hub with 64 neighbouring entities and 41,984 rows for 1,024, a 16x increase for the same 39-claim response (0.03 s to 0.24 s measured). `_neighbourhood` (associations.py:517) and `traverse` likewise expand every entity within the hop cap regardless of `limit`. The documented contract bounds only hops and records per entity, so this is a resource gap rather than a broken invariant; the cost is confined to the caller's own graph, though the walk runs on the shared read connection, so other clients' reads queue behind it on large graphs.
issues.fix_sketch: Read records lazily in the walk's own order (hops, recency, id) and stop once an item has `max_evidence`; cap the number of entities the neighbourhood expands and report the cut in `bounds` as `max_hops` is reported. Bound traverse's `_neighbourhood` work by `limit`, not only its output.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced at up to 1,024 entities (larger-graph timings in the reports were not re-run). Related: bug-459 (whose hop cap does not bound this work), bug-534.
issues.fix_note: _neighbourhood stops expanding at NEIGHBOURHOOD_MAX_ENTITIES, keeping the entities reached by the most recent relations. walk() reports a step onto an unexpanded entity as max_hops. Reverting the cap turns tests/test_2611a2_x15.py::test_the_walk_reads_no_more_entities_than_the_bound_and_says_it_cut and ::test_traverse_expands_no_more_entities_than_the_bound red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The block index build holds roughly 90-100 bytes per block row in Python lists while the file needs about 28 bytes of metadata per row. Only the bits are streamed to a temp file; the eight metadata columns are appended to Python lists of int objects (cpersona/block_index.py:318, eight appends per row at :351-358) and converted with `np.asarray` only after the whole scan (block_index.py:387-393). At the 3,480,069-block corpus the upgrade notes describe, that is about 350 MB of lists plus roughly 100 MB of array copies, held in the server process during a queue build that recurs every 35,000 change-log rows (`LIVE_ROW_BOUND`, block_index.py:83), with the feature on by default. This is a transient memory peak, not a correctness defect; it was estimated from the code and an allocation measurement of the same append pattern, not re-measured against a live build.
issues.fix_sketch: Write the metadata columns as fixed-width arrays during the scan (preallocated numpy arrays or `array.array`, or per-column temp files like the bits), instead of accumulating Python int lists and converting at the end.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced against a live build. Related: bug-535 (the same build function).
issues.fix_note: _write_rows holds its eight per-row columns in typed array.array buffers instead of lists of Python ints, about 57 instead of 125 bytes a row measured over the whole build. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x15.py::test_the_index_build_holds_its_columns_compactly red.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test pins the within-record tie-break of the Hamming fallback. `_collapse` (cpersona/blocks.py:1275-1285) represents a record by its best block, with ties at equal distance going to the lower block index (line 1283), as the documented order of distance, kind, parent id, block index requires. Hamming distances are small integers, so equal-distance blocks of one record are common, yet inverting the tie-break to prefer the later block leaves the block tests green. The code is correct today; a regression would silently change the reserved row's `match_reason.block`. The cosine counterpart at line 1382 is pinned by `test_equal_cosines_go_by_kind_parent_and_block` in tests/test_blocks_rerank.py, and no Hamming equivalent exists.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test that gives two blocks of one record the same Hamming distance from the query and asserts the lower block index represents the record, mirroring the existing cosine tie-break test.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code and a surviving mutant; no defect in the shipped behavior, only the missing regression test.
issues.fix_note: Test-only: three blocks of one record tie at Hamming distance 1 and the lowest block index must represent the record; inverting the tie-break in _collapse (-block_index) turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The dedup_msg_id_index repair always keeps the newest colliding row as the survivor, whatever the lock state. cpersona/checks.py:1686-1696 blanks msg_id only on unlocked rows whose id is not `MAX(id)` of their (agent_id, project_id, msg_id) group (survivor subquery at :1691). When the OLDER collider is locked and the newer one is unlocked, neither row is blanked, the CREATE UNIQUE INDEX fails on every run, and check_health keeps reporting the critical dedup_msg_id_index_missing finding with a fix_error. Keeping the locked row as survivor and blanking the unlocked newer one would build the index without touching any locked row. The docstring (:1645-1652) says this check exists because the finding was otherwise permanent, yet this collision shape stays permanent and write-time msg_id dedup stays off store-wide. Needs a legacy pre-v12 collision with an older locked row. The v12 migration uses the same MAX(id) rule (cpersona/database.py:1380-1397).
issues.pattern: SELECT COALESCE\(MAX\(CASE WHEN locked != 0 THEN id END\), MAX\(id\)\)
issues.fix_sketch: Choose the survivor per collision group by preferring a locked row (for example order by locked DESC, id DESC) and blank only the unlocked non-survivors; report fix_error only when two or more colliders in one group are locked. Apply the same rule to the v12 migration.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-145 (the repair this refines), bug-098 (locked rows are never altered), bug-639 (missing test for the locked guard).
issues.fix_note: The msg_id collision repair keeps a locked row's msg_id when its group has one (else the newest) and blanks the unlocked rest, so an older locked collider no longer blocks the index forever. Reverting the survivor to MAX(id) turns tests/test_2611a2_x08.py::test_msg_id_repair_keeps_the_locked_collider_and_blanks_the_newer_one red.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test pins the `locked = 0` guard in the dedup_msg_id_index repair. cpersona/checks.py:1688 restricts the cross-agent msg_id blanking to unlocked rows, as the docstring at :1650-1652 promises (locked rows are left alone and a locked collider surfaces via fix_error). The existing tests seed only unlocked colliders, so replacing the guard with an always-true condition leaves the suite green. Under that mutation, check_health(fix=True) silently blanks a locked row's msg_id, in a repair that is declared cross-agent and can reach other agents' rows, and reports fixed=True. Reproduced: the mutation changes behaviour this way and no test fails. The production code at this commit is correct.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test that drops idx_memories_dedup_msg_id, seeds an older locked and a newer unlocked collider under one (agent, project, msg_id), runs check_health(fix=True, checks=['dedup_msg_id_index']), and asserts that the locked row keeps its msg_id and that the issue reports the failed CREATE through fix_error. Update the expected outcome if bug-638 changes the survivor rule.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced by a mutation probe. Related: bug-098 (locked rows are never altered by repairs), bug-638 (survivor choice in the same repair).
issues.fix_note: Already settled on 1860476 by commit c4c6351, which added tests/test_2611a2_x08.py. Its two-locked-colliders test fails when the locked = 0 guard in check_dedup_msg_id_index's UPDATE is replaced by 1 = 1: the second locked row is blanked, the CREATE succeeds and fixed is reported True.

issues.summary: (LOW) The fresh-connection confirmation added for bug-439 builds an unescaped SQLite URI. cpersona/checks.py:1724 calls `aiosqlite.connect(f"file:{path}?mode=ro", uri=True)` with the raw DB path. For a path containing '%', SQLite percent-decodes it, the open fails, the helper returns None (:1725-1726), and check_sqlite_integrity keeps the stale-cache 'malformed' messages from the shared connection as a critical sqlite_integrity_failure for an intact file (the false positive bug-439 was meant to suppress). For a path containing '?', SQLite cuts the path at the first '?', `mode=ro` is lost in a junk parameter, the default read-write-create mode applies, and a new empty database file is created at the truncated path; quick_check on that empty file returns ok, so check_sqlite_integrity returns no finding (:1748-1750) and would also hide a genuine corruption, while leaving a stray file behind. Both cases need an unusual DB path.
issues.fix_sketch: Percent-encode the path before building the URI (for example urllib.parse.quote on the absolute path) or build it with pathlib's as_uri, so '%', '?' and '#' reach SQLite as literal path characters and mode=ro always applies.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code plus a standalone SQLite URI experiment, not reproduced through check_health. Related: bug-439 (the confirmation step this affects).
issues.fix_note: The fresh-connection quick_check builds its read-only URI with Path.as_uri(), which percent-encodes '%', '?' and '#', so the confirmation opens the server's own file. Reverting to the interpolated f-string turns tests/test_2611a2_x08.py::test_quick_check_confirmation_opens_a_path_that_needs_escaping red.

issues.summary: (LOW) check_invalid_source_type and check_anonymous_source still turn a failed count query into a clean result. cpersona/checks.py:2394-2403 wraps the invalid-source count in `try ... except Exception: return []`, and :2550-2573 does the same around the anonymous and unattributed counts. Any operational failure (a locked or interrupted read, an I/O error) is reported exactly like a clean corpus, and because the exception never reaches the runner, no check_crashed finding is synthesised (:3645). This contradicts the rationale recorded for bug-380 in the sibling check_invalid_json (:1818-1821), which removed the same pattern. The bug-144 json_valid ordering removes the malformed-JSON trigger but not other query errors. Confirmed by reading the code; a query failure is a rare condition.
issues.fix_sketch: Drop the blanket except in both checks so a query failure reaches the runner and becomes a check_crashed finding, as bug-380 did for check_invalid_json.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The anchor is the guarded invalid-source count; the anonymous_source site is the `anon = (` block in the same file. Related: bug-380, bug-354, bug-355 (the same pattern removed from sibling checks), bug-144.
issues.fix_note: check_invalid_source_type's count is no longer wrapped in except Exception: return [] (the same for both anonymous_source counts), so a failed query reaches the runner as check_crashed. Restoring the swallow turns tests/test_2611a2_x08.py::test_a_failed_count_is_reported_as_a_crashed_check red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Agent-scoped vector_index and coarse_index findings report row counts for the whole store. check_vector_index builds `all_axes = isolation_where(agent_id=None)` (cpersona/checks.py:2801) and reports `indexed_rows` and `rows_still_present` computed over every agent (:2834-2848); check_coarse_index does the same for coarse_index_rows_missing (:3016-3028) and reports `rows_read_exactly` from `rows_read_exactly(db, index, "memories", all_axes)` (:3033), whereas the vector twin scopes that tail count to the caller (:2869). Report-only check_health needs only read on the caller's agent, so a client scoped to one agent can learn the store-wide embedded-row count once an index is built and any agent has deleted an indexed row. This is the size disclosure bug-058 and bug-062 removed elsewhere; the in-code justification (:2831-2833, 'a count of rows is a size rather than corpus content') contradicts the bug-062 rule as stated at :2637-2638. Confirmed by reading the code; only an aggregate count leaks.
issues.fix_sketch: Compute the live and tail counts with the caller's isolation scope (as check_vector_index's tail already does), or withhold the store-wide figures from agent-scoped callers and report them only on the global sweep. index.count is inherently store-wide, so it should be omitted for scoped callers.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-058 and bug-062 (agent-scoped counts), bug-549 (the same count is also miscomputed). Re-anchored with bug-514, which removed rows_still_present (and the counts behind it) from both findings; coarse_index_tail_grown still reports indexed_rows and rows_read_exactly over every agent.
issues.fix_note: check_coarse_index counts the rows read exactly in the checked scope, and both index checks report indexed_rows through _indexed_rows_in_scope (the agent's rows in the file). Reverting either to the store-wide figure turns tests/test_2611a2_x08.py::test_agent_scoped_coarse_index_finding_counts_that_agents_rows (or the vector twin) red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The coarse index built by check_health(fix=true) is published from the fix run's uncommitted transaction. `check_coarse_index` calls `build_coarse_index` on the `transaction()` connection (cpersona/checks.py:3058, cpersona/maintenance_handlers.py:148), so the build sees rows that earlier checks in the same run deleted (for example `duplicate_content`), and `os.replace` publishes the file (cpersona/coarse_index.py:217) before the transaction commits. If the run then rolls back (cancellation, client timeout or a crash before the commit), the deleted rows return to the database but are missing from the published index, below its watermark and outside its excluded set, so coarse search never offers them. `check_coarse_index` cannot see the gap: its only shrink test is `live_indexed < index.count` (checks.py:3023), and here the live count is larger. Reproduced with a fix run over duplicate_content, coarse_index and block_index.
issues.fix_sketch: Do not publish a derived file from inside an uncommitted transaction: build after the commit on a read snapshot (the bug-550 fix), or stage the built file and rename it into place only after `transaction()` commits.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. Shares its root and its fix with bug-550.
issues.fix_note: Fixed with bug-550: check_health(fix=true) no longer builds the coarse index inside its transaction. The coarse repair runs after the run commits, on a snapshot of committed rows, with the vector change log turned on in a commit of its own first, so a run that rolls back never publishes a file. tests/test_2611a2_w08.py::test_bug643_a_fix_run_that_rolls_back_leaves_no_coarse_file_that_hides_a_row turns red if the build moves back into the run.

issues.summary: (LOW) `check_block_index` is effectively untested. The only coverage is the generic repairable-count seeder (tests/test_255_repairable_contract.py), which asserts that a `block_log_without_index` issue exists with repairable 1. Nothing asserts that the fix actually stops the change log (cpersona/checks.py:3099), that the check is silent when the log is off (checks.py:3088-3089), or any enabled-path verdict: unusable, absent, or behind after a `PRAGMA schema_version` change (checks.py:3123). Reproduced: replacing the fix with `issue["fixed"] = True`, removing the log-off early return, and removing the schema-cookie comparison each left the suite's failure set unchanged.
issues.fix_sketch: Add tests that assert `block_log_clock.logging` is 0 after fix=true, an empty result when the log is off, and each enabled-path verdict (absent, unusable, behind after a schema_version change, silent when current).
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced by mutation. The code is correct today; this entry is the missing regression coverage.
issues.fix_note: New tests pin check_block_index: the fix turns block_log_clock.logging to 0 and empties record_block_changes; the check is silent with the index and the log both off; with the index on it reports absent, unusable (bad magic) and behind after a PRAGMA schema_version change, and is silent on a fresh build. Replacing the fix with issue["fixed"] = True turns the first test red.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test covers the chmod-failure path of `check_file_permissions`. On fix, an `OSError` from `os.chmod` is recorded as `fixed: False` plus `fix_error` (cpersona/checks.py:3217-3223) so that one unwritable path does not cost the rest of the repair pass. The tests cover fix success, never-widen, the directory case and platform gating, but none makes `os.chmod` raise, so a regression that re-raises (aborting the check, rolling back its savepoint and leaving the remaining widened files unreported and unnarrowed) would pass the suite. Confirmed by reading the code and tests; not reproduced.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test that monkeypatches `os.chmod` to raise `OSError` for one of two widened files and asserts `fixed: False` with a `fix_error` for that file while the other file is still reported and narrowed.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading. Related to bug-289. The code is correct today; this entry is the missing regression coverage.
issues.fix_note: A new test makes os.chmod refuse the first of two widened owned files and asserts the first is reported fixed False with an EPERM fix_error while the second is reported fixed True and narrowed to 0600. It turns red when the except branch re-raises, and also when it stops the pass early.

issues.summary: (LOW) The missing_blocks health check reads every in-scope record's full text and runs the pure-Python divider on it without yielding the event loop. `check_missing_blocks` (cpersona/checks.py:3435) calls `blocks.records_without_current_blocks`, which does one unpaged `SELECT id, <text>` of the whole scope (cpersona/blocks.py:534) and then, in a loop with no await, calls `segment()` for every record without a current block set (blocks.py:558). A single-block record never has a block set by design, so those records are divided again on every run, as is every record during a backfill backlog or after an embedding-model change. The loop blocks every other request on the server for the whole pass, which grows linearly with corpus text, and a fix run pays it twice (prefetch, then the residual re-run). Confirmed by reading the code; not reproduced.
issues.pattern: out\.extend\(await asyncio\.to_thread\(_divisible, kind, records, sets, bounds, keys\)\)
issues.fix_sketch: Page the scan and yield to the event loop between pages (or run the division off the loop), and avoid re-dividing records already known to be single-block, the way the bounded backfill sweep does.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading. The blocks counterpart of bug-500, which covers the token-count requests of missing_nodes but not this CPU stall.
issues.fix_note: records_without_current_blocks runs the currency test and the pure-Python divider in a worker thread (asyncio.to_thread), so check_health and the checkup CLI no longer hold the event loop for the whole pass. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x15.py::test_the_missing_blocks_scan_divides_records_off_the_event_loop red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The bug-361 contract is two-sided: a crashed check's writes roll back, and the rest of the fix run still commits (cpersona/checks.py:3611-3618). Only the first side is tested: every bug-361 test in tests/test_2512b2_handlers.py selects a single check (`checks=['invalid_json']`). Changing the per-check rollback at checks.py:3643 to `ROLLBACK TO health_run` would discard every earlier check's repair while their issues still report fixed, and no test would fail. Reproduced: on a store where `memory_annotation` repairs a row and a later `invalid_json` repair is forced to abort, the current code commits the annotation repair; the regression to whole-run rollback is not caught by the suite.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a multi-check fix-run test that forces a later check to crash and asserts that an earlier check's repair is committed.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. Missing coverage for the bug-361 fix; the code is correct today.
issues.fix_note: A new test runs do_check_health(fix=True, checks=['memory_annotation','invalid_json']) with a trigger that aborts invalid_json's metadata write. It asserts that only invalid_json crashed, that memory_annotation's content rewrite is committed, and that invalid_json's half-written source is rolled back. Changing the per-check ROLLBACK TO "{savepoint}" to ROLLBACK TO health_run turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) deep_check's anonymous_source repair takes any leading bracketed token as the speaker's name. `deep_anonymous_source` (cpersona/checks.py:3731) selects User rows with an empty id and name and matches `_USERNAME_PREFIX_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^\[(.+?)\]\s")` (checks.py:137) against the content; on fix=true it writes `match.group(1)` into `source.name` (checks.py:3752-3766). Content that begins with a Markdown checkbox, a date stamp or a log level, such as `[x] `, `[2026-10-01] ` or `[WARN] `, is therefore attributed to a user named `x`, `2026-10-01` or `WARN`, and later per-speaker reasoning treats that token as a person. Confirmed by reading the code; not reproduced.
issues.fix_sketch: Narrow the recovery to the annotation format CPersona itself writes (for example `[Memory from <name>]`) or reject tokens that look like checkboxes, dates or log levels, and leave the rest reported as unrecoverable.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading.
issues.fix_note: deep_anonymous_source recovers a speaker only through _speaker_from_prefix, which rejects checkboxes, dates and times, log levels, CPersona's own labels and admonitions. Reverting to the bare ^\[(.+?)\]\s match turns tests/test_2611a2_x08.py::test_deep_anonymous_source_recovers_names_but_not_other_brackets red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The `never_calibrated` branch of `deep_calibration_staleness` is untested. With an embedding client, no calibration sidecar (`state is None`) and at least 50 embedded rows, the check returns `status: never_calibrated` (cpersona/checks.py:3900-3906). The operations runbook promises operators this status after a restore without the sidecar (docs/operations.md:44-45). Every staleness test either writes a sidecar or runs without a client and gets `not_applicable`, and no test mentions `never_calibrated`. A regression that changes the `>= 50` threshold or makes the branch return `ok` would hide an uncalibrated gate, and the suite would stay green.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test that installs a fake embedding client, stores 50 embedded rows (plus a 49-row control) with no sidecar on disk, and asserts `never_calibrated` at exactly 50 and `ok` below it.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code and tests, not reproduced. Related: bug-377.
issues.fix_note: A new parametrized test, with the fake embedding client and no sidecar on disk, asserts status ok at 49 embedded rows and never_calibrated (with embedded_rows and the calibrate_threshold hint) at exactly 50. Changing '>= 50' to '> 50' turns the 50 case red, and '>= 49' turns the 49 case red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The `stale_scoring_version` hint from `deep_calibration_staleness` says 'restart the server (it recalibrates automatically on boot)' (cpersona/checks.py:3923). The check's own docstring (checks.py:3882-3887) names the configuration where this status persists: `CPERSONA_AUTO_CALIBRATE` and `CPERSONA_CALIBRATE_ON_MODEL_CHANGE` both off. In that configuration a restart is a no-op. `ensure_calibrated_on_startup` returns `noop` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2231-2250), and its warning says `deep_check` will keep reporting `stale_scoring_version` until calibration is enabled or run manually. An operator who follows the hint restarts and gets the same status and the same hint again, while recall stays on the heuristic gate.
issues.fix_sketch: Make the hint depend on the boot configuration. When recalibration on boot is disabled, say to enable `CPERSONA_CALIBRATE_ON_MODEL_CHANGE` and restart, or to run an all-agent calibration that keeps other agents' state. Keep the restart advice only when boot recalibration is on.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-184, and bug-554 (the manual calibration route drops `set_recall_precision` overrides).
issues.fix_note: The stale_scoring_version hint names a restart only when the configuration lets boot recalibrate (CPERSONA_AUTO_CALIBRATE or CPERSONA_CALIBRATE_ON_MODEL_CHANGE on); with both off it says a restart repairs nothing and names CPERSONA_CALIBRATE_ON_MODEL_CHANGE=true. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u11.py::test_stale_scoring_hint_does_not_promise_a_restart_when_boot_will_not_recalibrate red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `deep_unnormalized_content` and `deep_embedding_norm` report a scan that read every row as incomplete when a table holds exactly the cap. Both read with `LIMIT CAP` and report `complete = all(n < CAP ...)`: `NORMALIZATION_SCAN_CAP` at cpersona/checks.py:4057-4061 and :4095, and `_NORM_SAMPLE_ROWS = 2000` at checks.py:4154-4158 and :4185. At exactly CAP rows the count is the total but is labelled a floor, which contradicts the docstrings ('so a floor is not read as a total'). bug-376 fixed the same boundary in `check_invalid_source_type` by reading CAP+1 rows (checks.py:2417-2426). The error is conservative and occurs only at exact equality.
issues.fix_sketch: Read CAP+1 rows in both scans, cap the processed rows at CAP, and set `complete` from whether the extra row exists, as `check_invalid_source_type` does.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The second site is checks.py:4185 (`_NORM_SAMPLE_ROWS`). Related: bug-376.
issues.fix_note: deep_unnormalized_content (and deep_embedding_norm the same way) reads one row past the cap and calls a scan complete when no extra row came back, so exactly the cap is complete. Reverting to `n < CAP` turns tests/test_2611a2_x08.py::test_a_scan_of_exactly_the_cap_is_complete red.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test pins `unrecoverable` in `DEEP_FINDING_KEYS` (cpersona/checkup.py:48). `_deep_findings` keeps a deep-check result only when one of these keys is truthy, the result has an error, or its status is not ok or not_applicable. `deep_anonymous_source` reports only `recoverable` and `unrecoverable`, with no status. The bug-381 regression test uses recoverable=1 and unrecoverable=0, and the structural gate passes as long as any one key is readable. If `unrecoverable` were dropped from the set, a result of `{recoverable: 0, unrecoverable: 3}` would print nothing in the plain checkup output. That is the bug-381 symptom for exactly the rows that need a human, and the suite would stay green.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a case to the bug-381 test where the anonymous-source result has recoverable=0 and unrecoverable greater than 0, and assert that the plain-text output includes it.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code and tests, not reproduced. Related: bug-381.
issues.fix_note: A new test drives checkup._run (report-only, --deep, plain text) with do_check_health and do_deep_check stubbed to return anonymous_source {recoverable: 0, unrecoverable: 3}. It asserts the single deep[agent] line names it with "unrecoverable": 3 and leaves out a clean stale_profile result. Dropping 'unrecoverable' from DEEP_FINDING_KEYS turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Test-only. `_lost_since_build` (cpersona/coarse_search.py:350-357) correctly intersects the agent's NULL-embedding ids with the selected candidates, but no test would catch a regression to `return bool(rows)`. In the coarse test fixture (tests/test_coarse_search.py:108-115) the named unembedded hole receives an embedding after the build, so no NULL-embedding row remains in any test that asserts the index answered. Under that mutation every coarse test still passes, yet the index would refuse to answer whenever the agent has any unembedded row, and in the default auto cue mode (`live=False`) the remainder would silently become an empty `skipped` result. Confirmed by mutation; the production code is correct today.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test that keeps a never-embedded row (a named hole) present after the build and asserts that `coarse_candidates(..., live=False)` still answers from the index with the expected candidates.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; the coverage gap was confirmed by a mutation run, the production code is not defective.
issues.fix_note: Test added: with a build-named, still-unembedded row present, coarse_candidates answers from the index (live=False and live=True) with the reference candidates. Replacing the isin intersection in _lost_since_build with `return bool(rows)` turns it red ('skipped' != 'index').

issues.summary: (LOW) `CPERSONA_MAX_MEMORIES` is parsed without a clamp (cpersona/config.py:92), unlike the neighbouring scan settings that use `max(0, ...)`. With a negative value such as -1, which an operator may set to mean unlimited, the cue arm passes `start=MAX_MEMORIES` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2080-2083) to the coarse supplier, and `coarse_candidates` raises `ValueError` at cpersona/coarse_search.py:171-172. Nothing above it catches the error, so every recall that carries a `time_cue` fails in every cue mode except `off`, including the default auto. `far_list_enabled()` (cpersona/vector.py:562, `VECTOR_REACH > MAX_MEMORIES`) also becomes true at the default reach of 0. Reproduced on a fresh database with the local vector path.
issues.fix_sketch: Clamp `MAX_MEMORIES` at parse time, for example `max(1, ...)` with the usual malformed-value warning, as the neighbouring scan settings do, or refuse a negative value at startup.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced; the report claimed MEDIUM and the severity was lowered to LOW.
issues.fix_note: A scan window below one row falls back to the default 10000 with a warning, so a negative value can no longer reach the coarse supplier as a scan position or switch the far list on. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x12.py::test_a_scan_window_below_one_row_falls_back_and_says_so red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The reconstruct budget and tail-quote defaults are fixed numbers that do not follow the settings they are checked against, so changing one neighbouring setting stops startup over a default the operator never set. `RECONSTRUCT_DEFAULT_BUDGET` is a fixed 4000 (cpersona/config.py:303) and `RECONSTRUCT_TAIL_QUOTE_CHARS` a fixed 400 (config.py:291). `validate_reconstruct_counts` (config.py:333-360) raises when the unset default budget is below `CPERSONA_RECALL_PREVIEW_CHARS`, above a lowered `CPERSONA_RECONSTRUCT_MAX_BUDGET`, or when the unset tail exceeds a lowered `CPERSONA_RECONSTRUCT_QUOTE_CHARS`. Reproduced: `RECALL_PREVIEW_CHARS=5000` (valid in 2.5.x), `RECONSTRUCT_QUOTE_CHARS=300` (valid before the tail setting existed) and `RECONSTRUCT_MAX_BUDGET=3000` each make startup fail with an error that names the unset default.
