The count settings deliberately avoid this: an unset default count follows the maximum down (config.py:243-247). docs/configuration.md does not mention the coupling.
issues.fix_sketch: When unset, derive the defaults the way the default count is derived: default budget = min(max(4000, preview floor), max budget) and tail quote = min(400, quote chars). Keep the refusal for explicitly set values, and document the coupling in docs/configuration.md and the upgrade notes.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced; the reports claimed up to MEDIUM and the severity was lowered to LOW. Related to bug-457, whose fix aimed to keep every configuration that starts today starting.
issues.fix_note: Unset reconstruct budget defaults follow the preview tier up and the maximum down, and the unset tail follows the quote size down, so changing one neighbour no longer refuses startup over a default nobody set. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x12.py::test_raising_only_the_preview_tier_still_starts (and the four sibling tests) red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Boolean feature flags read any value other than `true` as false, with no warning. Each flag is computed as `os.environ.get(KEY, "true").lower() == "true"`, so for the default-on flags the common affirmative spellings `1`, `yes` and `on` turn the feature off, the opposite of what the operator asked. Sites include `FTS_ENABLED` (cpersona/config.py:598), `DEGRADED_ADVISORY_ENABLED` (:683), `TASK_QUEUE_ENABLED` (:685), `UPDATE_CHECK_ENABLED` (:703), `SCOPE_STATS_CACHE_ENABLED` (:716), `BLOCK_BUILD_ENABLED` (:746), `BLOCK_INDEX_ENABLED` (:771), `STORE_BLOB` (:811), `CALIBRATE_ON_MODEL_CHANGE` (:876), `FUSED_GATE_ENABLED` (:885) and `AUTOCUT_ENABLED` (:919). For example, `CPERSONA_FTS_ENABLED=1` silently disables the keyword channel. This contradicts the module's own rule for word-valued settings (config.py:22-41), that an unreadable value falls back to the documented default and says so. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_sketch: Parse the flags through one boolean helper that accepts the usual true and false spellings and falls back to the documented default with a warning for anything else, as `_parse_choice` does for word-valued settings.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading, not reproduced. Related to bug-133 and bug-321 (malformed-value fallback rule).
issues.fix_note: Boolean flags are read through _parse_bool, which accepts the usual spellings of true and false and warns and keeps the default on anything else, so CPERSONA_FTS_ENABLED=1 no longer turns the keyword channel off. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x12.py::test_the_usual_spellings_of_true_are_true red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Test-only. `cue.parse` correctly refuses a time cue whose `before` equals its `after` (cpersona/cue.py:139, `before <= after`), including the date-only case after='2026-08-02', before='2026-08-01', where a date-only `before` becomes the end of its day and so equals `after`. The only test of the 'later than' refusal (tests/test_recall_cue.py:56) uses a strictly earlier `before`, so relaxing the check to `before < after` would pass the suite. Under that regression the empty period would reach `period()`, become a short window, and the caller would get a revised cue instead of an error. Confirmed by reading the code and the tests; the production code is correct today.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a parse case with `before` equal to `after`, and the date-only pair one day apart in reverse, asserting the 'later than' refusal.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading, not reproduced. Related to bug-443 (time cue period bounds).
issues.fix_note: Test added: before == after, including the same instant in two offsets and the date-only pair one day apart in reverse, raises 'later than'. Relaxing cue.parse's `before <= after` to `<` turns all three red.

issues.summary: (LOW) A time cue instant with a non-UTC offset at the edge of the date range escapes as `OverflowError`. `_parse_instant` keeps the caller's offset (cpersona/cue.py:117), and with the `sure` margin of zero `period()` returns such a bound unchanged, so the bug-443 clipping does not apply. `sql_instant` (cue.py:257) then calls `astimezone(timezone.utc)`, which overflows for values such as `0001-01-01T00:00:00+05:00` or `9999-12-31T23:00:00-05:00`. The cue arm calls it with no guard (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2046), and recall and reconstruct catch only `TimeCueError` (cpersona/reconstruct.py:1524), so the tool returns a bare `date value out of range` error instead of the documented refusal shape or a clipped period. Confirmed by reading the code; the overflow in `sql_instant` was demonstrated directly, but the full tool path was not reproduced.
issues.fix_sketch: Normalise parsed instants to UTC with the same clipping as the period arithmetic, or make `sql_instant` clip to the representable range instead of raising, so an edge instant yields either a clipped period or a `TimeCueError` refusal.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading. It is an incomplete part of the bug-443 fix, which clipped period arithmetic but not the conversion to UTC.
issues.fix_note: sql_instant clips a bound whose offset carries its UTC instant past the representable range to the end it passed, as a margin that reaches past one is clipped (bug-443), so recall and reconstruct answer instead of failing with 'date value out of range'. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u13.py::test_a_cue_bound_past_the_range_is_clipped_to_the_end_it_passed and ::test_recall_with_an_out_of_range_time_cue_bound_answers red.

issues.summary: (LOW) docs/configuration.md:47 says `CPERSONA_PRIOR_FAR_WEIGHT=0` "is the reach turned off: the far region is not scanned", but that is not equivalent to turning the reach off when far seats are enabled. At weight 0 the far list is not used (`far_out=far_results if PRIOR_FAR_WEIGHT > 0 else None`, cpersona/memory_handlers.py:692), while `far_seats.scan_start()` still returns `max(vector.MAX_MEMORIES, vector.VECTOR_REACH)` (cpersona/far_seats.py:58). With CPERSONA_FAR_SEATS_ENABLED=true and a reach above the window, scan positions between CPERSONA_MAX_MEMORIES and CPERSONA_VECTOR_REACH are searched by no vector reader at all, so records there can be found only lexically; with CPERSONA_VECTOR_REACH=0 instead, the far seats start at the window. Needs two non-default settings (far seats are off by default) plus a reach above the window. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.pattern: takes the far list out of both fusions, so the region between the window and the reach is not scanned
issues.fix_sketch: Correct the sentence to say that weight 0 drops the far list from fusion but does not move where the far seats start, or make the far-seat scan start at the window when the far list is not used, and document whichever behaviour is chosen.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related to bug-470, which covered the weight's effect on fusion.
issues.fix_note: The CPERSONA_PRIOR_FAR_WEIGHT row now says 0 removes the far list from both fusions but does not move where the far seats start, and that with far seats on the reach is turned off with CPERSONA_VECTOR_REACH=0 (docs only, English and Japanese).

issues.summary: (LOW) Test gap, no shipped defect: `far_seats.seat_rows` correctly skips a row matched by the caller's content exclusion (cpersona/far_seats.py:164) and stops at SEATS rows inside a refill chunk (far_seats.py:161), and `ranked` rejects a stored vector whose width changed (far_seats.py:126), but no test pins any of the three. Dropping `or excluded(...)`, turning the inner `>=` into `>`, or replacing the width check with `True` each leaves every far-seat and time-cue test result unchanged. A regression could therefore seat a record recall(exclude_contents=...) asked to exclude, or seat three far rows where two places are reserved, with the suite green. Confirmed by reading the code and by mutation runs.
issues.fix_sketch: Add far-seat tests where the best coarse hit is an excluded record, where the first chunk is short and a refill would over-seat, and where a stored vector has the wrong width; each must fail under the corresponding mutant.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code and by mutation, the production code is correct.
issues.fix_note: Tests added for the exclusion skip (recall(exclude_contents=[best far record]) seats the next two instead), the refill bound (a dead first hit plus three live ones seats exactly SEATS), and the width recheck (a candidate rewritten at double width after the coarse search is dropped, not crashed on). Dropping `or excluded(...)` in seat_rows turns the exclusion test red. `>` for the inner `>=` and `True` for the width check turn the other two red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `fileperms.owned_paths()` says it lists every path the package places, but it omits the coarse index files (`{db}.memories.coarseindex` / `{db}.episodes.coarseindex`, cpersona/coarse_index.py:83-85) and the block index file (`{db}.blocks.blockindex`, cpersona/block_index.py:103-105); its only index entries are `vector_index.index_path(table)` for memories and episodes (cpersona/fileperms.py:225-227). check_file_permissions iterates only owned_paths() (cpersona/checks.py:3171), so after a data directory is copied or restored at mode 0644, check_health reports and fix=true narrows the database, WAL/SHM, sidecars and vector index files but never reports or narrows the coarse and block index files, which hold embedding sign bits and agent/project/channel codes. Fresh builds write these files owner-only, so only copied-in files are exposed. Confirmed by reading the code.
issues.fix_sketch: Add `coarse_index.index_path(table)` for both tables and `block_index.index_path()` to owned_paths(), and add a test that every module that writes through fileperms.open_private has its path in the list.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The list was introduced by bug-296 before the coarse and block indexes existed.
issues.fix_note: owned_paths lists the coarse index files for memories and episodes and the block index file, so a readable copy is reported and narrowed by the file_permissions check. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x12.py::test_owned_paths_names_the_coarse_and_block_index_files red.

issues.summary: (LOW) A misconfigured embedding backend is delivered on get_session_findings at severity info although check_health stamps it warn. bug-372 made `finding_kind` return `embedding_backend_misconfigured` as a delivery kind (cpersona/findings.py:166-167), but the static map has only `"embedding_backend_unreachable": "warn"` (findings.py:105), so `severity_for_kind` falls back to FALLBACK_SEVERITY info (findings.py:126-128) while checks.py:698-703 stamps the same issue warn. A consumer routing on severity treats degraded semantic recall as informational. Reproduced through do_get_session_findings with the misconfigured fault latched: kind embedding_backend_misconfigured, severity info, health_severity warn, while the unreachable twin is delivered as warn. Reachability is narrow because unsupported embedding modes are refused at startup, so the latch needs an http/api client whose transport is absent.
issues.fix_sketch: Add `"embedding_backend_misconfigured": "warn"` to `_TIER_KINDS`, and add a test that every kind `finding_kind` can return for a tiered check has an explicit FINDING_SEVERITY entry.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. A residual of bug-372, which added the kind without its severity.
issues.fix_note: The misconfigured embedding backend kind has a static warn severity like its unreachable twin, so it is no longer delivered at the info fallback. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x12.py::test_a_misconfigured_backend_is_delivered_as_warn_like_its_twin red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Test gap, no shipped defect: the `if kind not in capped` de-duplication in `deliver()` (cpersona/findings.py:247-248) is never exercised. Every capping case, in the conformance trimming fixtures and in tests/test_superauditor_findings.py (3 findings with limit 2, 2 findings with limit 1), overflows a kind by exactly one, so the overflow branch runs at most once per kind. Removing the de-duplication leaves the suite green, while a database with three findings of one kind under per_kind_limit=1 would then list that kind twice in capped_kinds and in the rendered summary. Confirmed by reading the code and the fixtures.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a delivery test (and a conformance case) where one kind overflows its cap by two or more, asserting the kind appears once in capped_kinds.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code and test fixtures, the production code is correct.
issues.fix_note: A new test delivers two kinds that each overflow per_kind_limit=1 by two (interleaved). It asserts capped_kinds == ['stale_pending', 'duplicate_pending'], with each kind named once, and that the summary names stale_pending exactly twice (once in kinds, once in the cap sentence). Replacing 'if kind not in capped:' with 'if True:' turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The lock contract does not say whether operator re-scoping tools may move a locked memory, and they do. docs/behavior-contracts.md:297 says `lock_memory` protects a row from deletion and editing, while both `migrate_channel_axis` UPDATEs (cpersona/maintenance_handlers.py:519-523 and :540-543) re-channel locked rows with no `locked = 0` guard, and with `globalize_unrecoverable=true` a locked row moves to channel '' (visible from every channel). `merge_memories` with move likewise relocates a locked row to another agent. Reproduced: two locked `discord` rows came out as channel `111222333` and '' with the lock flag kept. The behaviour itself is defensible: the only edit path the lock gates is `update_memory`, which changes content, no user tool edits channel, and skipping locked rows would strand them on the bridge channel after the default flip, defeating the section's own advice to lock what must never be lost. The defect is the undocumented gap, not the migration.
issues.pattern: blocks its deletion; it does not pin the
issues.fix_sketch: Do not add `locked = 0` to the migration. State in behavior-contracts.md section 9 (and in the bug-098 note) that a lock freezes content and blocks deletion but does not pin the isolation axes, and that operator re-scoping tools (`migrate_channel_axis`, `merge_memories` move) relocate locked rows with the flag preserved; optionally report the number of locked rows moved in the migration output.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Related to bug-098 (the `locked = 0` guard on health-check fixers) and bug-569 (the same migration leaves associations behind).
issues.fix_note: Behaviour-contracts §9 (EN/JA) and the lock_memory description now state that a lock makes delete_memory and update_memory refuse the row but does not pin its agent or channel: migrate_channel_axis and merge_memories move relocate locked rows with the lock kept, and delete_agent_data removes them with the agent. Docs only; the open anchor 'protects a row from deletion and editing' is gone.

issues.summary: (LOW) The `repairs_skipped` disclosure that `migrate_channel_axis` makes under no-persist has no test. docs/tools.md:140-141 says the tool is forced into dry-run and reports `repairs_skipped`, and the code does so at cpersona/maintenance_handlers.py:562-564 (`if paused and not dry_run:` sets `repairs_skipped` and `repairs_skip_reason`). The only migrate assertions check `dry_run` (tests/test_257_session_key_stage2.py:218-221); every `repairs_skipped` assertion in the suite covers `check_health` or `deep_check` (tests/test_no_persist.py:201-218, tests/test_257_session_key_stage2.py:208-214). Removing the block leaves the whole suite green, and a caller that branches on `repairs_skipped` would then read a no-persist downgrade as a requested dry run. The code is correct today; only the regression guard is missing.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test that calls `migrate_channel_axis(dry_run=False)` from a paused session and asserts `repairs_skipped is True` with a skip reason, plus the control that an unpaused caller and an explicit `dry_run=True` call carry no `repairs_skipped` key.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code and the tests.
issues.fix_note: New test calls do_migrate_channel_axis(dry_run=False) from a paused session and asserts repairs_skipped is True with a no-persist reason and the row unmoved; replacing `if paused and not dry_run:` with `if False:` turns it red. A control test asserts the key is absent for an explicit dry run and an unpaused run.

issues.summary: (LOW) The legacy `message` form of `store` stores an empty timestamp verbatim, while the flat form treats an empty timestamp as omitted and stores the current time. `do_store` reads `message.get("timestamp", now)` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:199), which substitutes the default only when the key is absent, and the message schema accepts `""` (cpersona/server.py:1099); the flat form goes through `_flat_message`, which sets the key only `if timestamp:` (server.py:237-238). A row stored with timestamp '' is then outside every timestamp-based mechanism: the time-cue period predicates never match it, the confidence span skips it, and the `invalid_timestamp` check and repair both filter `timestamp != ''` (cpersona/checks.py:1871, also :1882 and :1900), so it is never reported or repaired from `created_at`. It needs a legacy-form client that sends an explicit empty string.
issues.fix_sketch: Treat an empty or missing `message.timestamp` the same way the flat form does and substitute the current time, so both forms agree. Optionally let the `invalid_timestamp` check report rows whose timestamp is '' so existing rows can be repaired from `created_at`.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code. The broader lack of bounds and format validation on the timestamp field is bug-570.
issues.fix_note: do_store_boundary drops an empty timestamp from the legacy message form so it reads as omitted, matching _flat_message; reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_x05.py::test_an_empty_legacy_timestamp_means_now_as_in_the_flat_form red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The project-visible dedup that `store` performs (bug-106) is not protected against concurrent writers across buckets. The msg_id and content probes run on a plain read connection (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:269-294) before the awaited embedding call (:310-312), and the INSERT happens later under `transaction()` (:327-331). A write to project `X` probes `X` and the global pool, and a write to '' probes only ''; if both probe before either inserts, both pass, and because their (project_id, channel) differ the exact-bucket UNIQUE index (cpersona/database.py:1068-1069), which the comment at memory_handlers.py:262-264 names as the race backstop, lets both rows in. `recall` in `X` then returns the same text twice, the duplicate bug-106 set out to prevent. The channel axis behaves the same way. It needs simultaneous stores of identical text to different buckets.
issues.pattern: db, agent_id, project_id, channel, msg_id, content, own_source_id, beyond_bucket=True
issues.fix_sketch: Repeat the project-visible dedup probe inside the write transaction immediately before the INSERT (the write lock serialises it against other stores), keeping the earlier probe only as a fast path before the embedding call.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code. Related to bug-106 (project-visible dedup) and bug-010 (the exact-bucket race backstop).
issues.fix_note: do_store re-runs the dedup probe inside its write transaction for the part of the γ-visible scope the exact-bucket unique indexes cannot see (the global project and unscoped channel), so a global copy committed after the first probe answers the bucket write; reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_x05.py::test_a_global_copy_landing_mid_store_answers_a_bucket_write and ::test_concurrent_bucket_and_global_stores_never_insert_after_the_global_copy red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `store`'s `INSERT OR IGNORE` also swallows NOT NULL violations and reports them as duplicates. The OR IGNORE was added to absorb the bug-010 UNIQUE race, but SQLite's IGNORE resolution skips a row that violates NOT NULL too, and both `timestamp` and `channel` are NOT NULL (cpersona/database.py:388 and :391). `do_store` does not coerce `channel` (unlike `project_id`) and takes `timestamp` verbatim (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:199), so a library caller passing `channel=None`, or a message with `timestamp: None`, gets no row written and the response `ok:true, result:'skipped', reason:'duplicate (unique index)'` (memory_handlers.py:340-342), which states a false cause; the caller treats the memory as stored. MCP callers are kept off this path by the input schema, so it needs a library caller that ignores the type contract.
issues.fix_sketch: Coerce or refuse null `channel` and `timestamp` in `do_store` before the INSERT (a `rejected` result for an unusable value), so the OR IGNORE branch can only be reached by a real UNIQUE collision; optionally confirm the collision with a probe before reporting it as a duplicate.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code. Related to bug-010, which introduced the OR IGNORE.
issues.fix_note: do_store settles every value bound into a NOT NULL column before its INSERT OR IGNORE (timestamp None -> now, id None -> '', channel coerced like project_id, agent_id None refused), so IGNORE can only absorb a uniqueness conflict; reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x05.py::test_a_none_timestamp_is_an_omitted_timestamp and ::test_a_none_channel_is_the_default_channel red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Under `CPERSONA_VECTOR_SEARCH_MODE=remote` the `/index` and `/search` URLs are derived with `rsplit("/", 1)`, which drops the query string of the configured embedding URL and mishandles a trailing slash. The store path builds the index URL at cpersona/memory_handlers.py:359, and the same derivation sits at cpersona/vector.py:131 (index upsert) and :437 (remote search) and at five sites in cpersona/admin_handlers.py (474, 562, 743, 805, 2437). The vendored embedding client derives its own sibling routes with `_sibling_route` (cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/embedding_client.py:143), which keeps the query, and in http mode a query-string credential is the only way to authenticate. Reproduced against a mock transport that requires `api_key`: `/embed` and `/capabilities` kept the key while the `/index` push and `/search` call lost it and got 401. The failure is logged at warning on every write and search, and under the default `CPERSONA_STORE_BLOB=true` the local vector is still written and recall falls back to local search; semantic recall of new rows is lost only with `STORE_BLOB=false`. The trailing-slash variant (`.../embed/` producing `.../embed/index`) was not run end to end.
issues.fix_sketch: Derive every remote sibling route (`/index`, `/search` and the admin sites) with the vendored `_sibling_route` helper so the query string is kept and a trailing slash is handled. Refuse, or warn once, when the configured URL does not end in `/embed`.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Related to bug-425, which treats credentials in the embedding URL's query string as a supported configuration.
issues.fix_note: Every remote index-service URL (index, search, remove, purge) is derived by vector.remote_route through the embedding client's _sibling_route, keeping the configured query string and handling a trailing slash; a URL not ending in /embed yields no route, no remote call and one warning. Reverting to the last-slash cut turns tests/test_2611a2_x07.py::test_store_and_search_reach_the_service_with_the_configured_query and ::test_every_remote_side_effect_keeps_the_configured_query red with requests that lost api_key.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test pins which session a store or archive build is attributed to. `do_store` and `do_archive_episode` pass the caller's resolved session key to `nodes.queue_build` / `blocks.queue_build` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:411, :419, :4210, :4218), and the task queue's drain uses that key to decide whose no-persist pause discards the build. Replacing the key with the shared keyless bucket (`'transport'`) at any of the four call sites leaves the full suite green, because the attribution tests exercise the queue directly rather than these call sites. A regression would let a keyless caller's pause discard a declared session's block or node build (leaving the record without derived blocks or nodes until a backfill), and stop the session's own pause from dropping it.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a handler-level test per call site that stores (and archives) under a declared session key while a different session is paused, and asserts the queued build carries the caller's key, so the build survives the other session's pause and is dropped by its own.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code (the four call sites and the drain's pause check); not reproduced as a separate probe.
issues.fix_note: A handler-level test stores and archives under a declared session key and asserts that both queued builds are attributed to that key: the caller's pause governs them and a keyless pause does not. Replacing key with 'transport' at any of the four queue_build call sites in memory_handlers.py turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) In the cascade path the profile row is appended before the keyword stage and counted against the limit (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:523-525: `_append_profile_rows` then `remaining = max(0, limit - len(results))`), so it always takes a seat and, after the final `results.reverse()` (:2914), lands in the last position. Every empty-query recall takes this path whatever the recall mode, and by the same code so does every non-empty recall under CPERSONA_RECALL_MODE=cascade. Reproduced on a fresh database with 60 memories and a profile under the default rrf mode: an empty-query recall with limit=5 returned 4 memories followed by the profile as the final element. docs/behavior-contracts.md:20-21 reserves the final element for the strongest match, and :265-267 says that above the pool threshold with confidence off profile rows sort last and are cut by `limit` when scored results fill it; here one memory inside the limit is dropped instead.
issues.pattern: remaining = max\(0, limit - sum\(1 for r in results if r.get\("id"\) != -1\)\)
issues.fix_sketch: Decide the contract for unscored and empty-query recall: either append the profile after the keyword stage in `_recall_cascade` so it is cut by `limit` and placed worst, as the profile contract says, or document that empty-query and cascade recalls reserve a slot for the profile.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. The fix needs a contract decision about where an unscored profile row belongs before code changes.
issues.fix_note: Contract rewritten plus a small fix (maintainer decision): the cascade's keyword stage no longer counts the profile row against limit, so a scope too small for the profile to pass the gate lists limit memories; where the profile passes, the cut to limit drops the extra keyword row and the listing is unchanged (limit - 1 memories, profile last). behavior-contracts sections 1 and 7 and architecture.md describe the empty-query listing. Pinned by tests/test_docs_behavioural_claims.py::test_the_profile_row_takes_no_memory_place_in_a_listing; counting the profile again turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `_propagation_seat_rows` reads the anchor's and every candidate's embedding with a single `id IN (...)` per table, one bound parameter per id and no chunking (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:1811-1820). The candidate count comes from a deeper ranking clamped only to RECALL_LIBRARY_MAX_LIMIT (default 10000, :1777), while the sibling id reads on the same path are split at `vector._ID_FETCH_CHUNK` for the 999-variable ceiling of SQLite builds older than 3.32. The read is not guarded, so with CPERSONA_RECALL_PROPAGATION_SEAT on and a raised CPERSONA_RECALL_DEPTH_FLOOR, a recall whose deeper ranking admits more ids than the build's variable limit fails with `too many SQL variables` instead of returning its answer without the seat. Reachable only with non-default settings.
issues.pattern: f"SELECT id, embedding FROM \{table\} WHERE id IN \(\{\{ph\}\}\) AND agent_id = \?",
issues.fix_sketch: Split the id list at `vector._ID_FETCH_CHUNK` as the other id reads on this path do, or cap the candidate list fed to the blob fetch; on failure skip the seat rather than failing the recall.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Same class as bug-301 and bug-318.
issues.fix_note: The propagation seat reads the anchor's and candidates' vectors through vector._fetch_rows_by_id, split at vector._ID_FETCH_CHUNK like every other id read on the recall, so a deep ranking no longer passes SQLite's variable limit and fails the whole recall. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x07.py::test_the_propagation_seat_reads_its_vectors_under_the_variable_ceiling red with 'too many SQL variables'.

issues.summary: (LOW) The channel exception in the block arm is untested. `_block_reserved_rows` lets a source-scoped recall see episodes when a channel is also set (`episodes_visible = not source_id or bool(channel)`, cpersona/memory_handlers.py:1901), the rule bug-080 fixed elsewhere for the grounding path. The only related test in tests/test_blocks_retrieval.py calls `do_recall` with `source_id` and no channel, so it pins only the suppression half; changing the line to `not source_id` would silently drop every channel-scoped episode from the block arm for a source-scoped caller with no test failing.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a block-retrieval test that recalls with both `source_id` and `channel` set and asserts the channel's long episode can be reserved, alongside the existing no-channel suppression test.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code and tests, not reproduced. Related: bug-080.
issues.fix_note: Test added: archives a long episode in a channel and recalls with source_id plus that channel under block reach; asserts the episode is reserved with signal 'block'. Mutation `episodes_visible = not source_id or bool(channel)` -> `episodes_visible = not source_id` turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The boundary of `_period_has_remainder` is untested. It runs `LIMIT 1 OFFSET ?` bound to `MAX_MEMORIES` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2010-2011), which is true exactly when the period holds more than MAX_MEMORIES embedded rows and decides whether a cued response carries the `left_out` remainder disclosure. The tests use either a cap far below the period size or a cap equal to the whole store, so the period never holds exactly MAX_MEMORIES rows; an off-by-one in the offset would either claim a period was not searched whole when nothing was left out, or drop the disclosure when one row was, with no test failing.
issues.fix_sketch: Add tests with a period of exactly MAX_MEMORIES embedded rows (no disclosure) and MAX_MEMORIES + 1 rows (disclosure) under CUE_COARSE_MODE=auto with no coarse index.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code and tests, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: Tests added for a cue period of exactly MAX_MEMORIES embedded rows (no remainder disclosure) and one past it (disclosure), under CUE_COARSE_MODE=auto with no coarse index. `LIMIT 1 OFFSET ?` -> `OFFSET ? - 1` reddens the first, `OFFSET ? + 1` the second.

issues.summary: (LOW) The cue arm's DEPTH bound is untested. `_search_cue_arm` cuts to `depth` in two places: the merged exact and remainder vector list (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2100, `merged[:depth]`) and the final fused list (:2169, `ordered[:depth]`), as cue.py documents ('The cue arm searches to its own depth, DEPTH, whatever the count'). No test seeds a period with more than DEPTH candidates, so removing either cut goes unnoticed; without them the cue arm can return rows ranked past DEPTH, which `do_recall` then treats as liftable, changing the order of a cued answer against the documented bound.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a cue test with more than DEPTH matching rows in the period (and one with a coarse remainder past MAX_MEMORIES) that asserts the cue arm returns at most DEPTH rows and that rows past DEPTH contribute no votes.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code and tests, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: Tests added that seed more candidates than cue.DEPTH: dropping `merged[:depth]` lets a vector rank past the depth vote and reorders the arm (red); dropping `ordered[:depth]` returns DEPTH + 1 rows (red in test_the_cue_arm_returns_no_more_than_its_depth).

issues.summary: (LOW) Nothing tests that recall lower-cases caller-supplied exclude_contents. `do_recall` builds `exclude_set = {c.strip().lower() ...}` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2412), and `_content_excluded` lower-cases only the stored content and compares it with the set entries as given (cpersona/utils.py:63-74). The recall tool forwards `exclude_contents` unchanged (cpersona/server.py:562), so that `.lower()` is the only step that lets a mixed-case entry match. Every do_recall-level test passes an all-lowercase entry, and the `_content_excluded` unit tests pass entries already lower-cased, so dropping `.lower()` at :2412 would leave the suite green while `recall(exclude_contents=['Apples and pears ...'])` stops excluding the stored turn it names.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a do_recall (or recall tool) test that stores a mixed-case record and passes its exact mixed-case text in exclude_contents, asserting the record is excluded.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-399. recall_with_context lower-cases its own list, which hides the gap on that path only.
issues.fix_note: Already pinned since the 2.6.11a2 exclusion work by tests/test_2611a2_w11.py::test_an_excluded_episode_stays_out_of_the_fusions, whose MEMORY constant starts with a capital; a dedicated test now passes the stored text in its own, upper and swapped case. Dropping `.lower()` from the exclude_set build turns both red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The quality gate's pool count ignores source_id, so in a source-scoped recall other sources' volume decides which candidates the gate admits. `do_recall` takes the count from `scope_stats.get_pool_counts(db, agent_id, project_id=project_id, channel=channel)` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2505-2507), whose signature has no source axis (cpersona/scope_stats.py:217), although the comment there and at memory_handlers.py:2501 says the counts are scoped like the recall itself and the recall rows are source-filtered. That count drives the adaptive min_score, the profile rule `memory_count >= 50` and the unscored-volume rule `memory_count >= 100`. `scope_stats.get_span` (cpersona/scope_stats.py:114) is source-free in the same way, so the confidence time span also spans other sources. No other source's rows are returned, so this is not a leak; only gate membership and ordering change for a source-scoped recall in a multi-user agent.
issues.fix_sketch: Decide whether source_id is a gate axis; if it is, pass it to get_pool_counts and get_span and key their cache by it, otherwise correct the comments that claim the counts follow the recall's scope.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-216, bug-107. The fix needs a scoring decision, since scoping the gate by source splits the cache and shrinks pools.

issues.summary: (LOW) The regression test for autocut after a gate rescue no longer exercises the guard it was written for. `test_rescue_survives_autocut_when_a_profile_row_is_present` (tests/test_gate_remediation.py:548) seeds one profile row and two rescued rows, and its vacuity assert counts the profile toward `AUTOCUT_MIN_RESULTS` (3). Since `_autocut` removes the id -1 sentinel before its size check (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:944-947), it sees two scored rows and returns the list whole, so dropping `not gate_fallback` from `if AUTOCUT_ENABLED and not gate_fallback:` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2708) cannot change the test's output. The guard is still needed: with three or more rescued non-profile rows and a confidence gap, autocut would cut the rescued set while the response reports gate_fallback=true.
issues.fix_sketch: Seed at least AUTOCUT_MIN_RESULTS rescued non-profile rows with a large confidence gap between them, and count only non-profile rows in the vacuity assert.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-183, bug-335.
issues.fix_note: The test now seeds three rescued non-profile rows, one at a chosen backfilled cosine of 0.29 under a calibrated per-agent vector threshold of 0.6 so it scores above the other two, counts only non-profile rows toward AUTOCUT_MIN_RESULTS and checks the rescued scores hold a gap >= AUTOCUT_MIN_GAP_RATIO; dropping `not gate_fallback` from `if AUTOCUT_ENABLED and not gate_fallback:` turns it red (autocut cuts the two zero-score rescued rows).

issues.summary: (LOW) The guard that keeps keyword seats off a gate-rescue answer, `if keyword_seats > 0 and not gate_fallback:` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2795, documented in the comment at :2794), has no test: the keyword-seat fixtures set CONFIDENCE_ENABLED=False (tests/test_pro_block_seats.py:37, tests/test_keyword_seats.py:54), where a rescue cannot fire. The route is narrower than an rrf-refused row, because under a rescue the gate signal is confidence. It is still reachable: during a rescue the results become the backfilled pre-gate rows and `admitted` is taken before the `results[:limit]` cut, so rescued lexical-only rows beyond the limit are in `passed_gate` but not in `present`. Without the guard they would be added as keyword seats to a gate_fallback answer, which the design excludes.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test with CONFIDENCE_ENABLED, keyword_seats > 0 and a forced rescue holding lexical-only rows beyond the limit, asserting that no row carries the keyword reservation label.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-183.
issues.fix_note: New test forces a gate rescue under CONFIDENCE_ENABLED with three keyword-only rows, limit=1 and a depth floor of 10, keyword_seats=2, and asserts no row carries a keyword seat; dropping `and not gate_fallback` from `if keyword_seats > 0 and not gate_fallback:` seats the two cut rescued rows and turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The keyword-seat eligibility filter `_rid_of(r) not in present` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2800) is untested, and the keyword-seat tests cannot see a duplicate because they key the response by content (`rows = {m["content"]: m for m in out["messages"]}`, tests/test_keyword_seats.py:146). The keyword-seat, reconstruct and recall test files all still pass under that change. The shipped code is correct.

issues.summary: (LOW) The presence re-filter on the extra block places, `extra = [row for row in block_spare if row["_rid"] not in present][:extra_block_seats]` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2900), is untested. `block_spare` is computed at reservation time (around :2774-2779) and excludes only rows present then; the keyword seats added later check a `present` set that holds the reserved block rows but not the spare ones, so a spare block row that is also a lexical-only keyword-eligible row can take a keyword seat first. Without the :2900 filter the extra block places would append it again, and do_recall's list would hold the same ref twice with the seat count off by one. The only extra-block-seat fixtures use block texts disjoint from the keyword row, so the overlap never occurs. Whether reconstruct's bundling would merge the two copies into one item was not checked.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test where a spare block row is also the best lexical-only row with keyword_seats > 0 and extra_block_seats > 0, asserting each ref appears once in do_recall's output.

issues.summary: (LOW) The recall_count bump binds one parameter per credited id in a single statement (`placeholders = ",".join("?" * len(returned_ids))`, cpersona/memory_handlers.py:3121, UPDATE at :3133) while its read twin is chunked at `vector._ID_FETCH_CHUNK` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:1541). The credited ids are bounded only by the recall limit, and `RECALL_LIBRARY_MAX_LIMIT` defaults to 10000 and can be raised (cpersona/config.py:172). Past the SQLite variable ceiling the UPDATE raises inside the non-fatal try, so the whole recall's recall_count and last_recalled_at bookkeeping is dropped with only a warning, and later confidence ranking treats those rows as never recalled. On SQLite older than 3.32 (ceiling 999) a library recall with limit 999 or more hits this; on current SQLite (ceiling 32766) it needs CPERSONA_RECALL_LIBRARY_MAX_LIMIT raised past 32766.

issues.fix_sketch: Run the UPDATE in chunks of the shared id-fetch bound inside the same transaction, as the read twin does.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test sends a non-string range `revision` to get_contents. `_parse_ref_entry` refuses one with `if revision is not None and not isinstance(revision, str): return ref, None, RANGE_INVALID` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:3583-3584). Deleting that check leaves the get_contents range and block quotation tests green, and the value then reaches the resolver's `revision != blocks.text_revision(text)` comparison, so `{'ref': 'mem:5', 'span': [0, 10], 'revision': 123}` would be reported as stale_revision (record rewritten) instead of invalid_range, sending the caller to re-fetch for a malformed request.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test gives `_partitions` a node or block set whose first offset is not 0. The conjunct `and rows[0][1] == 0` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:3625) is the only check that rejects a contiguous set that starts after 0 and ends at len(text); deleting it leaves every test that writes, corrupts or reads node and block sets green, while the seam, numbering and last-end conjuncts each have a failing test. Without it, get_contents for node 0 of a set whose first row starts at 7 would serve the text from offset 7 instead of reporting no_current_nodes, silently cutting the start of the record. The shipped check is correct.

issues.summary: (LOW) In get_contents' block branch, neither the boundary `if last >= len(rows):` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:3660) nor the `"of": len(rows)` count (:3662) is pinned by a test, while the node branch's twin boundary is. The only `of` assertions use the last block (tests/test_blocks_quotation.py:329), where `last + 1` equals `len(rows)`, so a regression to `of: last + 1` would also pass and tell a caller asking for block 0 of a 5-block record that there is 1 block.

issues.summary: (LOW) The rare-phrase keyword shortcut issues one FTS count statement per distinct query phrase, with no bound on how many. In the default rrf mode (and in the cascade) the keyword arm runs with rank_only, so `_common_phrases` loops `for term in sorted(set(candidates.values()))` and runs one `count(*) ... MATCH` each (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:3925-3927); query length is not capped at the tool boundary. When no phrase is at the idf floor the shortcut returns None and the whole OR-expression runs anyway (memory_handlers.py:4114-4115), so every count is discarded. Reproduced on a fresh 2,000-row CJK store: one `do_recall` issued 38, 2,998 and 19,998 count statements for 40-, 3,000- and 20,000-character queries, the shortcut was never taken, and recall time roughly tripled against the same query without the counts (4,864 ms against 1,435 ms at 20,000 characters). The cost is a constant factor on an arm that is already linear in query length, and the side connection these statements run on is shared by design, so the impact is wasted work and latency for a caller who already has access.
issues.fix_sketch: Bound the shortcut: skip `_common_phrases` when the candidate count exceeds a small limit, or count every candidate phrase in one statement. A query-length cap at the tool boundary is a reasonable second line.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. The same counting loop is where bug-687 reads its two non-atomic counts.
issues.fix_note: _common_phrases leaves a query with more than COMMON_PHRASE_MAX_COUNTS (64) distinct trigram candidates unclassified, so it issues no per-trigram count statements and the arm ranks on the whole expression. Reverting turns test_a_long_query_issues_a_bounded_number_of_phrase_counts red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `_common_phrases` reads the FTS row count (`SELECT count(*) FROM memories_fts_docsize`, cpersona/memory_handlers.py:3921) and each phrase's matching-row count (:3927) as separate autocommit statements, so rows committed in between can make a phrase's count exceed `n_rows`. `math.log((n_rows - held + 0.5) / (held + 0.5))` at memory_handlers.py:3931 then raises `ValueError: math domain error`, and the caller around `_rank_on_rare_phrases` catches only `sqlite3.OperationalError` (memory_handlers.py:4106), so the whole recall or reconstruct fails. Both counts are store-wide, not agent-scoped, so another agent's writes can break this agent's recall. Reproduced: with 20 rows all containing 'the', three stores for a second agent committed right after the docsize count gave held=23 against n_rows=20 and the recall raised; 100 recalls racing 200 stores without injection saw 19 failures, and sequential recalls afterwards all succeeded. The trigger needs a phrase held by nearly every row (in practice a tiny store) plus concurrent writes.
issues.fix_sketch: Clamp each count to at most `n_rows` (or read all counts in one read transaction, or take `n_rows` after the per-phrase counts). Also let the rare-phrase shortcut fall back to the whole expression on any exception, not only OperationalError.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Same code path as bug-686.
issues.fix_note: Each phrase count is capped at the row count read before it, so rows committed by any agent between the two statements can no longer make the idf take the log of a negative ratio; the rare-phrase shortcut's except also widens to Exception so any failure of the optimisation ranks on the whole expression. Reverting the clamp turns tests/test_2611a2_x07.py::test_a_phrase_counted_in_more_rows_than_the_row_count_is_common red with 'math domain error'; narrowing the except turns ...::test_the_shortcut_failing_in_any_way_ranks_on_the_whole_expression red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The episode FTS search has no guard for `sqlite3.OperationalError`, so two inputs that the memory keyword arm survives take the whole recall down. `_search_episodes_fts` runs `... WHERE episodes_fts MATCH ? ...` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:4003-4012) with no try, and none of its callers (`_lexical_arms` :633, the cascade, the cue arm) catches the error, while the memory keyword arm falls back to LIKE (bug-326, memory_handlers.py:4116-4124). Reproduced on a fresh DB: (A) a query decoded from the JSON-legal escape `apricot\u0000jam` makes recall raise `unterminated string` (the same query without the NUL succeeds), and recall, reconstruct and recall_with_context all fail the same way; (B) after `DROP TABLE episodes_fts`, recall raises `no such table: episodes_fts`, whereas dropping `memories_fts` degrades to LIKE. Each failure is an error for that one request with no data loss; a missing episodes_fts table is an abnormal state that an ordinary boot repairs. Separately, the comment at cpersona/acl.py:46 saying NUL is not legal in a JSON string is wrong, since `\u0000` decodes to U+0000.
issues.pattern: Episode FTS search unavailable, searching no episodes by keyword
issues.fix_sketch: Give `_search_episodes_fts` the same OperationalError guard as the memory keyword arm, logging and returning no episodes so the recall degrades. Optionally strip or reject U+0000 in queries at the tool boundary.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. It is the episode-side gap left by bug-326, whose regression test exercises only the memory keyword path.
issues.fix_note: _search_episodes_fts catches sqlite3.OperationalError around its MATCH, logs a warning and answers no episodes, as the memory keyword arm degrades (bug-326) and as the arm does with FTS disabled; an absent episodes_fts or a NUL inside a query token no longer fails the whole recall. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x07.py::test_a_nul_in_the_query_does_not_fail_the_episode_search and ::test_recall_degrades_when_the_episode_index_is_absent red.

issues.summary: (LOW) A very long recall query that the FTS arm does not match makes the keyword LIKE fallback raise, and the whole call returns an error. When FTS returns no memory rows, `_search_memories_keyword` builds one contains-pattern from the entire query (`patterns = [_like_escape_contains(query)]`, cpersona/memory_handlers.py:4133) and runs it at :4138 with no try; SQLite refuses LIKE patterns over 50,000 bytes, and the OperationalError propagates through `_lexical_arms` and `do_recall` to the tool wrapper as a bare `{"error": "LIKE or GLOB pattern too complex"}`. Reproduced over the MCP transport on a fresh 20-row store: recall, reconstruct and recall_with_context all fail for `'z'*49999` (50,001 bytes once the two % are added), a 50,100-byte CJK query and about 52 KB of non-matching words; adding one word FTS finds makes all three succeed. The trigger is narrow (a query over about 50,000 bytes with no lexical overlap with the visible rows, such as an encoded blob or a long query against an empty store), and the failure is confined to that one request.
issues.pattern: patterns = \[p for p in patterns if len\(p\.encode\("utf-8"\)\) <= _LIKE_PATTERN_MAX_BYTES\]
issues.fix_sketch: In the LIKE fallback, leave out or cut short any contains-pattern whose UTF-8 length plus the two % signs exceeds SQLite's pattern limit, and catch OperationalError there as the FTS branch does, so the recall comes back empty with a shortfall reason. A maxLength on the query in the recall, reconstruct and recall_with_context schemas could be added as defence in depth.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. Related to bug-326, whose LIKE fallback is the path that raises here.
issues.fix_note: The LIKE fallback leaves out any pattern over 50,000 UTF-8 bytes (SQLite's default SQLITE_MAX_LIKE_PATTERN_LENGTH) and catches OperationalError as an empty arm. Removing the filter turns test_a_short_extra_term_still_matches_beside_a_long_query red; removing both layers turns the long-query recall/reconstruct tests red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `archive_episode` stores caller-supplied future timestamps with no check. It derives `start_time` and `end_time` from the history entries' timestamps (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:4290-4309) and writes them unchecked; `future_timestamp_issue` is called only on the store seam (memory_handlers.py:243) and in the import report (admin_handlers.py:2955). docs/configuration.md:126-127 says `CPERSONA_FUTURE_TIMESTAMP_MODE` governs a caller-supplied `timestamp` and lists only import and unreadable stamps as deliberate exceptions (:193-201), so under `reject` a stamp that `store` refuses enters through an episode without warning, and a future episode `start_time` never decays and widens the span the same way the docs describe for memories. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Partly a docs-scope ambiguity, since the prose is framed around `store`.
issues.fix_sketch: Apply `future_timestamp_issue` to the episode span ends under the same mode (warn, reject or off) the store seam uses, or state in docs/configuration.md that episodes are outside the setting.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: do_archive_episode applies the store's future-timestamp verdict to the history stamps it will store (warn reports timestamp_ahead_of_clock, reject refuses before the embed); reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_x05.py::test_reject_refuses_an_episode_stamped_ahead_of_the_clock and ::test_warn_stores_the_episode_and_reports_the_stamp red.

issues.summary: (LOW) OAuth verification drops every JWKS key that has no `kid`, so a conformant issuer that publishes a single kid-less key can authenticate nobody. `_refresh` keeps a key only when `key.key_id` is truthy (cpersona/oauth.py:460), so the single-key branch for a kid-less token (oauth.py:379-384), whose own comment calls that the unambiguous case it means to serve, never has a key to return, and the log blames the provider ('key set ... carries no usable signing key'). RFC 7517 section 4.5 makes `kid` optional. Reproduced with one real RS256 key and the shipped verifier: the same token verifies when the JWKS entry carries a kid and is refused when it does not. The failure is closed, so there is no security impact, and mainstream issuers publish kids; a self-hosted or minimal issuer hits it, and the misleading log slows diagnosis.
issues.fix_sketch: Keep kid-less signing keys under a synthetic key and let the cache lookup serve the sole key when the token has no kid; a set with several kid-less keys should still be refused rather than guessed.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced.
issues.fix_note: _refresh keeps a sole kid-less signing key under "" (RFC 7517 section 4.5 makes kid optional), served through _from_cache's existing sole-key branch to a token without a kid; several kid-less keys are still refused and logged as such. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_x14.py::test_a_single_signing_key_without_a_kid_verifies_a_token_without_one red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The `_discover_jwks_uri` docstring overstates what the per-subject partitioning gate does. It says that, with the gate on, the walk continues until an OIDC discovery document has been read and, if none can be, the issuer is refused, because fail-closed is the whole point of the setting (cpersona/oauth.py:478-483). The code does not refuse: when gated and no OIDC document was read, it logs that `subject_types_supported` was never checked and returns the RFC 8414 `jwks_uri`, so the issuer's tokens are accepted (oauth.py:541-558), and the inline comment there says turning this into a refusal would be a policy change. The behaviour is the deliberate ruling; the docstring is what is wrong, and a reader relying on it would expect a refusal that never happens. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced.
issues.pattern: rather than refuses, and the abstention is logged
issues.fix_sketch: Rewrite the docstring to say that an issuer with no readable OIDC discovery document is accepted with a logged abstention, matching the code and its inline comment.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The code follows the ruling made under bug-339; only the docstring needs to change.
issues.fix_note: The _discover_jwks_uri docstring now says a pairwise-only issuer is refused, while an issuer with no readable OIDC discovery document is accepted with the RFC 8414 jwks_uri and a logged abstention, matching the code and its inline comment. Docstring only.

issues.summary: (LOW) One per-issuer log window covers every diagnostic in a discovery walk, so an earlier message permanently hides the pairwise-subject refusal. `_log_outage` drops any message for an issuer logged within `JWKS_MIN_REFETCH_SECONDS` (cpersona/oauth.py:607-613). The walk tries the RFC 8414 document before the OIDC ones (oauth.py:143-147); if that document has no https `jwks_uri`, line 534 logs 'publishes no https jwks_uri' and stamps the window, and the pairwise-only refusal logged from the OIDC document at oauth.py:521 in the same walk is then dropped before the walk returns ''. Discovery re-runs only after the same 60-second constant (oauth.py:63, 405-407), so every later walk repeats the order and the operator only ever sees the misleading jwks_uri complaint; the issuer-mismatch line at :500 can hide it the same way. Tokens are refused either way, so this is diagnostic visibility only, and it needs a rare issuer configuration. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced.
issues.fix_sketch: Rate-limit per issuer and message kind, or collect the walk's diagnostics and log the final verdict (the refusal reason) rather than whichever message came first.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related to bug-373.
issues.fix_note: _log_outage keeps one window per issuer and per message template (a fixed string, so the map stays bounded), so the RFC 8414 jwks_uri note no longer suppresses the pairwise-subject refusal that follows it in the same discovery walk on every walk. Reverting to one stamp per issuer turns tests/test_2611a2_x14.py::test_an_earlier_diagnostic_does_not_suppress_the_pairwise_refusal red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The stdio proxy forwards any 2xx body verbatim, so a 200 HTML page corrupts stdout and leaves the request unanswered. Only the status range is checked (cpersona/proxy_stdio.py:216); for a 2xx response that is not `text/event-stream`, `_response_messages` appends `response.text.strip()` unchecked (proxy_stdio.py:149-151), and the result is queued at :222 and written line by line with `sys.stdout.write(message + "\n")` (:281-284). An SSO login page, an SPA fallback or a wrong remote URL path answering 200 is therefore written as several non-JSON lines on the JSON-RPC stream, and no error reply is queued, so the request id never gets an answer. This is the same stream corruption and hang fixed for non-2xx responses, reached through 2xx. It needs a misconfigured or intercepted remote. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced.
issues.fix_sketch: Before forwarding a 2xx body, check that it is SSE or parses as JSON (or carries a JSON content type); otherwise queue a JSON-RPC error for the request, as the non-2xx branch does.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The 2xx counterpart of bug-063 and bug-082.
issues.fix_note: _response_messages raises _NotJsonRpc for a 2xx non-SSE body that is not a JSON object or array, and _forward answers the request with a JSON-RPC error instead of writing the body to stdout; multi-line JSON is compacted to one frame and non-JSON SSE data lines are dropped. Reverting the check turns tests/test_2611a2_x14.py::test_a_2xx_html_page_is_answered_as_an_error_not_written_to_stdout red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Invariant 8 (docs/RELIABLE_RECALL_2_6.md:612, a paraphrase is not a separate item) and the section 7 promise that a shortfall is never filled with duplicates (:368) do not hold for trivially different copies of one sentence. Store dedup is exact-content only, and bundling merges only on `CLUSTER_KEYS` (cpersona/reconstruct.py:95-101: msg_id, episode, adjacent, relation, chain), none of which is a content-identity key, so copies that differ only in letter case or a trailing '.'/'!' each become a singleton item. Reproduced with embeddings on: six such variants stored across sessions filled a count=5 window, the record that supersedes them fell to item 10, and the response reported no shortfall and no conflict. The same document already says semantic sameness is not judged (:544), which contradicts invariant 8 as written.
issues.pattern: Content sameness is not judged: two
issues.fix_sketch: Either narrow invariant 8 and the section 7 sentence to 'one cluster is one item; content sameness is not judged', or add a cheap deterministic content-identity cluster key (casefold, collapse whitespace, strip trailing punctuation) ahead of the existing keys, which is normalisation rather than semantic judgement.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced. The fix needs a contract decision: narrow the documented invariant or add a content-identity bundling key.
issues.fix_note: Contract follows the code (maintainer decision): invariant 8 now reads one cluster is one item and content sameness is not judged, and the section 7 shortfall sentence says a shortfall is never filled by splitting a cluster. The page is a design page whose released tool descriptions take precedence; no runtime change.

issues.summary: (LOW) Three documented bundling boundaries are not pinned by any test. A memory stamped exactly at an episode's start belongs to it (inclusive bound, cpersona/reconstruct.py:556); two rows exactly RECONSTRUCT_ADJACENCY_SECONDS apart are one burst (`gap <= window`, :575); and claims at the same instant order memories before episodes (`_claim_key`, :337). Mutants `start < mem.ts`, `gap < window` and a swapped kind rank each pass the reconstruct tests; tests/test_reconstruct_v1.py:132 uses 40-second gaps against the 60-second default and never an exact 60. A regression to a strict bound would split an episode and its memory, or a burst, into separate items and drop the `supports` role with every test green.
issues.fix_sketch: Add boundary tests: a memory at exactly the episode's start time, two rows exactly the adjacency window apart, and a memory and an episode at the same instant with the memory ordered first.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code; the code is correct today and only the tests are missing.
issues.fix_note: Test-only: tests/test_2611a2_y04.py pins the inclusive episode-start bound, a gap of exactly RECONSTRUCT_ADJACENCY_SECONDS as one burst (61 s as two), and memory-before-episode at one instant. Mutant `start < mem.ts` in bundle turns test_a_memory_stamped_at_an_episodes_start_belongs_to_it red; `gap < window` and a swapped kind rank in _order_key turn the other two red.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test pins which relation reaches an entity when two edges converge on it in the same hop. `walk()` keeps the edge with the lower recency value, which is the more recently declared relation (cpersona/reconstruct.py:636; cpersona/associations.py enumerates relations newest first). That edge's predicate becomes the claim's `why` and its recency orders the evidence cut. Inverting the comparison to `>` keeps the older edge, mislabels the evidence and reorders which reached records survive a max_evidence cut, yet the mutant passes the reconstruct and association tests; tests/test_associations_reconstruct.py:241 covers recency only across different reached entities.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test where two frontier entities both relate to one entity in a single hop with different declaration times, and assert the claim's `why` names the newer predicate.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code; the code is correct today and only the test is missing.
issues.fix_note: Test-only: tests/test_2611a2_y04.py walks Billing-feeds->Ledger and Payments-audits->Ledger in one hop, in both declaration orders, through do_reconstruct and asserts the reached record's why names the newer predicate. Mutant `recency > step[other][0]` in walk() turns both parametrized cases red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The walk's records-cut bound is exercised by no test. When an entity reached by a relation is mentioned by more records than the graph read holds, cpersona/associations.py:709-710 adds it to `records_cut`, `walk()` turns that into BOUND_EVIDENCE (cpersona/reconstruct.py:648-649), and reconstruct reports `max_evidence` in `bounds.reached` (:1889-1890). Replacing :648 with `if False:` passes the reconstruct and association tests, so a regression that silently claims a complete walk would not be caught.

issues.summary: (LOW) `record_passages` computes a governing range for every ranked block and only afterwards drops ranges that overlap one already taken (cpersona/reconstruct.py:1305-1309: `blocks.context_range(text, spans, row[0])`, then the overlap check). A block whose own span already lies inside a governed range always overlaps, so its context walk is wasted. On list-shaped text (one short line per block) this is one walk per block: a record of 1,600 `- item ok` lines costs 1,600 `context_range` calls to produce 10 passages (about 0.08 s). The whole and evidence sequences build passages for every head before the budget or cap cut (:1800-1804), so a lite or pro call over many such heads spends up to a second or two of event-loop CPU on discarded work. Output is correct; this is a performance issue only.
issues.fix_sketch: Before calling `context_range`, skip a block whose own span already lies inside a governed range; the overlap check after it then only handles partial overlaps.

issues.summary: (LOW) The bug-237 span filter `timestamp != '' AND datetime(timestamp) IS NOT NULL` (cpersona/scope_stats.py:185-187) admits a bare number such as '2025', because SQLite's datetime() reads it as a Julian day number. do_store accepts that timestamp, text MIN picks it as the scope's oldest stamp, and the julianday settling window (scope_stats.py:194-203) cannot replace it because `date(substr('2025',1,10), '+3 days')` yields no window. The Python parser then cannot parse it, so memory_handlers.py:1619-1623 leaves `time_range_hours` at 0 and `newest_age_hours` unset. Reproduced: after one store with timestamp '2025' the span becomes ('2025', <newest>) and the oldest parses to None, so with confidence scoring enabled the whole scope loses range-scaled decay and the bug-207 age anchor, the consequence bug-237 meant to remove.

issues.summary: (LOW) The recall tool's `limit` description (cpersona/server.py:1303) describes `limit` only as a per-retriever depth and says 'Fewer rows than this may be returned', and docs/upgrading-to-2.6.md:153 says '`limit` is the number of rows returned'. Neither tells a client that more rows can come back. Block build and retrieval are on by default, and after the gate and the count cut `do_recall` appends up to `BLOCK_RESERVATION` (2, cpersona/blocks.py:1103) block-reached rows the gate did not admit, with no opt-in (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2777-2778); `check_recall_count` (cpersona/providers.py:277) allows the returned count to exceed `limit` by that reservation and the seat allowance. A client that sizes its context for `limit` rows can receive more, including rows that never passed the quality gate. The behaviour is intended and is disclosed in docs/configuration.md under CPERSONA_BLOCK_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED; only the client-facing tool contract and the upgrade note are wrong.
issues.pattern: places held beside it add up to \{blocks\.BLOCK_RESERVATION\} rows the block arm reached
issues.fix_sketch: State in the recall `limit` description that the response can carry up to the block reservation (and any time-cue, far or propagation seats) beyond `limit`, and correct the upgrading-to-2.6.md sentence to match.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: The recall `limit` description says more rows than limit can come back: up to BLOCK_RESERVATION block-reached rows the gate does not judge, plus any time-cue, far or propagation seats; the 2.6 upgrade note (en/ja) says limit counts the ranked rows and the held rows come on top. Docs item, no test.

issues.summary: (LOW) The reconstruct tool description's READ FURTHER steps (cpersona/server.py:1684-1686) tell the caller to read 'the neighbouring nodes ({ref, node: [index - 1, index + 1]})' after an item's `expand`, but under the defaults the response usually carries no node index. With CPERSONA_RECONSTRUCT_QUOTE_CHARS=800 head quotes are filled quotes that never read node sets (cpersona/reconstruct.py:1738, the bug-495 path), and with block retrieval on (the default) any record that has blocks is quoted by `_block_quote`, which emits `block`, not `node` (cpersona/reconstruct.py:1056). `node` is emitted only for excerpts of records with a current node set and no current block set (cpersona/reconstruct.py:1124). The instruction is stale and unqualified for the default response; the scenario in which an agent builds a node range from a block index was not established.

issues.summary: (LOW) set_recall_precision is annotated `idempotentHint=True` (cpersona/server.py:2104-2106, on the grounds that 'setting the same precision twice lands in the same state'), but every call reruns `do_calibrate_threshold` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2071), which samples with `ORDER BY RANDOM()` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1528, 1649) and has no fixed seed. calibrate_threshold is annotated `idempotentHint=False` for exactly that reason (cpersona/server.py:2062-2064). The two annotations contradict each other: a host that retries set_recall_precision on the strength of the hint can persist a slightly different threshold and fused gate. The median-of-K draws narrow the spread but do not remove it, and the hint is advisory.
issues.pattern: precision twice can leave a different gate: not idempotent, as calibrate_threshold\.
issues.fix_sketch: Annotate set_recall_precision `idempotentHint=False` (and correct the comment), or make the recalibration it triggers deterministic for an unchanged corpus, for example with a seeded sample.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. The anchor is the comment that justifies the annotation, because the annotation line itself is shared verbatim by other tools. Related: bug-064.
issues.fix_note: set_recall_precision is annotated idempotentHint=False, matching calibrate_threshold: each call draws a new calibration sample and restamps the calibration time. Anchored on the comment because the annotation line is shared verbatim by other tools; tests/test_recall_precision.py::test_setting_the_same_precision_twice_recalibrates_twice_so_it_is_not_idempotent reads the annotation from tools/list and turns red if it says True again.

issues.summary: (LOW) The check_health description names dedup_msg_id_index as the only fix=true repair that is not agent-scoped and says to 'exclude it via `checks` to stay agent-scoped' (cpersona/server.py:2384-2387). The registry also flags coarse_index and block_index with `cross_agent_fix=True` (cpersona/checks.py:3521, 3523), and `_health_demands` adds read-write on '*' whenever any flagged check is selected (cpersona/acl.py:408). A caller holding read-write on its own agent that follows the description and leaves out only dedup_msg_id_index is still denied. The comment at cpersona/checks.py:3490-3492 still calls dedup_msg_id_index the only such repair, and the docs/ACL_DESIGN.md section 6 table has no row for the '*' escalation. The guard itself is correct (it derives from the registry at cpersona/checks.py:3535) and fails closed, so the cost is a wrong contract and denied calls, not a leak.
