issues.summary: (LOW) main() calls `config.validate_reconstruct_counts()` and `config.validate_block_gates()` at startup (cpersona/server.py:3710-3711), turning a default or forced count/budget above its maximum into a startup error instead of a silent clamp. Tests call the validators directly but no test checks that main() calls them or drives main() under a bad configuration, so removing either call would likely leave the suite green (inferred from a grep, no mutation was run). Separately, the FORCED_BUDGET > MAX_BUDGET refusal branch (cpersona/config.py:349-353) is untested: every test sets the forced budget to None or 1234, and the one 'exceeds' test is caught first by the DEFAULT branch at config.py:345.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a test that drives main() (or inspects its call sequence) under a default count above the maximum and expects the startup refusal, a matching one for the block gates, and a validator test with a forced budget above MAX_BUDGET and a default below it.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code and tests, not reproduced and not mutation-tested. Test-only: the production code is correct.
issues.fix_note: Drives server.main() (stopped at _preflight_http_auth by a sentinel) under a default count above the maximum, a forced count above it, a forced budget above the maximum with the default below it, and block retrieval without build; each must raise the named ValueError. Deleting config.validate_reconstruct_counts() (or validate_block_gates()) from main() turns the matching cases red with _PastStartupValidation; a direct validator test pins the forced-budget branch and its inclusive bound.

issues.summary: (LOW) In http embedding mode main() awaits `generation.refresh(vector._embedding_client)` (cpersona/server.py:3778) before `init_db()` (server.py:3811) and before any transport starts. refresh() calls `capabilities_with_outcome()`, which runs `await self._client.get(url)` (cpersona/_vendored_mcp_common/embedding_client.py:401) on an httpx client built with the full embedding timeout (embedding_client.py:309, default 30 s). When the backend host drops packets rather than refusing connections, startup stalls for up to that timeout even though the result is optional (failures leave the identity unknown). A stdio client with a shorter startup timeout can mark the server failed, so the documented degradation to keyword-only recall becomes no server at all. Only an unreachable remote backend in http mode reaches this.
issues.fix_sketch: Bound the startup identity probe with a short timeout, or move it to a background task as the startup calibration was, so the database and transport open without waiting on an optional probe.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced in this verification (an earlier measurement with a 5 s timeout matched the code path). Related: bug-258, which moved the startup calibration off the startup path for the same reason.
issues.fix_note: main() wraps the startup identity probe in asyncio.wait_for(..., STARTUP_IDENTITY_PROBE_SECONDS=3.0). An unanswered probe no longer holds the database and transport closed for the full embedding timeout. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x10.py::test_a_backend_that_does_not_answer_does_not_hold_startup red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Nothing serialises the background startup calibration against a concurrent set_recall_precision for the same agent. `do_calibrate_threshold` reads the agent's beta when the fused-gate measurement starts (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:1870) and later writes the live gate (admin_handlers.py:1891) and the sidecar with no lock or generation check. If the startup run (beta read as 1.0) finishes after an operator's set_recall_precision(strict) (beta 2.0), the live and persisted state pair beta 2.0 with a gate measured at beta 1.0, while the operator was told the beta-2.0 gate; the mismatch persists until the next recalibration. Reproduced with the real handlers, using a 1 s delay to force the finish order; unperturbed runs usually finish in the safe order. Triggering it needs a recalibration boot, a precision change for the agent being measured, and an unfavourable finish order.
issues.fix_sketch: Serialise calibrations per agent, for example with a per-agent asyncio.Lock taken by do_calibrate_threshold, or re-read the agent's beta before applying and persisting and discard the fused-gate result when it changed during the measurement. The startup loop could also skip an agent whose beta was set by set_recall_precision after the loop started.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced with a forced finish order. Related: bug-149 (its compare-and-restore covers only the failure rollback) and bug-258 (which moved the startup calibration beside serving).
issues.fix_note: do_calibrate_threshold records the beta it measured the gate at (gate_beta). Just before the sidecar save, with no await between, it discards the gate when the agent's beta changed during the measurement, and it writes the gate there rather than where it was measured. Reverting the comparison turns tests/test_2611a2_x02.py::test_a_gate_measured_at_the_old_beta_does_not_replace_the_one_precision_applied red.

issues.summary: (LOW) An unknown `CPERSONA_TRANSPORT` value is rejected only after the expensive startup has run. `_preflight_http_auth` returns silently for any transport other than `streamable-http` (cpersona/server.py:3535-3536), and `config.transport()` is documented as unvalidated (cpersona/config.py:1028). So a typo such as `http` or `streamable_http` passes the preflight. `main()` then opens and migrates the database (`await init_db()`, server.py:3811), schedules calibration when embeddings are enabled, schedules the outbound update-check GET, starts the task queue, awaits `blocks.queue_backfill()` (server.py:3871) and `block_index.on_startup()`, and only then raises `ValueError(f"Unknown transport: ...")` (server.py:3884). The `finally` block cleans up, so nothing leaks. The cost is that under `Restart=always` every restart repeats that startup work to reach a refusal that needs only an environment variable. bug-203 removed this same cost for the HTTP auth guard.
issues.fix_sketch: Reject an unknown transport name in the preflight, before `init_db()`, alongside the existing HTTP auth checks. For example, validate it against the set {`stdio`, `streamable-http`} at the top of `main()` or in `config.transport()`.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-203, which fixed the same ordering for the HTTP auth preflight.
issues.fix_note: main() calls config.validate_transport() together with the other configuration checks, so an unknown CPERSONA_TRANSPORT is refused before the database, calibration, update check, queue and block index start. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x10.py::test_an_unknown_transport_is_refused_before_startup red.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test checks that the attribution reconcile reads past the first 500-id chunk. `_forget_vanished_rows` reads the live ids in chunks of `_RECONCILE_READ_CHUNK` (cpersona/tasks.py:162), and the shipped code is correct. But the bug-366 regression test (tests/test_task_queue.py:406-437) seeds a single live row at `held[0]`, which is in the first chunk. A reconcile that reads only the first chunk still yields `live={held[0]}` and passes. A probe reproduced this: with live rows at ids 1, 501, 2001 and 4096, such a mutant keeps only id 1 and drops the other attributions. Those rows then fall back to `TRANSPORT_KEY` through `_session_for`, so a no-persist pause would govern them under the wrong session. The existing reconcile tests stay green.
issues.fix_sketch: Extend the bug-366 test, or add one, to seed live rows in later chunks (for example ids 1, 501, 2001 and 4096). Assert that exactly those attributions survive, so a reconcile that skips or truncates later chunks fails.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced with a mutant of the chunk loop. This is a test gap only; related: bug-366.
issues.fix_note: The reconcile test seeds live rows at both edges of the first chunk and in later chunks (1, 500, 501, 2001, 4096) and asserts that exactly those attributions survive. A reconcile that reads only the first chunk (range bounded by min(len(held), 500)), or slices a chunk one short, turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) A keyless no-persist pause makes the queue drain delete server-originated work that no session asked for. The block backfill sweep (cpersona/blocks.py:783) and the block-index build (cpersona/block_index.py:823) are enqueued with no session_key. They are therefore attributed to `TRANSPORT_KEY` (tasks.py:174-176). The drain deletes any row whose session is paused (cpersona/tasks.py:244-252). A probe reproduced this: under a keyless pause the sweep row was deleted without running, and a second drain after resume found nothing. A declared session's pause let the sweep run. The sweep is queued only once per process start (server.py:3871), so the rest of the corpus gets no blocks until a restart or a capped `check_health(fix)` missing_blocks repair. Under stdio, the single client is keyless, so any pause the user arms has this effect. This contradicts the drain's own comment that a pause must not discard work it never asked for (tasks.py:240-243). The impact is limited. Block construction is opt-in, the block layer is derived (missing blocks shrink block-arm reach and corrupt no data), and the next `build_blocks` re-queues the index build (tasks.py:327). A related but weaker case is a declared session's own build_blocks/build_nodes rows being dropped by that session's pause after the record was committed. That case arguably falls inside the documented rule that ephemeral intent overrides queued work.
issues.pattern: if task_type not in derived and session\.is_paused_for\(task_session_key\):
issues.fix_sketch: Attribute server-originated work (the backfill sweep and its continuations, and `block_index_build`) to a reserved system key that no caller can pause, or exempt those task types from the pause gate. Optionally, let the derived builds of already-committed records survive a pause.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced, with a declared-session control. Related: bug-151.
issues.fix_note: The drain exempts derived task types (node/block builds, the backfill sweep, the block index build) from the pause gate, so a keyless or session pause no longer deletes them. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x15.py::test_a_keyless_pause_does_not_delete_the_servers_own_derived_work and ::test_a_pause_does_not_drop_the_build_of_a_record_already_stored red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The `ok is False` half of the drain's update_profile failure check has no test, and it is the only half the real handler reaches. cpersona/tasks.py:273 treats a handler result as a failure when it has `error` or `ok: False`. The real `do_update_profile` returns its failures without an `error` key, as `{"ok": False, "profiles_updated": 0, "reason": ...}` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py:122, :126). The only test double returns `{"ok": False, "error": "synthetic failure"}` (tests/test_audit_2500b1.py:278), so the `error` half alone satisfies it. If the check were reduced to `result.get("error")`, a real failure would delete the row and log completion instead of taking the retry and discard path. The row is removed in both cases, so the visible effect would be mislabelled logging and a skipped retry.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a drain test whose update_profile double returns the real failure shape (`ok: False` with a `reason` and no `error` key). Assert that the drain retries the task and then discards it, rather than logging completion on the first pass.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. This is a test gap only; related: bug-090.
issues.fix_note: A drain test runs the real update_profile handler on payloads it refuses (ok: False with a reason, no error key). It asserts the task is retried TASK_MAX_RETRIES times, then discarded with the 'exceeded max retries' log and no 'completed' log. Reducing the drain's check to result.get("error") turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) No test checks that a `build_blocks` task in the drain queues the block-index rebuild. After the blocks build (cpersona/tasks.py:322), the drain calls `block_index.queue_build_if_needed()` (tasks.py:327), and deleting that call leaves every block test file green. The consequence of such a regression is narrower than a stale index, and it affects performance, not correctness. The block-index reader merges live change-log rows past `built_seq` (block_index.py:615-650). When those exceed `LIVE_ROW_BOUND` (35,000), it refuses and falls back to SQLite (block_index.py:633-634). Without the call, recalls would merge more live rows, and later every recall would fall back to SQLite until a restart or a backfill pass (tasks.py:338) queues a build. The anchor is the `build_blocks` line because the call at line 327 is textually identical to the backfill branch's call at line 338.
issues.pattern: assert ran == \[block_index\.TASK_TYPE\], "the drained block build queued no index build"
issues.fix_sketch: Add a drain test that runs a `build_blocks` task with the block index file enabled. Assert that a `block_index_build` row is queued afterwards, so removing the call at tasks.py:327 fails.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. This is a test gap only; related: bug-463.
issues.fix_note: A test stores a record with the block index file enabled and drains the queue. It asserts that the drained build_blocks task queued a block_index_build, that the build ran, and that the index file holds the new blocks. Deleting the queue_build_if_needed call in the build_blocks branch of tasks.py turns it red. A sibling test pins the backfill branch's call the same way.

issues.summary: (LOW) `_requeue_at_tail` can move a vanished task's session attribution onto another session's task. It runs `UPDATE pending_memory_tasks SET ... id = (SELECT MAX(id) + 1 ...) WHERE id = ?` without checking that a row matched. It then reads `SELECT MAX(id)` as the moved row's new id (cpersona/tasks.py:450-458). Suppose the failing build's row was deleted while the build was in flight, for example by the same delete `delete_agent_data` issues (admin_handlers.py:655). Then the UPDATE matches nothing, and `MAX(id)` is a different live task, which inherits the failed task's key. A probe reproduced this: session B's queued update_profile was re-attributed to session A and written despite B's pause. A mirrored case would delete a task whose own session is not paused. Reachability is narrow. The path runs only when a non-derived row waits behind a failing build, and in 2.6.10 no production path enqueues a non-derived task (update_profile and archive_episode bypass the queue, server.py:118-121). So it takes library use of `MemoryTaskQueue.enqueue`, a concurrent row delete during a failing build, and parallel declared sessions.
issues.pattern: if moved and key is not None and new_id is not None:
issues.fix_sketch: Check the UPDATE's rowcount, or use `RETURNING id`, in `_requeue_at_tail`. When no row matched, drop the attribution and do not re-attribute. Never read `MAX(id)` as the moved row's id.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced, with a control in which the row was not deleted. Related: bug-463.
issues.fix_note: _requeue_at_tail reads the UPDATE's rowcount and re-attributes only when the row actually moved. When the row vanished it drops the attribution instead of writing it onto MAX(id). Reverting turns tests/test_2611a2_x15.py::test_requeueing_a_vanished_row_does_not_reattribute_another_sessions_task red.

issues.summary: (LOW) A failed update-check fetch always overwrites the standing verdict with `unknown`. `refresh()` stamps `fetched_at` before the await, but on a failed fetch it calls `_store(..., _checked_at)` with the current global stamp instead (cpersona/update_check.py:561-564). `_superseded_by` then compares `_checked_at > _checked_at`, which is always False (update_check.py:521-524), so the bug-375 guard never applies on the failure branch. This has two effects. (a) A fetch that was issued first and fails last replaces a fresher successful verdict with `unknown`, which is the bug-375 race on the failure path. (b) An offline `check_update(refresh=true)` erases a known `yanked` or `newer` verdict until the next successful fetch or a restart, which drops the `version_yanked` health issue and the recall notice. The resulting state is `unknown` with a non-null `checked_at`, which contradicts the documented meaning of unknown, that no check has completed (update_check.py:100). Because the verdict kind changes, `_told_sessions` is also cleared and every session is re-notified. The effect is limited to the in-memory notice and the health hint: the cache file is not rewritten and no stored data is affected.
issues.pattern: if verdict is None or verdict\["state"\] == STATE_UNKNOWN:
issues.fix_sketch: On the failure branch, do not replace a standing verdict. Either return the current verdict, with the failure reported separately in the call's own answer, or pass the call's own `fetched_at`, so `_superseded_by` orders it against a fresher answer. Keep `checked_at` consistent with the documented meaning of `unknown`.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-375, whose fix covers only the success branch.
issues.fix_note: A failed fetch or an unreadable index no longer stores state=unknown over a known verdict (and is not cached); refresh() returns the standing verdict and only stores unknown, unstamped, when nothing is known. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_x11.py::test_a_failed_refresh_keeps_a_known_yanked_verdict and ::test_a_slow_failing_fetch_does_not_overwrite_a_fresher_verdict red.

issues.summary: (LOW) For a source checkout parked at a release tag (detached HEAD), the update notice, the check_health hint and check_update's `install.command` all give a `git pull` command that fails. `detect_install` always builds `git -C <repo> pull && <installer> <repo>` for a checkout (cpersona/update_check.py:845-855). The detached-HEAD alternative (`fetch --tags && checkout v<tag>`) is computed as `detached_command` (update_check.py:865), but only `apply()` exposes it, in its refusal reason (update_check.py:954). `_public_install` drops it. docs/tools.md:104-106 calls a tag-parked clone a normal way to deploy. On such a clone, git refuses with "not currently on a branch" and the `&&` stops before the install. The failure is immediate and visible, and nothing is half-installed.
issues.fix_sketch: Show the right command without spawning a subprocess on the notice path, for example by reading `.git/HEAD` to tell whether the tree is on a branch, or by showing both forms in the notice, the hint and `install.command`.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: detect_install reads the checkout's HEAD file (no subprocess; follows a `gitdir:` .git file) and shows the fetch --tags/checkout-tag command for a detached tree on every surface. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_x11.py::test_a_detached_checkout_is_given_the_tag_command_everywhere red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `check_update(apply=true)` has no single-flight guard, so a second apply can run its installer while the first is still writing to the same environment. `apply()` runs each installer step in sequence (`for step in install["argv_steps"]`, cpersona/update_check.py:961-962), and `_run_step` starts it with `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` (cpersona/update_check.py:1008) with nothing around the reads that kills the child on cancellation. The module keeps no lock or in-flight flag (the comment at cpersona/update_check.py:121-125 covers only the state mutators), and `do_check_update` awaits `update_check.apply()` directly (cpersona/maintenance_handlers.py:672). Two concurrent apply calls, or a call cancelled by a client timeout followed by a retry while the orphaned child keeps running, therefore start two `pip install --upgrade` (or `git pull`) processes over one site-packages or working tree. pip does not lock against concurrent installs, so the environment the next restart imports from can be left half-installed; the uv path takes its own environment lock and is less exposed. Reaching it needs an explicit apply plus a timeout and retry or a second client.
issues.pattern: if _apply_task is not None and not _apply_task\.done\(\):
issues.fix_sketch: Make apply single-flight within the process: refuse (or join) a second apply while one is in progress, and on cancellation either terminate and reap the child or keep the in-progress mark until the child exits so a retry cannot overlap it.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: apply runs its steps in a module-held task awaited through asyncio.shield, refuses a second apply until that task ends (so a cancelled call keeps the slot until its child exits), and a cancelled call starts no further step. Reverting the guard turns tests/test_2611a2_x11.py::test_a_second_apply_is_refused_while_a_cancelled_one_still_installs and ::test_two_concurrent_applies_run_one_installer red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The update installer child inherits the server's stdin, which under the stdio transport is the client's JSON-RPC stream. `_run_step` starts each step with `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(*argv, stdout=PIPE, stderr=STDOUT)` and sets no `stdin` (cpersona/update_check.py:1008-1012), and the pip installer prefix is `[sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install"]` with no `--no-input` and no `PIP_NO_INPUT` (cpersona/update_check.py:785, 789). pip prompts by default when an index answers 401 and no credentials are stored, and its prompt calls `input()`, which reads a line from fd 0. On a stdio deployment that installs with pip from a private index requiring credentials, `check_update(apply=true)` can therefore consume a JSON-RPC message meant for the server (that request is never answered), or, with an idle client, block apply indefinitely since apply has no deadline. git normally prompts through the terminal rather than stdin, and the uv path does not prompt, so the pip path is the realistic one; the configuration needed is rare.
issues.fix_sketch: Start installer steps with `stdin=asyncio.subprocess.DEVNULL`, and pass `--no-input` (or set `PIP_NO_INPUT=1` in the child environment) for pip so an authentication prompt fails fast with a readable error instead of reading the protocol stream.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code and pip's prompt path, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: _run_step gives every child an empty stdin so a prompting installer cannot read the stdio transport's JSON-RPC stream. Reverting it turns tests/test_2611a2_x11.py::test_an_apply_step_cannot_read_the_servers_stdin red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Test gap: neither regression test for bug-032 fails when `_clamp_limit` stops flooring at 0. The shipped clamp is correct (`return min(max(0, limit), cap)`, cpersona/utils.py:34), but with the floor removed both `test_do_recall_negative_limit_still_clamps_to_zero` (tests/test_do_recall_response.py:480) and `test_recall_negative_limit_is_clamped` (tests/test_v2438_hardening.py:382) stay green. The first captures the fusion depth, which `_recall_depth` floors on its own with `max(limit, RECALL_DEPTH_FLOOR)` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:1861); the second uses a blank query, where the cascade's own `max(0, ...)` floor and the query gates hide a negative limit. Reproduced with that mutant: in cascade mode with a non-blank query and an agent holding 100 or more memories, a negative limit reached the episode FTS `LIMIT ?` bind (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:4010-4011), where SQLite reads a negative limit as no limit, every match was fetched, `results[:limit]` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2737) kept the rest, and the call ended in a ProviderContractError, while the existing tests passed. Blank-query and rrf/rsf paths returned nothing under the mutant. Negative limits reach `do_recall` only from library callers, since the MCP schema declares minimum 0.
issues.fix_sketch: Pin the floor directly: a unit test asserting `_clamp_limit(-5, cap) == 0`, and/or a `do_recall` test in cascade mode with a non-blank query that captures the limit passed to the cascade or the episode FTS bound rather than the separately floored fusion depth.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Reproduced with a mutant of the clamp; the code is correct and only the regression coverage for bug-032 is missing.
issues.fix_note: The bug-032 test now asserts _clamp_limit(-5, cap) == 0 and, in cascade mode with a non-blank query, that the cascade receives limit 0 and nothing comes back. `min(max(0, limit), cap)` -> `min(limit, cap)` turns it red at both assertions.

issues.summary: (LOW) Test gap: the only regression test for bug-121 cannot fail since the bug-217 floor. `_content_excluded` returns False for empty content (`if not normalized: return False`, cpersona/utils.py:68-69), and the test asserts `_content_excluded("", {"some filter"}) is False` (tests/test_audit_2500b2.py:315). Since bug-217 an exclude entry shorter than `EXCLUDE_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS` (32, cpersona/utils.py:49) matches only on equality (cpersona/utils.py:71-73), and `'' == 'some filter'` is False with or without the guard. With an entry of 32 or more characters, `excl.startswith('')` is True, so if the guard regressed every memory with empty or whitespace-only content would again be dropped from recall whenever such an entry is passed, and nothing in the suite would notice. Reach is limited because store refuses empty content, so such rows come from legacy or import paths.
issues.fix_sketch: Add a case that calls `_content_excluded` with empty and whitespace-only content against an exclude entry at or above `EXCLUDE_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS` and asserts False, so deleting the guard turns it red.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code and the tests; the guard itself is correct and only the bug-121 coverage lost its teeth after bug-217.
issues.fix_note: The bug-121 test now also checks empty and whitespace-only content against an entry at or above EXCLUDE_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS; disabling `if not normalized:` turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The recall exclusion list has no size bound and is scanned linearly for every candidate row on the event loop. `_content_excluded` iterates the whole exclude set for each row (`for excl in exclude_set:`, cpersona/utils.py:70-76), visiting even entries below `EXCLUDE_PREFIX_MIN_CHARS`, which can only match exactly and could be answered by a set lookup. The set is built from the caller's list without a limit (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:2412), the `exclude_contents` schema has no `maxItems` (cpersona/server.py:1317-1319), and `recall_with_context` builds the same set from every `external_context` entry (cpersona/server.py:1481). The HTTP body budget defaults to warn mode and still delivers the body whole (cpersona/config.py:527, 541). One recall therefore costs O(candidate rows x entries) of synchronous CPU, and on the shared streamable-HTTP transport an authenticated client sending tens of thousands of entries stalls every other client's request for seconds per call. Realistic payloads are small, so this is a resource edge rather than a common-path failure.
issues.pattern: index = exclude_set if isinstance\(exclude_set, ExcludeSet\) else ExcludeSet\(exclude_set\)
issues.fix_sketch: Bound the exclusion list (schema `maxItems` and a handler-side cap), answer entries below the prefix floor with a set membership test, and restrict the prefix loop to the remaining long entries.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code; the timings were not rerun. Related: bug-217.
issues.fix_note: _content_excluded answers a row from an index built once per recall (ExcludeSet: set lookup for exact matches, sorted entries at or above the prefix floor searched by bisection) instead of walking every entry per row. Restoring the linear walk turns test_exclusion_cost_per_row_does_not_grow_with_the_list red.

issues.summary: (LOW) store removes a `[Memory from ...]` annotation from anywhere in the text, not only from a leading bridge prefix, and reports nothing. `_MEMORY_ANNOTATION_PATTERN` is unanchored (cpersona/utils.py:38) and `_sanitize_with_cap` applies it with `.sub` over the whole body (cpersona/utils.py:90). Content that quotes the annotation format loses words from the middle: 'Bug: the bridge prepends [Memory from alice] to every message; strip it' is stored as 'Bug: the bridge prepends to every message; strip it', and a regex for the annotation is cut to fragments. The returned `truncated` flag reports only a cap hit, so the caller is told the text was stored as given. Stripping anywhere appears intentional (the annotation health check matches it anywhere, cpersona/checks.py:201, and update_memory's description says annotations are stripped, cpersona/server.py:2176), but store's description does not say text inside the content is removed.
issues.pattern: annotation is removed anywhere in it, and text left empty
issues.fix_sketch: Decide the contract: either strip only a leading annotation (and narrow the health check to match), or keep stripping anywhere but document it on store and report in the response that content was altered.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code and running the sanitizer directly; because stripping anywhere looks like the intended design, the fix needs a contract decision rather than a local change.
issues.fix_note: Contract follows the code (maintainer decision): the annotation is the stamp early versions put on recalled text, and an agent that stores recalled text back, several memories joined, carries it mid-text, so it is removed wherever it appears. store's content description and docs/tools.md (English and Japanese) now say so.

issues.summary: (LOW) A remote vector search hit whose `score` is not a number makes the whole recall fail instead of falling back to the local scan. `_search_vector_remote` reads `score = hit["score"]` without checking its type (cpersona/vector.py:476) and returns it as the row's cosine, so the function succeeds and its fallback (`except Exception`, cpersona/vector.py:541-543) never runs. The comparison happens later, outside any fallback, in the quality gate's `if cosine >= cos_threshold:` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:1125), where a string score raises TypeError and the recall reaches the client as a bare error. The bug-333 comment at cpersona/vector.py:458-464 says every other malformed body already falls back, which is not true for this shape. Reaching it needs remote vector mode and a search service that serialises scores as non-numbers, which the project's own backend does not do.
issues.fix_sketch: Validate each hit's score inside the guarded parse (a real, finite number, not a bool), and treat a body that fails it like the other malformed shapes: log a warning and return None so the local scan runs.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Related: bug-333.
issues.fix_note: Each remote hit's score is validated inside the fallback try (finite int/float, not bool), so a malformed score falls back to the local scan instead of raising at the quality gate; reverting turns test_2611a2_x13.py::test_a_recall_survives_a_string_score_from_the_remote_service red with TypeError.

issues.summary: (LOW) The near and far vector scan windows are two separate statements over the live table, and the far read starts by OFFSET at `MAX_MEMORIES` (`cpersona/vector.py:1850`). The bug-334 fix (`cpersona/vector.py:2068`, `near_rids`) only drops rows that appear in both lists, which covers an insert between the reads. A delete or merge of a near-window row committed between the two reads moves every later row up one position: the row that was at position `MAX_MEMORIES` lands at `MAX_MEMORIES - 1`, after the near list was read and before the far offset, so neither list scans it for that recall. The far docstring (`cpersona/vector.py:1831-1832`) says the regions are disjoint by position, which assumes a static table. Only reachable when `CPERSONA_VECTOR_REACH` > `CPERSONA_MAX_MEMORIES` (not the default) on the scan path; the effect is a one-row miss on a single recall.
issues.fix_sketch: Read the near and far windows inside one pinned read snapshot, or define the far window by a keyset boundary (the last near row's created_at/id) instead of a numeric OFFSET, so a concurrent delete cannot open a gap between them.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced. Completes bug-334, which handled only the insert direction.
issues.fix_note: _search_vector stamps the connection (PRAGMA data_version, total_changes) around the near+far reads and reads the pair again once when it moved, so a delete between them cannot hide the boundary row; removing the check turns test_2611a2_x13.py::test_a_delete_between_the_near_and_far_reads_does_not_hide_a_row red.

issues.summary: (LOW) `plan_rows` selects `json_extract(source, '$.id')` over every embedded memory with no `json_valid` guard (`cpersona/vector_index.py:201`, used by the meta query at :207-213). The schema has no JSON check on `source`, so one legacy row with a non-JSON source makes both `build_index` and `build_coarse_index` raise `sqlite3.OperationalError: malformed JSON` instead of returning the declining dict. The CLI build exits with an error, and `check_coarse_index` with fix=true crashes because it catches only `IndexUnusable` (`cpersona/checks.py:3058-3059`). If the row is locked, `check_invalid_json` reports it but cannot repair it (`cpersona/checks.py:1851`, `AND locked = 0`), so the build keeps failing until an operator finds and unlocks the row; no finding names its id. Recall stays correct through the scan fallback; the cost is latency, and in auto cue mode the coarse-index remainder goes unsearched.
issues.pattern: CASE WHEN json_valid\(source\) THEN json_extract\(source, '\$\.id'\) END
issues.fix_sketch: Guard the projection, e.g. `CASE WHEN json_valid(source) THEN json_extract(source, '$.id') END`, so a malformed source is indexed with a NULL source id instead of aborting the build. Optionally have `check_invalid_json` name the locked ids it cannot repair.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. Same unguarded-json_extract class as bug-144, bug-227 and bug-239, at a new site.
issues.fix_note: plan_rows reads the source id only when json_valid(source), so a malformed source indexes as a NULL source id instead of aborting both builders; reverting turns test_2611a2_x13.py::test_a_locked_row_with_a_malformed_source_does_not_stop_either_build red with 'malformed JSON'.

issues.summary: (LOW) On Windows, `load_index` reads every array with `np.fromfile` (`cpersona/vector_index.py:523`), including the full count x dim float32 matrix of every agent, and `cached_index` keeps it for the life of the process. On a reload after a rebuild, `cached_index` calls `load_index` while `_cache[src]` still holds the previous index (`cpersona/vector_index.py:796-799`), so the peak is about twice the corpus. The justification in the `_maps_files` docstring (`cpersona/vector_index.py:459-461`) and `docs/CONTIGUOUS_INDEX_DESIGN.md:165` that this costs what the scan already touches is false: the scan reads at most `MAX_MEMORIES` rows of one agent in chunks. Reproduced with the Windows branch forced: 20,000 rows of 256 dimensions across 2 agents gave 21.3 MB resident after the first load (about 20x one agent's scan window) and a 42.9 MB peak during reload. Resident memory grows at 4 x dim bytes per row of the whole corpus; larger figures are extrapolations. Only Windows with the opt-in index built is affected.
issues.fix_sketch: Correct the comment and design doc to say the Windows cost scales with the whole corpus, and drop the stale cache entry before loading the replacement to remove the 2x peak. A fuller fix keeps the memory mapping on Windows by having the builder write a new file name per build instead of replacing a mapped file.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; reproduced. A consequence of the bug-503 fix, which switched Windows from mapping to reading. Partly fixed in 2.6.11a2: cached_index (and cached_coarse_index) pop the replaced entry before reading the rebuilt file, so a Windows reload never holds two copies; the doc and docstring now state the whole-corpus resident cost. Reverting turns test_2611a2_x13.py::test_a_reload_lets_go_of_the_replaced_index_before_reading_the_new_one red. The open anchor now names the remaining half.

issues.summary: (LOW) `load_index` validates the size and header from one open of the file (`cpersona/vector_index.py:481-482`) and then maps each array by path in a separate `np.memmap` (or `np.fromfile` on Windows) call (`cpersona/vector_index.py:521`, called for ids, embeddings, four axis codes and created_at at :525-534). A rebuild swaps the file with `os.replace` (`cpersona/vector_index.py:387`). If that replace lands between two of those calls and the new file is at least as large, nothing raises, and the loaded index mixes arrays from two files at the old header's offsets. `cached_index` takes the stat key before the load (:794, :798-799). The next query's stat differs, so the mixed object serves only the in-flight query, and the hydrate step re-applies isolation, so the effect is a wrong ranking for that one query. `load_coarse_index` has the same per-array pattern (`cpersona/coarse_index.py:275`, replace at :217). The window is microseconds per load.
issues.pattern: return np\.memmap\(fh, dtype=dtype, mode="r", offset=offset, shape=shape\)
issues.fix_sketch: Open the file once and derive every array from that single handle (one mmap or one read of the whole file), or re-check the file's stat or inode after mapping and retry the load if it changed.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: Both loaders open the index once and map or read every array from that handle, so a rebuild's os.replace mid-load cannot pair one header with another file's bytes; reverting to per-array opens by path turns test_2611a2_x13.py::test_a_rebuild_replacing_the_file_mid_load_does_not_mix_two_files red.

issues.summary: (LOW) Section 7 of `docs/RELIABLE_RECALL_2_6.md` states `0 <= reserved <= reservation (0 unless the block arm is on)` (:350) and that `returned_count` can exceed `effective_count` by at most the reservation (:377), and the reconstruct tool description says held items follow the window only with the block arm on (`cpersona/server.py:1676-1677`). The code allows more: `reconstruct.py:1896` bounds held items by the block reservation plus time-cue seats, far seats, the mode keyword seat and pro's extra block seats, and `tests/test_recall_cue.py:612` pins `reserved_count == 3` with `BLOCK_RESERVATION=0`. So held items appear with the block arm off, and a client sizing its context by the documented bound is wrong. Lines 491-506 of the same doc describe the mode seats as held items, but the formal invariant and the tool description were not updated. Documentation mismatch only; the code is consistent with its own check.
issues.fix_sketch: Restate the invariant and the bound sentence in section 7, and the tool description, as the sum the code checks (block reservation plus time-cue, far, mode keyword and mode extra block seats), and drop the claim that held items need the block arm.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code and docs, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: Section 7's invariant bounds reserved items by held_places, defined as block reservation + time-cue seats + far seats + mode keyword seat + pro's extra block places, and no longer says held items need the block arm; the reconstruct tool description says the same at equal length.

issues.summary: (LOW) `docs/configuration.md:4` calls itself the canonical reference and `README.md:174` describes it as listing every environment variable and its default, but about 49 `CPERSONA_*` variables read under `cpersona/` are absent from it (50 tokens, one of which, `CPERSONA_EMBEDDING_`, is a prefix fragment). Confirmed absent examples: `CPERSONA_EXPORT_DIR` (which decides ACL treatment of export/import and is named in denial details), `CPERSONA_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` (needed for the documented `api` embedding mode), `CPERSONA_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_SECS`, `CPERSONA_RECALL_PRECISION`, `CPERSONA_MAX_IMPORT_BYTES`, `CPERSONA_EMBEDDING_MODEL` and `CPERSONA_OPERATING_CONTEXT`. `docs/getting-started.md:395` says the reference is not exhaustive, so the docs also contradict each other. Documentation only.
issues.pattern: This page is the canonical reference and lists every
issues.fix_sketch: Add the missing variables to configuration.md, at least the security, embedding and import ones, or drop the completeness claims from configuration.md and the README and point to `cpersona/config.py` as the full list, consistently with getting-started.md.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by grep against the docs, not a runtime reproduction.
issues.fix_note: configuration.md now has a row for every CPERSONA_* name the package reads (49 added, in the same order on the .ja twin), and its header says so; getting-started no longer calls the page non-exhaustive.

issues.summary: (LOW) `docs/configuration.md:31` and `docs/operations.md:272-274` tell operators to raise `CPERSONA_MAX_MEMORIES` for large corpora. `docs/behavior-contracts.md` section 4 (around :175-178) and the comment in `cpersona/config.py` record that widening the window from 10,000 to 200,000 cost about 20 NDCG@10 on answers inside the window to gain about 5 below it, and call it 'a knob with a price, not the supported answer for a larger corpus'; the supported route is `CPERSONA_VECTOR_REACH` and the far seats. An operator following the configuration page degrades recall on recent memories. The code behaves as the contract says, so this is a documentation contradiction only.
issues.pattern: To reach older records by meaning, set
issues.fix_sketch: Replace the 'raise it for large corpora' advice in configuration.md and operations.md with a pointer to `CPERSONA_VECTOR_REACH` and the far seats, and note the measured cost of widening the window.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the docs and code, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: The CPERSONA_MAX_MEMORIES row no longer says 'raise it for large corpora'; it points to CPERSONA_VECTOR_REACH or the far seats and gives the measured cost (-20 NDCG@10 inside the window, +5 below). operations, faq and SKILL.md say the same.

issues.summary: (LOW) `docs/configuration.md:66` documents `CPERSONA_RECONSTRUCT_MAX_COUNT` as an absolute ceiling whose excess requests are clamped and reported. Under `mode='pro'`, `resolve_count` raises the maximum to `max(RECONSTRUCT_MAX_COUNT, PRO_COUNT)` with `PRO_COUNT = 15` (`cpersona/reconstruct.py:381-382`, :210) for both an omitted and an explicit count, so an operator ceiling below 15 is exceeded and `count_policy.clamped` stays false. The override is intended per the docstring, and a forced count still applies. `docs/RELIABLE_RECALL_2_6.md:484-485` mentions it only for an omitted count, and configuration.md does not mention it at all.
issues.pattern: the ceiling is at least 15, Pro's own window
issues.fix_sketch: Document in configuration.md that mode pro may read up to 15 items regardless of `CPERSONA_RECONSTRUCT_MAX_COUNT`, and extend the section 7 mode bullet to cover an explicit count as well as an omitted one.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10; confirmed by reading the code and docs, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: The CPERSONA_RECONSTRUCT_MAX_COUNT row says mode pro raises the ceiling to at least 15 while a forced count still applies, and section 7 says a named count may also reach 15 under pro.

issues.summary: (LOW) docs/configuration.md:78-80 (and docs/configuration.ja.md:81) says that when `count=5` yields only two valid items the response carries `requested_count=5`, `effective_count=5`, `returned_count=2` and a `shortfall_reason`. Every non-trace reconstruct response goes through `_compact` (cpersona/reconstruct.py:1550), which deletes `requested_count` and `count_policy` whenever the count was not clamped and its source is `caller` or `server_default` (cpersona/reconstruct.py:246-247, `_ASKED` at :160). A client written from the configuration page that reads `requested_count` after `reconstruct(count=5)` finds the key absent, so the canonical configuration reference contradicts the compact response contract.
issues.pattern: requested_count. and .count_policy. are added only when the server clamped
issues.fix_sketch: Reword the example in configuration.md and configuration.ja.md to match the compact envelope: `requested_count` and `count_policy` appear only when the count was clamped or forced, and an honoured count shows only `effective_count`, `returned_count` and `shortfall_reason`.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: The count=5 example lists effective_count, returned_count and shortfall_reason only, and says requested_count and count_policy appear only when the count was clamped or forced.

issues.summary: (LOW) docs/operations.md:370 says 'a late rebuild never changes an answer', and docs/configuration.md:34 says the coarse index makes the far search 'cheaper, never different'. That does not hold after a row is re-channelled: `vector_index.select` filters by the channel codes recorded at build time (cpersona/vector_index.py:840), while `do_migrate_channel_axis` (cpersona/maintenance_handlers.py:406) rewrites `memories.channel` in place from 'discord' to the recovered channel id (or to '' when globalizing). With an index built, `recall(channel=<id>)` still sees those rows as 'discord' and gives them no vector vote until the next rebuild, while the scan path would score them. docs/CONTIGUOUS_INDEX_DESIGN.md already accepts this staleness, but the operator pages and the migrate_channel_axis entry in docs/tools.md do not say a rebuild is needed after the migration.
issues.fix_sketch: Qualify the operations.md and configuration.md sentences so they cover only rows written after the build, and say in the migrate_channel_axis docs (and its result) that the contiguous index should be rebuilt after a migration that re-tags rows.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10. Confirmed by reading the code, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: Settled by the vector change log (bug-514): a migrate_channel_axis re-tag is logged by the UPDATE OF channel trigger and the row is read live until the next build; the test builds the index, migrates, and requires indexed search to equal the scan for both the old and new channel. Removing 'channel' from the trigger's UPDATE OF list in VECTOR_LOG_SQL turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The archive_episode row in docs/tools.md:18 says archiving moves the episode boundary, 'which down-weights everything written before it' (docs/tools.ja.md:21 says the same). The boundary penalty is gated on `EPISODE_PENALTY_ENABLED` (cpersona/memory_handlers.py:1636), which defaults to false (cpersona/config.py:939), and behavior-contracts.md section 3 states it is off by default. On a default install archiving an episode has no ranking effect, so a reader may skip a documented session-end call or misattribute recall changes to it.
issues.pattern: down-weights earlier records only when `CPERSONA_EPISODE_PENALTY_ENABLED` is on

issues.summary: (LOW) scripts/check-docs-live.py marks a line STALLED only when the age of the local manifest commit exceeds lag_hours (line 192), and that age is computed from the local manifest's commit (line 297), which is the branch tip, the youngest unpublished commit. With several unpublished commits, the oldest is the one that has been waiting. As long as a commit lands within 48 hours of each run, a publisher that stopped long ago is reported LAGGING, which gets only a notice, is excluded from comparison, and lets the job exit 0. Reproduced with a repository holding commits at T0, +30h, +70h and +110h and the site pinned at the first: each simulated daily run measured the tip's age, stayed under 48h, and reported LAGGING.
issues.fix_sketch: Measure the wait from the oldest commit not contained in the published commit (for example the first commit of `git rev-list published..local`) and compare that age against lag_hours. Add a test with multiple unpublished commits.

issues.fix_note: main measures each lagging line's wait from the first commit in published..local (git rev-list --reverse), not from the branch head, so a stopped publisher is STALLED while commits keep landing. issues.summary: (LOW) scripts/mutation-proof.py:194 marks M06 (removing the `if not tally.dry_run:` guard around the memory INSERT at cpersona/admin_handlers.py:2894) as `equivalent=True`, so the blocking mutation-proof job expects no test to fail. issues.summary: (LOW) The mutation-waiver verifier accepts a registry that has lost its subject. verify() (scripts/mutation_waivers.py:139), active_waivers() (:215) and main() (:244) all read `registry.get("waivers", [])`, and load_registry (:102-103) is a bare `json.loads` with no shape check. A missing or renamed `waivers` key, or an empty object in its place, therefore verifies as an empty registry and exits 0, even with --strict, although the CI step (.github/workflows/ci.yml:64-68) says it fails on a malformed registry. A non-empty object would crash on `w.get` and fail loudly, so only the missing-key and empty-value shapes are silent. Every approved waiver would then silently stop applying. Impact today is small: the registry holds one waiver, none human-approved, and the mutation lane is advisory.

issues.summary: (LOW) scripts/verify-issues.sh:243-245 counts matches with `grep -cP ... 2>/dev/null || grep -cE ... 2>/dev/null || match_count=0`, so any grep error (exit 2: a pattern that does not compile, such as an unbalanced paren, or a pattern starting with `-` that grep parses as an option) becomes `match_count=0`. For an `absent` entry, lines 262-266 then report [FIXED], the row lands in the fixed bucket and the bucket reconciliation passes, so the regression the entry exists to catch is never checked. A `present` entry with the same error shows STALE, so only the absent direction fails open. Reproduced with an unmodified copy of the script: an absent entry with pattern `fts_query = build(query` against a file containing that text printed [FIXED] and exited 0, while the escaped control printed [UNFIXED]; a pattern starting with `-` also gave [FIXED]. The probe ran with BSD grep; the GNU grep behaviour used in CI was not run. qa/issue-registry.schema.md already tells authors to escape metacharacters, and none of the live entries fails to compile or starts with `-`, so nothing is affected today.
issues.pattern: grep could not evaluate the pattern against
issues.fix_sketch: Distinguish grep exit 1 (no match) from exit 2 or more (error) and count an error as an invalid row in `errors` instead of zero matches. Pass the pattern after `-e` (or `--`) so a leading `-` is never read as an option.
issues.note: Found by the 2026-10-13 audit of 2.6.10 and reproduced with a copy of the script on a scratch registry. Related to bug-432 and bug-309 (other ways this gate passed rows it had not checked).
issues.fix_note: The verifier separates grep's exit 1 (no match, a count of 0) from 2 or more (an error): an entry whose pattern cannot be evaluated is reported INVALID and counted as an error, -E is tried only when -P could not run, and the pattern follows -e. No current entry changes verdict (801 patterns compile under both engines and none starts with '-'). Pinned by three tests in tests/test_252a2_i6.py; reading an error as zero again, or dropping -e from both calls, turns them red. Changed with the maintainer's approval, the script being read-only infrastructure otherwise.

issues.summary: (CRITICAL) With CPERSONA_EXPORT_DIR set, the ACL demand for import_memories and export_memories covered only the agent named in the call (cpersona/acl.py _file_io_demands), but the confined directory is one namespace shared by every agent and a file's name does not tie it to the agent that wrote it. A client granted read-write on agent A alone could import agent B's export with target_agent_id=A (do_import_memories relabels every record to the target) and then read B's memories, episodes and profile through A, although every direct read of B was refused; a per_subject client could do the same with target_agent_id='@me'. The same client could export A over B's backup file (os.replace onto any confined path), destroying it, or over any non-export file in the directory. The import demand now covers read on every agent the file names in its header and records, and the export demand covers read-write on the agent that owns the file being replaced ('*' for a file that is not an export).
issues.pattern: return \[\(own, PERM_WRITE\)\] \+ \[d for d in file_demands\(args\) if d\[0\] != own\]
issues.fix_sketch: Tie each file in the shared export directory to the agents it holds: import demands read on every agent_id in the file's header and records (as merge_memories demands read on its source), and export demands write on the agent named in the header of any existing file it would replace, or '*' when that file is not an export. Keep the '*' escalation when EXPORT_DIR is unset, and correct ACL_DESIGN §6 / D4, which implied that confinement alone limits the call to one agent.

Unchanged when EXPORT_DIR is unset or the call already demands '*'. Reverting this line (back to the agent-scoped demand alone) turns red tests/test_2611a1_u02.py::test_import_of_another_agents_export_needs_read_on_that_agent, ::test_export_does_not_replace_a_file_another_agent_wrote, ::test_export_does_not_replace_a_file_no_export_header_claims, ::test_a_per_subject_client_cannot_restore_another_subjects_export and ::test_import_demand_names_every_agent_in_the_file.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) check_health's file_permissions repair changes files every agent shares but was authorised by a grant on one agent. Its repair chmods the database, -wal/-shm, the calibration sidecar, the alias ledger, the update cache and the vector index files to 0600 (cpersona/checks.py check_file_permissions), yet the check was registered without cross_agent_fix, so the ACL guard's _health_demands asked only for read-write on the agent the call named. Under an ACL, a client holding one agent (or a per_subject tenant using '@me') could call check_health(agent_id=<own>, fix=true, checks=['file_permissions']) and narrow a mode the operator had widened on purpose for the whole deployment, for example a same-group backup reader. Reproduced: with the database at 0640 and a client granted only {A: read-write}, the call was allowed and the database became 0600.
issues.fix_sketch: Declare the file_permissions check cross_agent_fix=True so the guard demands read-write on '*' when it is selected, the same way coarse_index and block_index are declared because their repairs write files holding every agent's records.
issues.fix_note: The file_permissions health check is registered with cross_agent_fix=True, so CROSS_AGENT_FIX_CHECKS includes it and the ACL guard demands read-write on '*' before check_health(fix=true) may run its chmod of the database, its -wal/-shm, the calibration sidecar, the alias ledger and the index files. A grant on one agent is refused and the operator's chosen modes stay as they are; a grant on every agent still runs the repair. Removing the flag turns test_the_file_permission_repair_demands_every_agent and test_a_single_agent_grant_does_not_narrow_the_shared_database in tests/test_2611a1_u17.py red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The embedding client removed endpoint credentials from httpx's exception text only by replacing the configured URL string; httpx quotes its own normalised spelling of the URL, so with any other spelling (mixed-case host, explicit default port, characters httpx percent-encodes) the userinfo password or query key was written to the WARNING log and returned in the failure evidence that recall degraded advisories quote
issues.fix_sketch: Strip userinfo and query from every URL found in the exception text (regex over URLs, each rebuilt from urlsplit without userinfo/query), after replacing the configured spellings, in _failure_evidence, capabilities_with_outcome and count_tokens_with_outcome; same change needed in the shared mcp_common library the package vendors.
issues.fix_note: _failure_evidence and the capability / token-count evidence now run the exception text through redact_urls(), which first replaces the configured spellings and then strips userinfo and query from every URL in the text structurally (regex over URLs + urlsplit), so httpx's normalised spelling (lower-case host, dropped default port, percent-encoded userinfo/query) is cleaned too. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u07.py::test_failure_evidence_carries_no_credential_in_any_spelling and ::test_api_mode_evidence_carries_no_credential_with_uppercase_host_and_default_port red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The per-user source_id recall filter matched by bare string prefix, so a value naming one principal also admitted every principal whose id merely starts with the same characters ('discord:12345' admitted 'discord:123456', 'user:1' admitted 'user:10'), on every SQL arm built by source_id_where and in the contiguous index's startswith, while the recall schema described the filter as restricting recall to one user.
issues.fix_sketch: Give the filter a boundary: a value ending in a letter or digit names one id and is compared whole (as text, so JSON number ids still match); a value ending in a delimiter stays a namespace prefix. Decide the line in one helper used by both the SQL predicate and the contiguous index, and correct the schema, docstrings and operations guide.
issues.fix_note: source_id_where compares a value that ends in a letter or digit with the whole $.id (CAST ... AS TEXT = ?) and keeps the substr prefix only for a value ending in another character; vector_index.select applies the same line through isolation.source_id_matches. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u16.py::test_a_per_user_source_id_does_not_admit_an_id_that_extends_it (plus the do_recall, numeric-id, namespace[docs/a.md] and contiguous-index tests) red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) delete_agent_data dropped index files every agent shares on the authority of a grant on one agent. After a purge, _purge_local_vector_index unlinked the contiguous vector index, the coarse index and the block index (cpersona/admin_handlers.py), each holding every agent's rows, while the ACL demand for delete_agent_data is read-write on the named agent only. The row-count guard (a purge that deleted nothing keeps the files) was passed by storing one row first, so a client holding one agent, or a per_subject tenant through '@me', could repeatedly move every other agent's recall onto the slower read until the files were rebuilt; rebuilding the coarse index through check_health needs read-write on '*'. Reproduced through the guard: store(A) then delete_agent_data(A) by a client granted only A removed all three files while B's and C's rows remained.
issues.fix_sketch: Drop the shared index files from the purge only when the caller's grant covers every agent (or no ACL is active). Under a narrower grant leave them in place: readers hydrate candidates from the database, so the purged rows drop out of answers, and the next build removes them from the files.
issues.fix_note: _purge_local_vector_index drops the shared contiguous, coarse and block index files only when acl.caller_holds_every_agent() says the caller's grant covers every agent (always true with no ACL). Under a grant on one agent the files stay: readers hydrate candidates from the database (and fall back when a candidate is gone), so the purged rows are not served, and the next build leaves them out. A caller holding one agent can no longer store a row and purge it to push every agent onto the slower read. Removing the gate turns test_a_single_agent_purge_keeps_the_shared_index_files in tests/test_2611a1_u17.py red; test_a_purge_under_a_grant_on_every_agent_still_removes_the_index_files pins that the bug-337 removal is kept for '*' grants.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) store's content dedup ignored the source: a text already held under a different source id in the visible scope answered a second principal's store with result 'skipped' (ok:true) and the first principal's row id, so the second principal's copy was never written and its own source_id-scoped recall could not find it, and a store with lock:true locked the first principal's row through the lock rider.
issues.fix_sketch: Without a schema change, make the probe source-aware: skip only against a copy with the same $.id; where a different-source copy occupies the exact bucket the unique index guards, reject with no id; otherwise write the caller's copy.
issues.fix_note: do_store's content probe reads every visible copy and skips only against one with the same source $.id; a different-source copy in the exact bucket is rejected with no id, and one visible only through the global pool lets the caller's copy be written. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u16.py::test_an_identical_text_from_another_source_is_not_answered_with_its_row and ::test_another_sources_copy_is_written_where_the_bucket_allows_it red.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) With per_subject configured, the reserved 'u-' alias namespace was enforced only by the boot check: a store, archive_episode, update_profile, merge_memories or import_memories call from any client with write on such a name created an agent the alias ledger had not issued, and the next server start then refused to serve until an operator renamed it.

issues.fix_note: The ACL guard asks the boot check's own predicate (acl.reserved_for_new_rows) before any tool in _ROW_CREATING_SCOPE adds rows, and do_import_memories asks it per file record, so an unissued u- agent cannot be created at runtime while per_subject is configured. Reverting turns tests/test_2611a1_u16.py::test_a_write_cannot_create_an_unissued_alias_while_per_subject_is_on (8 cases) and ::test_an_import_cannot_create_an_unissued_alias_while_per_subject_is_on red.

issues.summary: (LOW) check_health(fix=true)'s remote index sync (_sync_remote_index) keeps posting chunk after chunk to a remote index that has stopped answering. Each post waits out the index deadline, so a repair that rewrote many rows spends one deadline per chunk. issues.summary: (LOW) set_recall_precision persists the new beta even when the fused-gate measurement degraded (no embedding client, a failing backend), so the sidecar holds the new beta beside the gate measured at the old one. issues.fix_sketch: When precision_override names a new beta and fused_stats is None, either leave the stored beta unchanged and report that the precision was not applied, or persist the beta together with a marker that the gate must be re-measured.

issues.summary: (LOW) check_memory_annotation's repair strips `[Memory from ...]` annotations with one regex pass. bug-616 made the write seam strip to a fixed point (utils._strip_annotations) because one pass can assemble a new annotation out of the text on either side of the one it removed. The health repair still makes one pass, so a repaired row can keep an annotation, and the next run rewrites it again.
issues.fix_sketch: Clean the rows with utils._strip_annotations (then strip) instead of _MEMORY_ANNOTATION_PATTERN.sub, so the repair and the write seam produce the same text.

issues.summary: (LOW) The content-rewriting health repairs (annotation, mention and oversized-content fixes, through _rewrite_or_delete_on_collision) change a row's text without queueing its overflow-node and block builds. The content triggers drop the row's node and block sets with the old text, so the record has none, and reads fall back to read-time division, until a later sweep (the block backfill at the next start, or a missing-nodes / missing-blocks repair) builds them. update_memory and merge_memories queue the builds after they rewrite text (bug-625).
issues.pattern: \"UPDATE memories SET content = \?, embedding = NULL, embedding_model = '' WHERE id = \? AND locked = 0\",
issues.fix_sketch: Collect the rewritten row ids during the fix run and queue their node and block builds after the run commits, as the merge path does.
issues.note: Found while fixing bug-625 (a sibling the fix did not cover); confirmed by reading the code.

issues.summary: (LOW) A lone UTF-16 surrogate (half of a pair, such as U+DFFF sent on its own) is refused by store, archive_episode, recall, reconstruct and get_contents (bug-633), but the other handlers still bind it and raise from SQLite with a bare error: update_memory, update_profile, the list tools, delete/lock/unlock, import_memories, declare_associations and traverse.

issues.summary: (LOW) The v12 migration's two dedup steps choose their survivor without regard to locks: the content step keeps MIN(id) and the msg_id step keeps MAX(id), and both leave locked rows alone. When the survivor they choose is unlocked and a locked collider exists, both rows stay and the unique index is skipped. bug-638 fixed the same choice in check_dedup_msg_id_index by preferring a locked survivor.

issues.note: Found while fixing bug-638 (a sibling the fix did not cover); confirmed by reading the code.

issues.summary: (LOW) check_duplicate_content's repair keeps MIN(id) of each duplicate group and deletes only unlocked rows, so a group whose oldest row is unlocked and whose newer copy is locked keeps both, and the finding reports the group as repairable on every run. issues.fix_sketch: Prefer a locked row as the survivor, and repoint associations to it as the current repair repoints them to MIN(id).
issues.note: Found while fixing bug-638 (a sibling the fix did not cover); confirmed by reading the code.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) source_id_where builds the per-user source filter with json_extract(source, '$.id') and no json_valid guard, so a scan filtered by source_id raises 'malformed JSON' as soon as one row in scope has a source that is not JSON, and the whole call fails. Such rows exist: check_invalid_json reports them and leaves locked ones alone. bug-743 guarded the same read in the index builder.
issues.pattern: source_id_expr = f\"CASE WHEN json_valid\(\{pre\}source\) THEN json_extract\(\{pre\}source, '\$\.id'\) END\"
issues.fix_sketch: Guard the read as CASE WHEN json_valid(source) THEN json_extract(source, '$.id') END, so a malformed source matches no source_id instead of failing the scan.
issues.note: Found while fixing bug-743 (a sibling the fix did not cover); reproduced.
issues.fix_note: source_id_where reads the id through CASE WHEN json_valid(source) THEN json_extract(source, '$.id') END on both forms (one id and namespace), so a malformed source matches no source_id and every source-scoped arm keeps scanning. A CASE rather than a leading json_valid(source) AND conjunct, as in bug-743, because the fragment is spliced into callers' WHERE clauses and a CASE evaluates only its selected branch wherever it lands. Before the fix the empty-query recall raised 'malformed JSON' and the keyword recall silently returned no rows. Pinned by tests/test_audit_2611_followups.py; mutations M444 (one id) and M445 (namespace) restore the unguarded read and each turns its tests red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The time cue's remainder search and the far seats read past the scan window from start=MAX_MEMORIES in a statement separate from the window's own read. issues.fix_sketch: Apply the same change stamp (PRAGMA data_version, total_changes) around the window and remainder reads and read the pair again once when it moved.
issues.note: Found while fixing bug-742 (a sibling the fix did not cover); confirmed by reading the code.

issues.fix_sketch: Hold a lock file beside the sidecar for the read, overlay and rename, as the alias ledger does.
issues.note: Found while fixing bug-630 (a sibling the fix did not cover); confirmed by reading the code.
