issues.summary: (LOW) The merge preview's `if not tally.dry_run:` guard around the memory INSERT in `_merge_memory_page` (cpersona/admin_handlers.py) has the shape bug-759 found in the import preview: the preview runs on the shared read connection, so without the guard its INSERTs are visible to concurrent read scopes and are rolled back when one of them exits, and the within-call dedup then rests on rows that are gone. Replacing the guard with `if True:` leaves the full suite green (measured on the 2.6.11a2 integration branch); no registered mutation removes the guard alone (M12 removes it together with the write seam).
issues.fix_sketch: Give merge_memories(dry_run=True) the deterministic test bug-759 added for import: open and close a read scope after every record, and assert that the preview counts equal a real run's and that no preview row is visible. Register the guard-only mutation in scripts/mutation-proof.py.
issues.note: Found while fixing bug-759 (a sibling the fix did not cover); measured by removing the guard against the full suite. Nothing is wrong at runtime: the shipped code keeps the guard.
issues.fix_note: tests/test_2611a2_y12.py::test_a_read_between_merge_preview_pages_sees_no_previewed_row opens and closes a read scope after every page of a merge preview and asserts it saw no target row, then that the preview's counts equal a real run's. Within one source the unique indexes already keep rows from colliding, so the counts cannot tell the guard's absence; visibility to a read is what the guard protects. Mutation M446 removes the guard alone (the import preview's M06 shape) and is CAUGHT: each interleaved read saw the 3 previewed rows of its page.

issues.summary: (LOW) The autouse `_jst` fixture in tests/test_2512b2_handlers.py calls `time.tzset()` on teardown while monkeypatch still holds `TZ=Asia/Tokyo`, and monkeypatch restores `TZ` afterwards without another `tzset()`. The C library's zone therefore stays at JST for the rest of the test process. On macOS `datetime.astimezone()` follows the restored variable, so nothing changes there; on glibc, where `localtime_r` does not re-read `TZ`, tests that run after this module may compute local times in JST while `TZ` says otherwise.
issues.fix_sketch: Restore TZ before the last tzset: after the yield, set TZ back explicitly (or call monkeypatch.undo()) and then call time.tzset(), as the helper in tests/test_audit_2500b2.py now does.
issues.note: Found while fixing bug-763 (a sibling the fix did not cover); confirmed by reading the fixture. The glibc effect is reasoned, not reproduced.
issues.fix_note: The fixture no longer uses monkeypatch for TZ: _pinned_zone restores the variable and only then calls tzset(), the order tests/test_audit_2500b2.py's _host_timezone uses. test_bug801_the_pinned_zone_does_not_outlive_its_block nests a pin inside the module's own and asserts both TZ and time.tzname come back; calling tzset() before the restore turns it red with TZ=Asia/Tokyo and the zone still PST/PDT, the shape of the defect. The glibc consequence stays reasoned, not reproduced; time.tzname shows the stale zone on any platform.

issues.summary: (LOW) tests/test_docs_behavioural_claims.py::test_deep_relaxes_the_quality_gate_rather_than_a_time_horizon fails when tests/test_recall_precision.py runs before it in the same process (reproduced on master cc4f9e3: `pytest tests/test_recall_precision.py tests/test_docs_behavioural_claims.py` gives 1 failed), and passes alone or in its own module. The full suite runs the files in alphabetical order, so CI never takes that order and the leak stays hidden. Saving and restoring vector's calibration globals (agent betas, fused gates, global gate and signal, agent thresholds) around the precision module's autouse fixture did not remove the failure, so the leaked state is something else; the cause is not established.
issues.fix_sketch: Find the process-global state the precision module leaves (diff cpersona.* module attributes before and after the module, as the behaviour-golden harness does) and restore it in the module's fixture; then add a test that runs the two modules in this order.
issues.note: Found while testing the contract decisions of 2026-10-15; reproduced on unmodified master.
issues.fix_note: The leaked state was config.VECTOR_MIN_SIMILARITY: test_sidecar_round_trips_agent_betas and test_restore_tolerates_pre_v2429_sidecar restore a sidecar whose global_threshold is 0.5, and the module's autouse fixture saved and restored the beta, gates and signal but not the threshold, so the victim's recall scored against 0.5 instead of 0.3 and deep admitted nothing new. Found by diffing every cpersona module attribute between the victim alone and the victim after this module. The fixture now restores the threshold and calls vector._reset_calibration_authority(), the reset entry the sibling sidecar fixtures use, for the claims the restore also left (no current test reads those across modules, so only the threshold restore is load-bearing). Pinned by tests/test_audit_2611_followups.py::test_bug802_a_recall_test_after_the_precision_module_still_passes, which runs the two in this order in a fresh process; dropping the threshold restore turns it red.

issues.summary: (LOW) The advisory mutation-diff lane ran every mutant, and its baseline, under the fixed `timeout = 120.0` in cosmic-ray.toml, and cosmic-ray 8.4.6 records a test command it stops at the timeout as KILLED (cosmic_ray/testing.py: `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: return (TestOutcome.KILLED, "timeout")`). A surviving mutant runs the whole suite, so as the suite approaches the limit a survivor is counted as caught, and once the suite passes it the baseline fails outright. On CI the unmutated suite was priced at 69.9-102.0 s in the runs of 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12, and every run with a production diff from 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-16 (13 runs) reported `baseline-failed` with `>>> timeout` (the last baseline took 121 s). The job is continue-on-error, so the checks read as passing while the lane measured nothing. `classify` did not tell a timeout kill from a test kill either, so a run that did proceed could not show how many of its kills were the clock.
issues.fix_sketch: Derive the per-mutant timeout from the unmutated suite the lane already times, as a multiple with the configured value as a floor, and run every cosmic-ray step under it; count timeout kills apart from test kills.
issues.fix_note: The lane now runs the unmutated suite once, before `cosmic-ray init`: that timed run is the baseline (a red suite reports baseline-failed and starts nothing) and the price, bounded by the budget. It writes the run's config with timeout = max(the configured floor, 3x the measured time) and passes that config to init, both filters and exec, so the limit grows with the suite. `cosmic-ray baseline` is no longer called, which also saves one full suite per run; the `unpriced` status is gone with it. The report carries `timeout_seconds` and `killed_by_timeout`, and the summary names the kills the clock made. Pinned by tests/test_mutation_diff_timeout.py; 14 mutations of the change (the factor, max/min, each step's config, the rewrite, the bound, a second unmutated run, the status, the count and the summary line) each turn it red. Run end to end with cosmic-ray 8.4.6 locally: the suite was priced at 95.7 s and the run config carried timeout = 287.1.

issues.summary: (LOW) Tests that point `database.DB_PATH` at a scratch database but leave `config.DB_PATH` on the path tests/conftest.py pins for the process build their index files beside that shared path, because the index and calibration files are named from `config.DB_PATH` (block_index.index_path, vector_index.index_path). Across the full suite 145 tests left such a file (138 block indexes, 7 calibration sidecars), and a later test reading the shared path found an index built from another test's database. Running tests/test_blocks_retrieval.py::test_hydrating_the_hits_stops_at_its_bound (or three other tests) before the golden scenario m1-recall-cue-sure-rrf-trace makes the scenario record `block_source.reason = logging_off` where the golden holds `no_file`. In the other direction, tests/test_blocks_retrieval.py::test_changing_the_count_alone_leaves_the_examined_set_unchanged failed alone and passed in its module only because an earlier test had left a stale file: its spy watches the SQLite read, which the block arm takes only when the file cannot answer. The alphabetical full-suite order hid both; a run narrowed to the tests that execute a set of changed lines exposed the first.
issues.fix_sketch: Clear what a test leaves beside the shared database path after every test, and make the test that relied on a leftover file pin the read path it watches.
issues.fix_note: An autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py removes every file a test created beside `config.DB_PATH` (names starting with the database's file name and a dot, so the database and its -wal/-shm are untouched; files present before the test stay). Removed rather than reported, like the path restore beside it: building those files is what the tests exercise. The count-invariant test now turns the block index file off, since its spy watches the SQLite read; tests/test_block_index.py::test_search_reads_the_file_and_answers_as_sqlite_does already pins that the file answers as SQLite does. With the fixture in place the full suite passes, and no other test changed verdict. Pinned by tests/test_audit_2611_followups.py, which runs the leaking test before the golden scenario, and the count-invariant test alone, each in a fresh process: making the fixture non-autouse, making it remove nothing, or dropping the pin each turns one of them red.

issues.summary: (LOW) From mcp 1.29.0 the streamable-HTTP session manager refuses any request body over 4 MiB with a plain-text 413 before the transport reads it, and the HTTP transport did not set that limit, so the SDK's fixed 4 MiB overruled CPERSONA_HTTP_MAX_BODY_BYTES and CPERSONA_HTTP_BODY_LIMIT_MODE. Under the default `warn`, which docs/configuration.md documents as serving the request in full, a 5 MiB tools/call was answered 413: with a Content-Length the SDK refused before a byte was read, so the budget counted nothing; without one the budget counted the body and logged "The body was served in full" before the SDK refused it. A budget raised above 4 MiB changed nothing, and in `reject` mode with such a budget the refusal was the SDK's text rather than this server's JSON naming the budget. uv.lock pinned mcp 1.28.1, so the suite never ran against the limit, and the body budget tests drive a stand-in endpoint rather than the SDK. A fresh resolve since 2026-07-28 takes mcp 1.29 or later, since the dependency was mcp>=1.26.0,<2. Legitimate traffic is far below 4 MiB (the largest single store is 144 KB), which is why this is LOW.
issues.fix_sketch: Build the session manager in one function that production and the transport tests share, and pass the SDK a body limit it cannot reach, so the configurable budget is the only limit. Raise the mcp floor to the release that accepts the argument.
issues.fix_note: server._http_session_manager() builds the stateless session manager with max_request_body_size set to sys.maxsize, and _run_http_server and tests/transport_harness.py both call it. The mcp floor is now 1.30.0: the argument first exists in 1.29.0, and pip keeps an installed mcp that satisfies the floor, so an upgrade over an older SDK would fail at HTTP startup; 1.30.0 is the release uv.lock tests. Pinned by three tests in tests/test_http_body_budget.py that drive the real transport: warn mode serves a 5 MiB body with and without a Content-Length and logs one crossing, a 6 MiB budget in reject mode serves 5 MiB and answers a 7 MiB body with its own JSON 413, and _run_http_server takes its manager from the factory. Removing the argument, setting it to the budget, building the manager inline in _run_http_server, or making the manager stateful each turns at least one of them red. The floor is pinned by test_runtime_dependency_floors_exclude_known_vulnerable_releases in tests/test_structural_gates.py, which lists mcp 1.29.1 as the last release the floor may not admit: lowering the floor to 1.26.0 or 1.29.0 turns it red.
